title: Secret Crush Loses Memory and Becomes My Boyfriend
author: Zi Xiaoqi
synopsis:
Sang Luoluo harbors a secret: she has long had a crush on the boy from the neighboring high school, the one who was the center of everyone’s attention.
Later, they frequently crossed paths.
Coincidentally, their mothers turned out to be close friends.
She nervously called him, "Gege."
---
Jing Ye, the top-tier heartthrob coveted by countless in the circle, was reckless and untamed, his head always held high.
Until an excessively beautiful and well-behaved little girl repeatedly caught his eye.
Not only did he bend down, but he also lowered his head.
---
Highlight Scene:
Until the rooftop secret photos were exposed, shocking the entire internet.
The once-arrogant Jing family prince trapped the girl, nuzzling her nose, silently pleading.
Lip-readers worked overnight to decode: *"Baby, kiss me again, okay?"*
---
After getting together, she discovered he had lost a segment of his high school memories.
In that forgotten time, he had once deeply loved someone.
One day, the Jing family told her the truth about his memory loss and near-death experience.
Terrified, she proposed a breakup.
His trembling, broken voice message arrived:
"You said... if I cry and beg, you’ll soften your heart."
"Look... I’m crying now... I’m begging you."
"Begging you... don’t throw me away like trash."
---
Later, in a dim room.
For three days and three nights, he pinched her waist in punishment:
"Waist... can be a little softer."

chapters.title: If You Like Me, Do It Like This?
chapters.content:
Liking him was like clutching a handful of stardust—if she loosened her grip, the light would spill across the entire summer.

Drip. Drip.

Water droplets fell from the overflowing edge of the bathtub.

Inside, a man lay reclined, the warm water gently cradling him, accentuating the exposed section of his collarbone—cold and alluring.

His pristine white shirt, soaked through, clung tightly to his skin, turning semi-transparent with a damp, forbidden allure.

Even with his face obscured by a black silk blindfold, revealing only his perfect jawline and tightly pressed thin lips, it did nothing to conceal the bone-deep handsomeness.

Splash.

A soft sound shattered the stillness.

A fair, slender foot stepped in, brushing against his submerged waist. The muscles there tensed instantly.

Then, another foot followed, causing the water to ripple more visibly.

She sat down, her damp fingertips landing on the hem of his soaked shirt.

Then, slowly, they traced upward along the narrow, sensitive gap between the shirt and his waist.

Wherever her fingers passed, his body tensed abruptly, his Adam’s apple rolling uncontrollably up and down in a shockingly sensual arc.

The blindfolded face turned toward her, his jaw clenched tight.

He wanted to move, to resist.

But his long, well-defined fingers were firmly bound behind his back with a tie. Every struggle only produced futile splashes, adding to the desperate allure.

Suddenly, her fingers changed direction, sliding downward.

"I like you."

"Like me, and this is how you show it?"

"Too scared to do it openly, so I have to play dirty."

His Adam’s apple bobbed heavily, as if choked by her words. Just as he was about to speak—

Her lips pressed down on his.

His lips were surprisingly soft. She awkwardly mimicked the blurred scenes she’d seen before.

When the kiss broke, their breaths mingled.

"Sorry."

With that, she pulled off his belt, letting it drop onto the wet tiles beside the tub.

"You—!"

His next words were swallowed by her lips again, leaving only suppressed groans and the continuous sound of splashing water.

"I am Jing Ye."

"I am from......"

Sang Luoluo jolted awake, her heart pounding as if it would burst from her chest.

On instinct, she leaned over the bunk bed and asked Meng Lin, who was sitting at the desk below, "What are you watching?"

Meng Lin had just turned down the video volume. Hearing the question, she looked up. "Sorry, Luoluo, did I wake you?"

"It’s fine, I should be up anyway. We have class this afternoon." Sang Luoluo steadied herself, her voice still thick with sleep. "Just now, I thought I heard someone introducing themselves... Jing Ye?"

"Yeah!" Meng Lin perked up, holding out her phone screen. "It’s a video of Senior Jing Ye’s speech at that top-tier university finance forum in the UK. The school’s official account just posted it. The whole thing’s in English—so ridiculously cool!"

On the screen, the young Eastern man stood tall at the podium, his suit impeccable. Under the spotlight, he seemed more mature, yet just as devastatingly handsome.

Behind him, a massive screen displayed complex financial models.

Sang Luoluo handed the phone back.

Meng Lin took it, excited. "The video’s gone viral. The comments are all saying he’s more like a professional elite than a student. Our school’s official account even featured it, and the dean personally reposted and liked it!"

Tan Shuyin, leaning against the headboard with a face mask on, chuckled. "Now the girls at Jing University are probably going to lose sleep for another month."

Su Nan, on the next bed, put down her phone and stretched, smug. "Luckily, I already have someone. A guy like that—so out of reach—you can look, but dreaming about him is pointless."

Sang Luoluo didn’t listen to the rest. Her mind was flooded with the dream and the dazzling figure on the screen.

She put on her headphones and opened the video on her own phone.

His voice came through the earphones, magnetic and textured like the deepest notes of a cello, or the teasing breath against an earlobe—it sent a tingling sensation straight to her heart.

He spoke fluently about financial models and market variables she couldn’t understand.

He had an extraordinarily noble face.

His bone structure was sharp and three-dimensional, the brow ridge and nose bridge forming a steep, striking landscape. His jawline was clean and precise, tapering to a slightly prominent Adam’s apple.

His skin was a cool, pale white, the kind cultivated by a lifetime of luxury.

Yet, he had a pair of flirtatious peach-blossom eyes.

Even through the screen, even in a formal suit, those eyes still held an untamed wildness.

Two years.

A full two years since she’d last seen him.

He was still unrestrained, dazzling—like a scorching summer wind, crashing into her world once more, stirring up a storm.

Her gaze drifted to his lips again.

Those very lips, in her dream...

Her fingers curled slightly, as if still lingering with the tense heat beneath his skin.

Sang Luoluo’s heart trembled, her ears burning.

How could she have such a dream—and tie him up, no less.

—Oh God, I’m not just a pervert, I’m a lustful woman.

The comments were flooding in. She focused on one:

[Damn, look at that dog’s waist—who could resist that? I’d sleep with him in a heartbeat.]

[I bet he could pick someone up and pin them against a wall for three hours straight without breaking a sweat.]

Sang Luoluo’s cheeks flushed again.

In her dream, his stamina had been *impressive*.

Even though she’d initiated it, he quickly took control.

She had no idea how he’d managed to free his wrists from that cursed tie, but the moment his hands were free, he seized all dominance.

The bedding was terrible.

No matter how tearfully she begged, he showed no mercy.

[Trust me, after sleeping with someone like him, ordinary guys will taste like water. Like drinking Moutai then switching to beer—bland, and all you’ll want to do is flip the table.]

[Alright, stop. I heard he suddenly went to the UK last year for an exchange program. Rumor has it it was for his girlfriend?]

[Yeah, I also heard his girlfriend studies dance. Her figure is amazing.]

Sang Luoluo bit her lip, the color draining from them.

On stage, Jing Ye’s speech was nearing its end.

He returned the microphone, and as the applause and chasing cameras grew more frenzied, he turned and strode off the stage with effortless grace.

Meng Lin put down her phone and said to herself, "I wonder what his girlfriend abroad looks like? I’m so curious—what kind of celestial beauty could capture someone like Jing Ye?"

The words *"celestial beauty"* stabbed Sang Luoluo like a fine needle—not deep, but sharp enough to hurt.

A man like him: top-tier looks, prestigious family, outstanding talent.

What must the girl by his side look like?

Probably so breathtakingly perfect it was impossible to even imagine.

1. Mutual secret crush, mutual pursuit.2. Dual purity—both leads’ first love, first kiss, first time are with each other.3. The male lead is currently suffering from memory loss. Even so, the only one who can make him fall again is the female lead.4. Short and sweet, clean pacing, no dragging.5. Remember to bookmark to avoid losing your place!6. Hope you readers don’t forget to leave ratings and reviews—give me, your little author, some sweet spiritual nourishment~ Love you all~~

chapters.title: The Year I First Saw Him
chapters.content:
Foreign Language Institute.

Sang Luoluo gathered her books while saying to her roommates, "You all go back first. I have an elective class to attend."

"Okay, I’ll take your bag back for you." Meng Lin slung her own backpack over her shoulder and picked up Sang Luoluo’s as well.

"Thanks!" Sang Luoluo hoisted her drawing board and walked downstairs with them. Meng Lin, arm in arm with Tan Shuyin and Su Nan, headed back to the dorm.

When she reached the art classroom, the familiar scent of turpentine and paint filled the air.

Inside, there were already two or three dozen students from different departments, standing or sitting in small groups, chatting softly.

Sang Luoluo found a spot by the window and set up her drawing board.

The instructor entered shortly after, exuding a casual air.

The room quieted down.

"Good afternoon, I’m Lin Ce, your teacher." Lin Ce stood at the front, his voice gentle. "For the first lesson, we won’t talk theory. We’ll do one thing only—*see*."

He walked to the window and, with a swift motion, pulled the already open curtains wider, letting the light pour in unobstructed.

"See what?" a student asked quietly.

"See the light." Lin Ce replied. "See where it lands, where it disappears, see how light and shadow outline the shapes of things..."

Sang Luoluo paused.

*Light...*

Her pen scratched across the paper, almost as if possessed, sketching the vague yet striking silhouette of a boy.

—When she was seventeen, she met him. From that moment, he became the only star in her world, suspended above her head, never falling.

---

The path back to the dorm passed through a wide Ginkgo Avenue.

She was walking with her head down when she suddenly heard hurried footsteps and excited voices ahead.

"Hurry! He’s really back! At the East Gate!"

"Who? The guy who disappeared for a year?"

"Yeah! The forums are exploding! They say he just got back from the UK. His whole vibe has changed—even more impossible to look away from."

A group of girls, like a gust of excited wind, rushed past her.

As they brushed by, fragments of their conversation reached her ears.

"That energy... so wild, yet his aura is so noble. Two extremes, perfectly fused in him..."

"Just one glance, and it makes your legs go weak..."

Sang Luoluo froze in place.

*He’s back?*

Her feet, as if no longer under her control, followed the direction the girls had run.

Her heart had been beating erratically since she heard that name.

The East Gate was usually quiet, but now it was unusually crowded.

People stood on tiptoes, craning their necks toward the gate, their faces alight with excitement and anticipation.

Sang Luoluo’s gaze locked onto the figure outside the gate, unable to look away.

A black Bentley Mulsanne was parked there, quiet yet eye-catching.

Beside the car stood a figure so striking that even in the simplest white shirt and black trousers, he was as conspicuous as a beam of light cutting through the ordinary.

It was Jing Ye.

It really was him.

No longer just an image on a screen, no longer just a legend passed around in others’ words.

He was here, in the flesh—warm, casting a shadow, breathing the same noisy air as her.

He was slightly turned, deep in conversation with a well-known professor from the Finance School.

As they finished talking, the professor glanced around. "Look at that—after a year away, everyone’s still this excited to see you."

Jing Ye didn’t look at the crowd. "Professor, don’t tease me."

The professor patted his shoulder. "You must be tired from the flight. Go rest. Come to class tomorrow."

Jing Ye gave a slight nod and opened the car door.

The black Bentley drove away silently.

The onlookers let out lingering sighs, dispersing in twos and threes, still buzzing about the fleeting glimpse of perfection.

Sang Luoluo walked slowly forward along the tree-lined path, her steps unsteady, her mind filled with the white-clad figure.

Beside her, a boy in a white shirt hurried past.

Unconsciously, she compared: *This guy’s white shirt... it just doesn’t have the same effect. Nowhere near as good as Jing Ye’s.*

The same white, on Jing Ye, wasn’t a warm, soft white—it was a cold, crisp white, like frost on a winter morning. Clean, sharp, catching the light, yet devoid of warmth.

It reminded her of the first time she truly saw him.

Back then, she was in her second year of high school, and he was in his third—the legendary figure of Jing City No. 1 High.

A name that carried an edge, a man of the hour, the white moonlight in countless girls’ hearts, the target countless boys sought to surpass.

That summer, the two high schools held a friendly basketball match at her school, No. 2 High.

The basketball court was packed, the noise deafening. The cheers were so loud they nearly lifted the roof off. Half the girls were there for one name: *Jing Ye*.

He took the court as the only one not wearing the team uniform.

White T-shirt, black pants—he stood out among the brightly colored players.

He played well, but what people remembered most was *how* he played.

When an opponent used a hidden push—a foul the referee didn’t call—he steadied himself, didn’t argue, his expression unreadable.

In the next play, he returned the favor with the exact same move, gliding past the opponent again.

The ball swished through the net. He turned his head slightly toward the referee, a faint, indifferent smile tugging at his lips. "Does this... count as a foul?"

Later, he was triple-teamed, his space completely locked down.

Jeers and mocking laughter rose from the sidelines.

He remained calm, gesturing with a careless wave to the players surrounding him.

Then, at the peak of the booing, he took a step back, leaned, and jumped.

The ball arced high, swishing cleanly through the net. The sound was so crisp it silenced the entire court.

He landed steadily, ignoring the stunned opponents and the sudden eruption of cheers from the crowd.

Lifting his cold, pale eyelids, he slowly raised a finger to his lips, pressing it lightly—a silent, yet more oppressive than any shout, *"shush"* gesture.

He was elegant, yet thorny.

In the most rule-abiding way, he displayed the most arrogant attitude, leaving you humiliated with no words, yet powerless to do anything.

There was an indescribable reckless roguishness in him, as if it were in his bones—dangerous, yet alluring.

When the game ended, he casually flicked his sweat-dampened hair, and amid the crowd’s adoration and attention, he turned and left the court.

Sang Luoluo stopped walking, standing in the dappled shade of the trees, tilting her face slightly upward.

The evening light was a bit glaring, filtering through the gaps in the leaves, casting fragmented patterns on her face.

In this dazzling glow, the silhouette of the boy from her memories and the man before her now silently overlapped.

Two shades of white—both clean, both distant, both utterly beyond her reach.

She lowered her head, blinking her eyes, letting the afterimage left by the harsh light slowly fade from her retinas.

chapters.title: She Picked Up His Lighter
chapters.content:
"Luoluo!" Meng Lin panted as she ran up to her, propping herself on her knees to catch her breath. "Jing Ye... has he already left?"

Sang Luoluo pulled her slightly unfocused gaze back. "He just left. You're a step too late."

"I ran over as soon as I heard the news," Meng Lin said, catching her breath and tucking her disheveled hair behind her ear. "I've never sprinted this hard, not even for the 800-meter physical test, and I still missed him."

She regulated her breathing, then suddenly narrowed her eyes, looking at Sang Luoluo thoughtfully. "Wait, why are you here? Did you come to see Jing Ye too? That doesn't make sense. Aren't you the type who keeps men at arm's length and only has a romance with books?"

Sang Luoluo walked on with a composed expression. "I just came to the east gate to buy something. I happened to run into him, that's all."

Meng Lin quickened her pace to keep up, clearly skeptical. "What a coincidence? Don't you usually go to the small shop at the south gate? Since when did you start going to the east gate?"

Sang Luoluo didn't stop walking, only glancing at her sideways. "The south gate ran out of orange soda."

Meng Lin's gaze followed to her hand, which was empty.

"Where's the soda you bought?"

"I drank it."

An unassailable reason.

Meng Lin let out an "Oh," though she still found it strange. She didn't press further, linking arms with Sang Luoluo as they headed back to the dormitory.

"I thought you had finally come to your senses!"

"What a shame. He went abroad as an exchange student right after we enrolled last year. We never even got to see him once, and now that he's finally back, we missed him again."

---

The next day at noon, after class.

The four of them followed the crowd out of the teaching building.

Meng Lin saw the students around them start to jog and spoke urgently, as if she were stepping on fire: "Hurry, hurry, hurry! Keep up! The cafeteria has pineapple sweet and sour pork and crab meat lion's head today. If we're late, we won't even get a drop of the sauce!"

Su Nan looked surprised. "What? Lion's head? Isn't that only on Fridays?"

"That's why we have to rush today!" Tan Shuyin had already started jogging, turning back to add, "I heard the head chef added these special dishes because Jing Ye brought great honor to the school, so he's in a good mood."

Before Sang Luoluo could react, Meng Lin grabbed her wrist and pulled her into the surging crowd heading toward the cafeteria.

It wasn't until they rushed to the cafeteria entrance that they truly realized what "unprecedented spectacle" meant.

Every line twisted and coiled like a greedy snake, with the tail already blurred among the shifting heads, leaving almost no room to step.

At the serving window, the auntie's hands moved so fast they seemed to blur, the stainless steel spoon clinking against the metal tray.

Even so, the line moved at a snail's pace.

Meng Lin stood on her tiptoes, peering inside the cafeteria. After straining to look around, she was stunned. "At this rate, someone might think they're giving out free money. No matter how good these two dishes are, they shouldn't attract two-thirds of the entire school, right?"

Tan Shuyin sighed, her gaze sweeping over the excited and eager crowd, her tone understanding. "Perhaps it's not all about the food."

Sang Luoluo, looking at the dense crowd before her, had already guessed the reason in her heart.

From the nearby line, a few excited discussions floated over without restraint:

"Hurry, hurry! Maybe we'll run into him! He just returned to school; he must eat, right?"

"I heard from a senior that he rarely appeared in the cafeteria before. With so many people today, we might be out of luck."

Someone else chimed in, "Forget it. Someone just saw him being called away by a professor."

Meng Lin pouted, standing on her tiptoes again to look at the line that hadn't moved much. She slumped her shoulders and wailed, "How long will we have to wait?"

Tan Shuyin, on the other hand, was calm. "We're here, so we might as well wait."

"Alright, when in Rome..." Meng Lin resignedly sighed, reluctantly shuffling forward a couple of steps.

Sang Luoluo followed behind her, her mind wandering far away.

By the time they finally reached the window, the pineapple sweet and sour pork and crab meat lion's head were long gone, even the trays had been taken away.

Meng Lin looked at the few bland, ordinary dishes left in the window and wailed on the spot. "These people are too much! I waited so long for nothing, not even a drop of sauce."

She clung to the window, stubbornly peering inside, her voice pitiful. "Auntie, is there really nothing left? Even a spoonful, just one spoonful!"

The cafeteria auntie didn't even look up, tapping the edge of the tray with her spoon. "Gone long ago! Hurry up and order!"

The four of them exchanged glances, then randomly ordered some of the remaining dishes. Carrying their trays, they circled the crowded cafeteria twice before finally snagging a table that had just been vacated.

Meng Lin plopped down, grabbed her chopsticks, and poked at the greens in her bowl, her voice listless. "I hope tomorrow isn't this crazy. Who can stand this every day?"

Amid the noisy chatter around them, the name "Jing Ye" and fragments of conversations about him occasionally drifted into Sang Luoluo's ears.

She kept her eyes downcast, eating slowly and quietly, one bite at a time.

After the meal, the four of them left the cafeteria.

The midday heat wave hit them in the face, and even the wind under the shade of the trees was lukewarm.

Meng Lin fanned herself with her hand and suggested, "It's so hot. Let's go straight to the library. The air conditioning there is strong, much cooler than the dormitory. We can also look for some materials while we're at it."

Sang Luoluo stopped in her tracks. "You all go. I need to go to the bookstore outside the school to buy a notebook."

"Now?" Tan Shuyin looked up at the sky, frowning slightly. "The sun is at its worst. What notebook is so urgent that you have to go out in the middle of the day?"

Sang Luoluo curved her lips slightly. "I need it for this afternoon. You all go to the library. Don't worry about me."

Seeing that she had made up her mind, the other three didn't try to persuade her further.

Sang Luoluo left the school gate and entered the familiar stationery store. She casually picked up a notebook, paid for it, and quickly left.

As she stepped out of the store, the heat wave hit her face again.

Instead of heading straight back to school, she walked slowly along the shade of the trees by the road, taking her time.

The cicadas buzzed loudly, and the sunlight was dazzling.

She needed some time alone, a moment to place those inescapable worries.

As she walked, she seemed to step on something. The slight hardness pressed against the sole of her shoe, pulling her wandering thoughts back.

She looked down and saw a silver lighter lying quietly in the gap between the tiles.

The body of the lighter had cold, sharp lines, and it looked expensive, not the kind of cheap item ordinary students would use.

She bent down to pick it up, rubbing off the dust with her fingertip.

This area was right next to the school, and most of the people passing by were students. It was probably dropped by some careless person.

She started walking toward the school, planning to hand it in to the lost and found at the security office.

"Classmate."

A lazy, roguish voice, with a hint of casual hoarseness, suddenly sounded very close to her side, without any warning.

Sang Luoluo turned her head to look.

Then, her breath stopped for a moment, and her heartbeat even skipped half a beat.

Jing Ye was standing just two steps away.

He was wearing a loose black short-sleeved T-shirt and pants of the same color.

A silver cross necklace hung lazily on his chest, and his hands were in his pockets.

He probably had just come out from some shaded place, as the ends of his hair were slightly messy.

Behind him, a group of people—the student council president and several department heads—stopped behind him, all looking at her.

Jing Ye looked at her, or rather, at the lighter in her hand.

"That lighter is mine."

Sang Luoluo lowered her long eyelashes, hiding the turmoil in her eyes. Her slender, fair fingers held the lighter, extending it forward, her fingertips trembling slightly.

"Here."

He reached out to take it.

His knuckles were long, his lines sharp like bamboo, and under his cool, pale skin, faint blue veins were vaguely visible.

The cold metal briefly exchanged between their fingertips.

His fingertip inadvertently brushed against her finger pad.

In an instant—

chapters.title: Encountering Him Again
chapters.content:
Sang Luoluo jerked her hand back as if she had been electrocuted, her fingertips curling up tightly behind her back.

The skin that had been touched, though only briefly and coolly, felt as if it had been set on fire, burning fiercely.

That scorching sensation even spread rapidly from her fingertips, making her entire hand feel stiff, and her breathing became cautious.

She kept her eyes down, staring at the small patch of ground in front of her toes, not daring to look up, not daring to look at him, for fear of revealing the secret in her heart.

The lighter spun a circle in his fingers, making a soft clicking sound, crisp and pleasant.

"Thanks." With that, he walked past her.

A cool, refreshing mint scent lingered at her nose, then quickly dissipated into the warm afternoon air, leaving no trace.

Sang Luoluo stood still, not moving.

Perhaps a long time had passed—so long that she thought her feet had stuck to the ground—or perhaps it was just a few seconds, too short for her to even catch the subtle changes in him over the past two years.

She continued toward the school, taking a few steps, but still couldn't help looking back.

The tall, slender figure of the boy was walking away slowly along the long path lined with phoenix trees, becoming the most familiar outline in her memory.

She had seen this back too many times, so familiar it was almost instinctive, so familiar that every time she saw it, her heart would ache with a dense, tingling sensation.

---

A few days later, in the dormitory.

Meng Lin swiped through her phone screen, sighed, and turned the screen toward the others. "There's a live stream in the group chat. The cafeteria is packed again. If we go now, we'll probably only catch the leftover scraps, and they'll all be cold. Just looking at it makes me lose my appetite.

These days, the cafeteria has gone crazy. It's packed with people, all just to catch a glimpse of Jing Ye."

Tan Shuyin leaned in to look at the photo of the dense crowd, frowning slightly. She immediately made a decision: "Let's go out to eat!"

"Hot pot! Hot pot!" Meng Lin's eyes lit up like a light bulb, and she jumped up in an instant.

Sang Luoluo silently put away her phone and looked up. "Then we'd better hurry. If we're late, even the hot pot restaurant will have a wait."

"Let's go, let's go."

When they arrived at the restaurant, fortunately, there was still one table in the farthest corner that could barely seat four people.

The four of them sat around the table, and Meng Lin couldn't wait to push the menu to the center. She pointed at the spiciness options with her fingertip, raising her eyebrows at everyone with a mischievous smile. "Ladies, what level today? Regular medium spicy, sweat-inducing extra spicy, or go straight for the hellish lava?"

Tan Shuyin: "Let's do medium spicy. It's so stuffy today that even the air conditioning can't dispel the heat. Any spicier and we'll really catch fire."

In Jing City's September, the sun was still blindingly fierce, and even the wind was scorching, carrying a suffocating heat.

"Alright." Meng Lin waved her hand generously, marking medium spicy on the menu, then looked at everyone. "How about some ice-draft beer? It's refreshing and will help cool us down."

Su Nan nodded. "Sure."

"Luoluo, what about you?" Meng Lin looked to her side, only to find that Sang Luoluo wasn't listening at all. Her gaze was fixed straight ahead, lost in thought.

Following her line of sight, there sat four boys. The steam from the hot pot blurred their faces.

Wait.

She narrowed her eyes, staring intently at the innermost seat.

The mist was swept away by the airflow for a moment.

The figure in the white T-shirt, leaning lazily against the back of the chair, was turned to the side, casually chatting with the person next to him.

Meng Lin gasped, subconsciously grabbing Sang Luoluo's wrist, disbelief in her voice. "Is that... Jing Ye?"

Tan Shuyin and Su Nan heard her and, in unison, turned their heads.

It really was him.

In person, he was far more striking than in videos. His face was so handsome it was almost aggressive, and even just a profile was enough to captivate anyone.

The two exchanged a glance, reading the same thought in each other's eyes:

This was truly a case of trying to plant a flower but failing, while a willow planted carelessly thrives.

The person they had waited for endlessly in the cafeteria, without success, had suddenly appeared, without warning, in this steamy hot pot restaurant.

At the other table, Jing Ye seemed to sense something. His long fingers set down the wine glass.

He lazily lifted his eyelids, his dark eyes falling precisely on their table.

Almost simultaneously, the girls seemed scorched by that gaze and panicked, pretending to be busy.

One looked at the menu, another poured tea, and another adjusted her hair.

Only Sang Luoluo was half a beat slower. Her pupils contracted slightly as she met his gaze directly.

After a belated realization, she lowered her eyes, her long eyelashes trembling uneasily.

From across the table, Jing Ye's gaze settled on her downcast face, lingering for a barely noticeable two seconds.

"I was talking to you. What are you looking at?"

Chen Ge, sitting next to him, had ash-blond hair and a small black diamond earring on his tragus. He nudged Jing Ye with his elbow.

Jing Ye withdrew his gaze, his fingertips tracing the rim of the glass, indifferently replying, "Nothing."

Across from him, Lu Zhi'an took off his fogged-up glasses, wiping them with a tissue while teasing him. "You've barely touched your food. After being abroad for a year, can't you even handle hot pot anymore?"

"Not very hungry." Jing Ye lowered his eyes, pulling out his phone and absently swiping the screen.

Shen Juan picked up another piece of meat with his chopsticks. "Forget it. Let's just eat our own."

Soon, the food for the girls' table was fully served, and the spicy oil in the pot began to bubble.

Meng Lin, while sliding a whole plate of fatty beef into the pot, lowered her voice, her eyes still sneaking glances over there. "What do you think? Should I secretly take a photo? Just one, to show off on WeChat Moments!"

Tan Shuyin shot her a sideways glance, her tone cool. "You almost got caught by the man himself just now. Do you really think if you raise your phone again, he won't notice in the next second?"

"Yeah, forget it." Meng Lin immediately chickened out, abandoning the idea, and honestly started cooking the meat.

"Come on, let's have a toast." Tan Shuyin raised her glass of ice-draft beer, brimming with fine foam, toward the other three.

The four glasses lightly clinked in the air.

Sang Luoluo took a couple of sips, her gaze uncontrollably drifting toward the table across from them.

He looked very relaxed, his brows and eyes at ease. This was different from the dazzling, untouchable image in the videos.

She recognized the boy with ash-blond hair; he was a prominent figure in the junior year of the Finance School. So they were roommates.

Halfway through the meal, a familiar heavy sensation arose in her lower abdomen, coming in waves, making her face pale with pain.

Her period seemed to have come early. Fortunately, she had a spare sanitary pad in her bag.

She stuffed the sanitary pad into her pocket, speaking quickly. "I need to go to the restroom."

"Okay, come back soon. The fatty beef will be done soon!"

Sang Luoluo endured the discomfort and quickly walked toward the restroom, her steps growing faster.

Halfway there, she stopped abruptly, unable to hold back, and started to jog. As a result, she didn't watch where she was going and bumped solidly into a masculine chest coming out from inside.

"I'm sorry, I didn't mean to." She staggered back a couple of steps, the apology slipping out automatically.

"It's fine."

That voice...

Sang Luoluo stiffly, very slowly, lifted her gaze.

Jing Ye looked down at her, his gaze settling on her face.

chapters.title: He Steps In for Her
chapters.content:
A sudden, sharper cramp shot through her lower abdomen. Her face paled, and she could no longer care about anything else—she quickly slipped into the women’s restroom.

Jing Ye turned his head and caught a glimpse of the small section of a sanitary pad peeking out from her pocket. Then, lower down, a slightly darker stain had spread on the back of her light-wash jeans.

He immediately turned around and walked to the entrance of the hotpot restaurant. The street was lined with nothing but small eateries—there wasn’t a single clothing store.

Both he and his roommate were wearing short sleeves; they didn’t even have a jacket to cover her with.

He turned back again.

Cutting through the bustling dining hall filled with the aroma of food and chatter, he ignored the surprised stares and even the suppressed gasps: “It’s really Jing Ye.”

He passed table after table of diners and finally stopped beside a table of girls.

The girls there clearly recognized him, their faces filled with disbelief and excitement.

Jing Ye pointed at the pink women’s blouse draped over the back of a chair. “Classmate, can I buy this blouse from you?”

“Huh?”

The owner of the blouse, a girl with shoulder-length hair, first looked stunned. She glanced at her ordinary, basic pink blouse, then at the impossibly handsome face before her.

Her cheeks flushed instantly, and an absurd yet heart-racing thought popped into her head uncontrollably.

—Could he possibly have a secret crush on me?

“No need to buy it, I’ll just—just give it to you!” she blurted out, hastily taking the blouse from the chair and handing it over.

“Thank you,” Jing Ye took the blouse, and with his other hand, he already had his phone out. “Trouble you to show me your payment QR code.”

“Really, it’s fine, this blouse isn’t worth much, just take it.” The girl’s face turned even redder as she waved her hands repeatedly.

“I don’t like owing people.”

Seeing this, the girl had no choice but to suppress the faint disappointment and confusion in her heart and pulled up her payment code.

Jing Ye scanned it and confirmed the payment.

“Thank you.” He thanked her again, then without lingering, took the blouse—which clashed completely with his cool demeanor—and left.

It wasn’t until he was far away that the girl finally looked down at her phone screen.

“F-five thousand?” she gasped in disbelief, her eyes widening.

“How much?” Her companion beside her immediately leaned over, also taking a sharp breath.

The girl showed them the screen. The transfer record was clear: “I only bought this blouse for a few dozen yuan!”

The group of them stared at each other, completely stunned.

Jing Ye took the blouse to the cashier. “Excuse me, could you please take this blouse to the women’s restroom? There’s a girl inside who needs help.”

The cashier was a middle-aged auntie who instantly understood—some girl must be in an awkward situation with her period.

“I’ll go right now, don’t worry.” The auntie took the blouse and responded promptly.

Jing Ye paused for a moment, then added, “Tell her she doesn’t need to return it.”

“Got it.” The auntie nodded and turned to quickly walk toward the restroom.

Jing Ye then sidestepped and quietly instructed another young waiter waiting nearby: “Please also settle the bill for the table of girls by the window over there.”

He gestured in a direction—it was the table where the blouse’s owner had been sitting.

“Yes, sir.” The waiter respectfully agreed.

Inside the restroom, Sang Luoluo finished cleaning up. She looked down and saw the glaring dark stain on her light jeans, and her heart sank.

This was bad.

She had rushed in so quickly that her phone was still on the table outside.

Holding onto a sliver of hope, she called out to the adjacent stall: “Hello? Is anyone there? Could you help me?”

No one responded.

The jeans were light-colored, and the stain was too obvious.

She couldn’t just cover her butt and walk out like this, could she?

And if Jing Ye saw her again...

Just the thought of that scene made her feel as if all the blood in her body had rushed to her head, her cheeks burning with embarrassment.

All she could do was prick up her ears and wait for the next person to come in.

Before long, footsteps approached and stopped outside the door.

Sang Luoluo’s heart leapt with joy, and she was about to speak.

A gentle female voice spoke first: “Excuse me, is there a guest inside who needs help?”

Sang Luoluo, as if grabbing a lifeline, immediately replied, “Yes, it’s me! Thank you so much!”

A blouse was passed over the top of the stall door. The cashier said, “Someone asked me to give you this. You can use it to cover up for now. They said you don’t need to return it.”

Sang Luoluo quickly took it. “May I ask who—”

The cashier’s phone suddenly rang, and then came the sound of her hurriedly leaving.

In her hands was a woman’s blouse—probably some kind-hearted girl had noticed her predicament and asked the cashier to bring it over.

She quickly tied the open-front blouse around her waist. The wide hem perfectly covered everything.

After fixing herself up, she pushed the door and walked out.

At the cashier, she softly asked, “Hello, may I ask who lent me the blouse? I’d like to thank them in person.”

The auntie smiled. “Little girl, that person has already left. They specifically said you don’t need to return it.”

“Oh... okay, thank you.” Sang Luoluo nodded, her gaze instinctively scanning the surroundings.

Just a moment ago, there had been several tables of girls still dining, but now they were all gone without a trace.

It seemed this blouse wouldn’t be returned after all.

When she returned to her table, she found it already empty.

“Luoluo, where’d you get that blouse?” Meng Lin curiously examined the pink blouse now tied around her waist.

“I don’t know which kind girl lent it to me.” Sang Luoluo didn’t dare sit down, afraid of dirtying the borrowed blouse.

“Did you get your period?” Tan Shuyin saw through her embarrassment at a glance.

“Mhm.”

“Luoluo, are you still eating?” Su Nan asked.

“No, you guys eat. I’ll go back first to clean up.” Sang Luoluo picked up her phone and bag.

“Wait, we’re almost done too. Let’s go together.” Meng Lin, seeing this, immediately started packing up.

After paying the bill, the four of them left the restaurant together.

Back at the dorm, Sang Luoluo took a shower first. After washing, she scrubbed her dirty clothes clean and hung them up to dry.

She flicked her blow-dried hair, the long ends softly cascading down her back.

She sat down and drank half a glass of warm water, her hand naturally resting on her lower abdomen.

It didn’t hurt much, just a slight heaviness. Compared to those who suffered excruciating pain and had to take medicine to get through it, she considered herself very lucky.

Most importantly, her period only lasted three days—it was incredibly comfortable.

On the way back, she had already heard many excited discussions. Fragments of conversation drifted into her ears, all revolving around one name, lingering inescapably.

She logged into the school forum, and sure enough, the homepage was completely flooded with the same name.

She clicked on the most popular post—a candid shot taken in class.

He leaned casually against the podium, with a dark green blackboard behind him.

His left hand rested lazily on the podium, his right hand loosely tucked into his pocket.

His posture was relaxed but not slouched, his shoulders and back forming an effortlessly graceful curve.

He tilted his head, seemingly listening to a student’s question, his expression focused with a rare hint of patience.

The replies below had already exceeded a thousand, with dozens of new ones popping up every time she refreshed.

...

“Luoluo, what are you looking at so intently?” Meng Lin tilted her head and caught a glimpse of her screen. “Oh! You’ve also seen the posts about Jing Ye. Isn’t he devastatingly handsome?”

Sang Luoluo quickly swiped up with her thumb, exiting the post. “Just browsing.”

Tan Shuyin chimed in: “You know, these days, girls really go for the ‘high-risk’ type. The more unconventional, wild, and untamed they seem, the more girls want to take on the challenge.”

Meng Lin nodded in strong agreement. “So true! It’s like knowing he’s a flammable material straight out of the fire safety manual, but you still want to go up and strike a match just to see what happens. It’s all about that rebellious, heart-pounding thrill.”

chapters.title: My Heart Recognized Him Before I Did
chapters.content:
Tan Shuyin smiled and shifted her gaze to Sang Luoluo, who had been quietly sitting to the side.

“But speaking of which, someone like our Luoluo—so gentle and soft like a little moon—probably wouldn’t go for a thorny sun like that. Too dazzling, afraid of getting burned, right?”

Caught off guard by the sudden question, Sang Luoluo’s delicate fingertips curled slightly.

Meng Lin placed her hand on her shoulder with a laugh. “Exactly! Our Luoluo should pair up with someone equally gentle and soft, like moonlight. Unlike someone like Jing Ye—just looking at him feels like your eyes are getting scorched.”

Sang Luoluo didn’t explain. She simply nodded along with their words, a faint dimple appearing at the corner of her lips before quietly disappearing again.

In everyone else’s eyes, he might be a blazing sun.

But only she knew.

He had always been a star.

The brightest, gentlest star hanging in her silent night sky, quietly illuminating her entire youth without ever hurting her eyes.

In everyone’s assumptions, she was supposed to like clean-cut, well-behaved guys.

Good family background, mild temperament, promising future.

Even her mother, whenever she brought it up, seemed to expect the same.

In truth, before meeting Jing Ye, she had thought the same way.

It was only after meeting him that Sang Luoluo realized for the first time that her heartbeat could betray her mind—falling for someone was completely beyond her control.

“Luoluo, what about that top student from the Business Management department, Xiao Xuechang? He’s always so scholarly, and we think you two would be a great match. Why haven’t you considered him?” Tan Shuyin pressed on.

“I don’t like him.” Sang Luoluo replied.

Meng Lin clicked her tongue and shook her head with a laugh. “Your standards are pretty high too. If we didn’t know your ‘I already have someone I like’ line is just an excuse to fend off suitors, we’d really think you’ve secretly got someone in your heart.”

She looked Sang Luoluo up and down, her gaze growing more appreciative the longer she looked.

Her face, still flushed from the hot shower, glowed with a delicate pink. Her small, palm-sized face was dewy, like a ripe peach, making one want to pinch her cheeks.

Her eyes were watery, her lashes still damp with traces of water, and whenever she looked at someone, it was as if they were veiled in a soft mist, incredibly alluring.

Her figure was well-proportioned—slim waist, long legs. She looked slender, but in all the right places, she was amply curved. A perfect example of “clothes make her look slim, but without them, she’s all the right kind of soft.”

Meng Lin propped up her cheek and persisted. “Luoluo, seriously, what kind of guys do you like? You must have some criteria, right?”

Sang Luoluo was just running her fingers through her long hair. At the question, her movements paused slightly, and Jing Ye’s face automatically appeared in her mind.

“I don’t have a fixed type. As long as he makes my heart race.”

Meng Lin was clearly unsatisfied with this vague answer and pressed further with a smile. “Then what counts as making your heart race? There must be a more concrete feeling, right? Like, is it good looks? Height? Or gentleness?”

Sang Luoluo blinked, her eyes still appearing dewy under the light. “My heart recognizes him before I do.”

Su Nan, who had been on the upper bunk chatting with her long-distance boyfriend, poked her head out halfway. Hearing this, she couldn’t help but interject. “Like love at first sight, a spark that lasts forever?”

“Yes, exactly.” Sang Luoluo nodded.

“So, you and your boyfriend were love at first sight?” Tan Shuyin turned the question to Su Nan.

Su Nan leaned on the edge of the bed, waving her phone. The screen displayed a cozy photo with her boyfriend. “Not at all. We’ve known each other since we were kids—purely a case of love growing over time. Slow and steady, which is nice too.”

Tan Shuyin glanced at Su Nan’s sweet profile, then at Sang Luoluo, who was quietly lowering her gaze, lost in thought. She let out a small laugh.

“In the end, it’s all about fate. If it’s meant to be, you’ll meet across a thousand miles. If not, you’ll pass each other without recognition even face to face.”

Su Nan withdrew back onto her bed, her fingers flying across the screen. “Exactly! When fate arrives, your heart recognizes the person. Without fate, no amount of heart-pounding can change that.”

She finished typing, then poked her head out again, her tone lively as she called out to Sang Luoluo. “So, Luoluo, just wait for your heart to go *thump* and recognize someone! And when it happens, don’t forget to tell us so we can share in the excitement!”

Sang Luoluo lifted her smile. “Okay.”

She answered lightly, but a bittersweet ripple stirred in her heart.

Su Nan, seeing the other two weren’t moving, asked, “Aren’t you two going to wash up? Then I’ll go.”

Meng Lin waved her hand. “You go first.”

Sang Luoluo took her phone and climbed up the ladder to her bunk.

The dorm fell into silence, save for the occasional sound of typing and pages turning.

This kind of quiet was a comfort born of familiarity—no need for words to fill the space.

Their relationship was good. From the polite distance at the start of freshman year, they had gradually grown into the kind of close friends who shared everything.

Compared to the dorm next door, which had small arguments every three days and big blowups every five, their dorm was practically a peaceful, warm harbor.

The glow of the screen illuminated her face as she saved the photo.

Ever since he returned, his name and figure had effortlessly overflowed the banks of her thoughts.

During university, whenever the name “Jing Ye” drifted into her ears—no matter how far away or how noisy the surroundings—she would feel as if someone had pressed the mute button. Her breath would involuntarily pause for half a beat as she strained to catch any snippet of news about him in the cacophony.

Those rumors gradually pieced together a complete picture: He was the most noble branch of the Jing family, one of the top three clans in the capital. His family background was as deep and unfathomable as an icy abyss. His very existence was a towering, awe-inspiring pyramid.

The surname Jing—within the capital city, there was only one Jing family.

This surname was the city’s invisible crown, symbolizing a foundation and height that others could barely hope to reach.

And she? She was merely one of the countless figures, like dust, illuminated beneath that crown.

One soared in the heavens, bathed in light and breeze; the other lingered in the mortal world, dependent on others’ mercy.

The difference between them was as vast as that between clouds and mud.

She had seen it clearly from the very beginning.

So later, she learned to tell herself this:

Stars could be admired, gazed upon from afar.

But she must never entertain the delusion of plucking one down and claiming it as her own.

---

Tuesday, on campus.

Meng Lin flipped through her phone and suggested, “A new movie just came out with great reviews. Want to go watch it together?”

Sang Luoluo shook her head. “You guys go. I need to stop by the internet café.”

Meng Lin looked up with her big, round eyes, understanding immediately. “The manager’s taking another leave?”

“Mhm, she has something this afternoon.” Sang Luoluo waved at them. “See you later.”

Her mother had insisted on opening the café for a simple reason: she was worried about the poor campus network and that Sang Luoluo would have nowhere to go during breaks. This way, she could bring her roommates over anytime.

The café had a manager to handle daily operations, and Sang Luoluo only came by occasionally when the manager was on leave or when she was bored.

She hopped onto her light pink bicycle, the wheels rolling over the dappled sunlight on the tree-lined path as she pedaled toward the backstreet.

The backstreet wasn’t far—just two turns away.

She parked her bike under the sign for “Starry Night Internet Café,” locked it, and pushed open the slightly heavy glass door.

It was afternoon, and the café was dimly lit.

At this hour, most students from Jing University were still in class, so the place was nearly empty.

To the right was the long cashier counter. Behind it, the shelves were neatly stocked with snacks, instant noodles, and cigarettes.

“Luoluo, you’re here.” The manager, He Fang, in her twenties, had been watching a drama behind the counter with headphones on. Seeing Sang Luoluo enter, she quickly removed her headphones and smiled. “I was just about to call you.”

“He Jie, I’m here to cover for you. You go take care of your business.” Sang Luoluo walked behind the counter and set down her bag.

“Thanks, then.” He Fang picked up her own bag and pointed to the freezer against the wall. “I just restocked the drinks. If they sell out, remember to refill. I’ll try to come back as soon as possible.”

“Okay, drive safely.”

After seeing He Fang off, Sang Luoluo sat down on the chair and stretched lazily. Her gaze habitually swept across the hall.

A few guys with headphones on were immersed in intense gaming, the clatter of keyboards and mice filling the air, occasionally punctuated by a few curses.

chapters.title: Do You Think I’m Taking You to a Hotel Room?
chapters.content:
She withdrew her gaze, took out *Advanced English* and a notebook from her canvas bag, and spread them on the clean counter, ready to organize her morning notes.

She wrote with intense focus, occasionally pausing to think, unconsciously tapping her lower lip with the end of the pen, her brows slightly furrowed, her expression serious yet adorable.

Her lips were naturally cherry-pink, with a subtle, glossy sheen when pursed.

A strand of dark hair slipped from behind her ear, softly brushing against her fair, delicate neck, adding an unknowing touch of elegance and allure.

Occasional customers came and went in the meantime.

She efficiently registered their IDs, collected payments, and softly said, "Welcome" or "Goodbye," before lowering her head again, retreating into her own world.

It was a little past six in the evening when He Fang returned.

"Luoluo, you’ve worked hard."

"It’s fine, Sister He," Sang Luoluo stood up from behind the cashier’s desk, rubbing her slightly sore shoulders. "You go eat first. I can leave after you finish."

"No need, no need. I ordered takeout; it’ll be here soon." He Fang put down her bag and waved her hand briskly. "You go eat. Don’t wait."

"Okay, then I’ll head out."

Sang Luoluo packed up her books, pushed open the glass door, and stepped outside.

The day’s heat had long since faded, and the summer night breeze carried the freshness of grass and trees, brushing against her exposed skin with a perfectly cool touch.

She walked to her light pink bicycle, flicked open the lock with her fingertips, and gracefully sat on the seat.

After putting on her headphones, she pressed play, and a familiar melody began to flow gently into her ears.

With her feet on the pedals, she rode toward the school at a leisurely pace, the wind in her face.

Halfway there, lost in the music, her peripheral vision suddenly caught a tall, straight figure cutting across her path.

Her heart tightened unexpectedly, her fingers stiffened instinctively, and the handlebars instantly lost balance.

The bike wobbled violently, nearly crashing into the thick sycamore tree by the roadside.

Her mind went blank, and in a reflexive, almost foolish move, she jumped right off the bike.

She stumbled several steps before barely steadying herself, a thin layer of sweat breaking out on her back.

The pink bicycle, now unsupported, crashed heavily to the ground.

The wheels continued spinning rapidly from inertia, the chain grinding with a harsh, ear-splitting *clatter-clatter*.

The music in her ears played on, but her heart pounded like a drum.

She clutched at her clothes in a fluster, embarrassedly lifting her head to look in the direction of the figure.

At that moment, she met Jing Ye’s gaze.

His naturally almond-shaped eyes were half-lidded, the outer corners slightly upturned, exuding a roguish charm that seemed to seep from his very bones, lazily lingering at the corners of his eyes.

The fading twilight cast a warm, ambiguous glow in his eyes, and the teasing look in them was so boldly wicked that Sang Luoluo’s heart stopped dead in that instant.

Jing Ye leisurely ended his call, his long fingers slipping the phone into the pocket of his black sweatpants.

He stood still, his gaze fixed on the flustered girl before him, lingering for several seconds.

She wore a mint-green dress, the hem neither too long nor too short, falling just above her calves. The earlier stumble had caused it to ride up slightly.

Her exposed ankles were slender and fair, like smooth jade, with a faint trace of dust—likely from when she had jumped off the bike.

From head to toe, he examined her inch by inch, meticulously.

Then, with a long stride, he walked over.

Sang Luoluo hastily lowered her head, yanking off her headphones, and fumbled to pick up the fallen bicycle.

A hand with distinct knuckles beat her to it, firmly gripping the handlebars and effortlessly righting the bike.

He even gave the pedal a casual press, and the chain moved smoothly, silently.

"It’s fine. You can still ride it." He spoke lazily.

Sang Luoluo’s eyes were fixed on the hand holding the handlebars.

The knuckles were well-defined, the skin cool and pale—a sight she had traced countless times in stolen glances.

It was really so beautiful.

A wayward thought struck her: *If only I could touch it.*

The moment the thought surfaced, she forcibly suppressed it.

"Thank you."

Her voice was so soft it was almost carried away by the wind, even she could barely hear it.

Jing Ye steadied the bike, but instead of leaving, he stood there, both hands casually tucked back into his pockets. He lowered his cool, pale eyelids, looking down at her from above.

The girl remained bent over, her gaze glued to the ground, her long lashes trembling.

"Am I that scary?"

There was a clear note of mockery in his tone, the end of his sentence hooked with a hint of a smile.

Sang Luoluo hadn’t expected him to speak to her first. She lifted her head in confusion.

Her clean almond-shaped eyes still held lingering panic, like a little deer that had stumbled into a hunter’s trap.

The moment their eyes met, she flinched as if scorched, quickly lowering her gaze again. Her voice was barely a whisper: "Not scary."

Jing Ye: "......"

Not scary?

Then why was she shaking like that?

She looked like she wished she could shrink into a crack in the ground.

She couldn’t even bring herself to look at him for more than a second.

He lightly pressed his tongue against the inside of his cheek, his gums itching.

For some reason, he felt the urge to bite something to pass the time.

"On your period?"

The sudden, out-of-nowhere question left Sang Luoluo stunned. She instinctively lifted her slightly dazed eyes, her voice carrying a confused nasal tone: "Huh?"

Jing Ye patiently repeated, "I’m asking, are you still on your period?"

Her ears burned with sudden heat.

Sang Luoluo suppressed the flicker of confusion in her heart and honestly shook her head. "No."

Jing Ye nodded, said nothing more, and continued walking forward, tossing out casually: "Leave the bike here. Let’s go."

Sang Luoluo didn’t move. Her gaze drifted toward the hotel at the street corner, its neon sign glowing with an ambiguous warmth.

The pink neon lights flickered in the twilight, dazzling the eyes.

This was a frequent haunt for student couples.

As soon as she looked over, she saw a couple walking in, arms around each other; then another pair, holding hands, emerged with smiles on their faces.

Business was so good it had even made her envious before—she had once thought about opening a place like this herself.

Unfortunately, her mother had firmly refused, afraid she’d be corrupted by the atmosphere.

She took a deep breath, mustering all her courage, and said to Jing Ye’s retreating back, with forced resolve, word by word: "I... am... not... going."

Jing Ye stopped walking and turned back.

Following her gaze, he glanced at the hotel.

He raised an eyebrow, then slowly walked back toward her.

In front of the girl glaring at him like a puffed-up kitten, he slowly bent down.

He smiled wickedly, the mockery in his eyes almost spilling over, like honeyed wine—sweet with a touch of poison.

"Do you think I’m taking you to a hotel room?"

His sudden proximity enveloped her in his cool, fresh breath, and her ears burned uncomfortably.

She didn’t speak, but her beautiful almond-shaped eyes had already betrayed her answer completely.

*—Just now, that’s exactly what I thought.*

---

chapters.title: My Skills... Unprecedented
chapters.content:
A faint blush spread across her cheeks, like the color of cherry blossoms drenched in spring sunlight—tender enough to pinch water from.

Jing Ye watched, the mischief in his eyes deepening.

His Adam’s apple rolled lightly, as if suppressing something.

"But if you *really* want to book a room, I might consider it..."

Sang Luoluo detected the teasing in his voice. Her cheeks puffed up like a little pufferfish, and she glared at him with all the ferocity of a kitten—her gaze held no threat, only a silly, adorable charm.

Jing Ye’s defiant brows and eyes softened into a smile, clearly amused by her reaction.

He composed himself, straightening his expression, and lifted his sharp jaw toward the other side of the street. His tone returned to its usual nonchalance: "You picked up my lighter. I’m buying you ice cream."

Sang Luoluo froze.

She had misunderstood.

A wave of embarrassment crashed over her, overwhelming her completely.

*—So he just wanted to buy me ice cream... and I actually thought...*

She quickly lowered her gaze, unable to face his smiling eyes any longer.

She wished she could find a crack in the ground and disappear forever.

"It’s fine." Her voice trembled slightly.

"Wait here."

Jing Ye dropped those two words, took a long stride, and walked straight toward the shop across the street, giving her no chance to refuse.

Sang Luoluo lifted her head, watching his tall, straight back, and in frustration, raised a hand to slap her own forehead.

She cursed herself under her breath, her voice carrying a whiny, almost tearful edge.

"Sang Luoluo, what *are* you thinking... how could you even go there..."

The more she thought about it, the more embarrassed she felt. She wished she could dig a hole and bury herself in it right then and there.

She turned around and pressed her burning forehead against the rough tree trunk.

Not too hard, not too soft—she bumped it twice, as if punishing herself for her wild imagination.

"*He must think I’m delusional, reading too much into things...*"

Before long, she heard footsteps returning.

She immediately straightened up, frantically smoothing her disheveled bangs to either side.

She tugged at her skirt, trying to make her expression look natural.

"Strawberry flavor."

Jing Ye was already in front of her, his long hand offering a pink-and-white swirl soft-serve cone.

The chill of the ice cream was palpable even through the air.

"Thank you." Sang Luoluo responded softly, reaching out to take it.

Just as her fingertips brushed the cold cone, Jing Ye’s other hand suddenly lifted, passing over her line of sight and reaching toward her head.

Sang Luoluo instinctively shrank her neck and looked up.

Between his well-defined fingers was a tiny green leaf, still fresh with a hint of dew.

Sang Luoluo: "......"

It must have been from just now, when she pressed her forehead against the tree trunk—she had accidentally picked it up.

*—In just a short moment, in front of my crush, I’ve already embarrassed myself three times in a row.*

Jing Ye let go of the leaf, and it fluttered back to the ground.

He switched the lollipop in his mouth to the other cheek, forming a small arc, then turned to leave.

After two steps, he suddenly paused.

He looked back over his shoulder, his gaze passing over his own shoulder to land on the girl still standing there, stunned.

His peach-blossom eyes curved with a half-smile, and his lips hooked in a mischievous grin: "My skills... unprecedented."

"?"

She blinked her clear almond-shaped eyes, the ice cream in her hand still emitting a faint chill, but her mind was blank.

*What skills?*

She stood there in confusion, watching him walk away step by step, until he finally disappeared into the neon-lit street corner.

Her delicate brows furrowed slightly. *Whatever. Forget it.*

She crouched beside her bicycle like a wronged little hamster, taking small, careful bites of her ice cream.

*—Wait.*

*—He just asked: Are you still on your period?*

*—He actually saw it!*

Too embarrassing.

*Really* too embarrassing.

The ice cream in her hand instantly lost its appeal.

She ate it all anyway, bite by bite, mechanically.

Then, she got on her bicycle and numbly pedaled toward the school.

---

Back in the dorm, she seemed drained of all energy, slumping limply into a chair.

"What’s wrong with you? You went out and came back looking like a frostbitten eggplant." Meng Lin was slurping instant noodles.

"Nothing." Sang Luoluo buried her face in the crook of her arm, her voice muffled.

"Don’t be so down. I’ll make you a bowl too. We’re not going to the cafeteria tonight—just manage with this." Tan Shuyin pushed aside her empty bowl and tore open a new pack of braised beef noodles.

Sang Luoluo lifted her face, forcing a smile that looked more painful than crying. "Thanks, Sister Tan."

Tan Shuyin was older than them and quite caring; they all called her "Sister Tan" like a reliable older sister.

Sang Luoluo slowly finished her noodles and cleaned up the table.

"Give me all your laundry. I’ll wash it together."

The moment the words left her mouth, the other three froze mid-motion, all turning to look at her.

Meng Lin crossed her arms and raised an eyebrow. "Spill it. What’s wrong?"

When Sang Luoluo was in a bad mood or troubled, she wouldn’t cry or make a fuss. Instead, she’d find something to throw herself into.

Back in their first year, when they had just moved in together and weren’t yet close, one night everyone was on their phones when she suddenly seemed to inject herself with stimulants. Without a word, she scrubbed every inch of the dorm, even the dust on top of the door frame.

Another time, she had silently gathered everyone’s dirty laundry and spent an entire afternoon washing it all in the laundry room, hanging it neatly across the balcony.

Sang Luoluo: "I did something embarrassing. Don’t ask. Just give me the clothes."

Meng Lin and Tan Shuyin exchanged a glance, silently agreeing not to press further. It must have been *really* embarrassing.

Since it was summer, they usually washed their clothes right after showering in the evening. They didn’t have any dirty laundry, so they just handed over a few clean items for Sang Luoluo to rewash.

Sang Luoluo didn’t wash them in the dorm’s small sink. Instead, she carried the basin to the laundry room on the first floor.

The space was larger there, with more sinks, making it easier to wash.

After finishing all the laundry, she carried the basin back to the dorm.

Meng Lin and Tan Shuyin immediately took it and went to hang everything on the balcony.

"Feeling better now?" Su Nan asked, handing her a glass of warm water.

"Mm, much better." Sang Luoluo let out a long sigh and slowly sipped the water.

From the balcony, they could hear Meng Lin shaking out the clothes. She poked half her body inside: "I swear, how are you so different from everyone else? When others are upset, they binge-eat or go shopping. But you? You turn into a little snail, burying yourself in work. Our dorm’s cleanliness and laundry are all thanks to your occasional emotional lows."

Sang Luoluo set down her glass, her eyes curving into a smile. A hint of amusement finally returned to her gaze. "Working helps me burn off all the messy emotions. Plus, I get things done at the same time. Two birds, one stone."

Meng Lin: "That makes sense. I’ll try that next time."

After hanging the clothes, she stepped back into the dorm in a few strides, excited: "You missed a *huge* scene while you were out! The dorm next door had another fight—this time, they actually *threw punches*! Oh my god, you should’ve seen it. They were pulling each other’s hair, kicking, scratching—no one could pull them apart. They even got the dorm supervisor involved!"

Sang Luoluo: "What was it about this time?"

Nine times out of ten, the fights next door were started by Wang Xiangru.

She could occupy the bathroom for an hour at a time, leaving her roommates desperate outside; she once complained that the smell of instant noodles ruined her expensive perfume; she even accused a roommate of *intentionally* disturbing her sleep because of a slight creak from the bed frame in the middle of the night.

In all her life, Sang Luoluo had never met anyone like her—constantly pushing boundaries in ways she never expected.

chapters.title: Obedience Doesn’t Mean Stupidity
chapters.content:
Meng Lin: "This reason is absolutely wild—you’d never guess it."

"Just because her new roommate gave Jingye a love letter, Wang Xiangru blew up. She pointed at the girl’s nose and called her a toad trying to eat swan meat, saying she should look in the mirror before daring to fantasize about Jingye."

"The new girl didn’t back down either—she’s got a sharp tongue. She fired back, saying some people stare at the mirror all day, but no one even knows who they are."

"Ouch, that really poked the hornet’s nest. Their words got uglier and uglier, and then they started pulling at each other."

Sang Luoluo listened quietly. She hadn’t known Wang Xiangru liked Jingye.

Su Nan: "She blows up just because someone gave him a love letter? That’s not love—that’s a psychological problem. Classic possessiveness and delusions, acting like Jingye is her personal property."

Tan Shuyin rubbed her temples, her face full of annoyance. "I’ve had enough of her. If the dorms weren’t so packed, I’d apply to switch just for some peace."

"Tan jie!" Meng Lin dramatically clutched her chest. "You’d abandon us for that idiot?"

"How could I?" Tan Shuyin shot her a helpless look. "I meant, if we switch, we switch together. How could I leave you guys behind—"

Before she could finish, the dorm door was slammed open with a *bang*, hitting the wall with a dull thud.

Wang Xiangru stood in the doorway, hair disheveled, a few sweat-dampened strands clinging to her forehead. Her face still bore the flushed red of anger, and her collar was visibly torn from the struggle.

Clearly, she had just come straight from the fight without even tidying up, her furious gaze locked onto Meng Lin.

All four of them stood up immediately.

Meng Lin crossed her arms, meeting Wang Xiangru’s glare without flinching. "Yeah, you. What? You want to fight us? We’re not scared of you."

She’d long since had enough of Wang Xiangru’s constant drama. Old and new grievances surged up, and her tone was sharp.

Wang Xiangru swept her eyes over the four of them standing in front of her but ultimately didn’t dare to actually throw a punch.

Her cold, piercing gaze finally settled on Sang Luoluo, who had been silent the whole time, as if she’d suddenly found an easier target to bully.

"Sang Luoluo, you usually act so superior. What’s this? Now you’re just like them, hiding behind others and gossiping?"

Sang Luoluo’s brows carried a faint, cold disdain. She didn’t even spare Wang Xiangru an extra glance. "What I do is none of your business. Get out. If you want to go crazy, do it on your own turf."

Wang Xiangru, like a wild cat with its tail stepped on, shrieked, "You dare call me crazy? Who do you think you are?! Just some girl from a run-down internet café! Even with the title of campus beauty, a hill myna can’t turn into a phoenix!"

She was jealous of Sang Luoluo’s face.

That face was too striking.

Even bare-faced, it carried a captivating, crisp allure. And with the title of campus beauty, it made Wang Xiangru’s heart burn with envy and rage every time she saw boys flocking around Sang Luoluo, fawning over her.

Did they really think she was a soft persimmon, to be pushed around?

She might be obedient, but she wasn’t an idiot!

Being mocked like this—did they really think she’d just take it?

Sang Luoluo let out a cold laugh. "What’s wrong with running an internet café? The money’s clean, and the people are decent."

She deliberately paused, her dark eyes clearly reflecting Wang Xiangru’s jealousy-twisted face.

The countless times Wang Xiangru had glared at her with venom, as if she wanted to scratch Sang Luoluo’s face—those images flashed through her mind in an instant.

Then, lightly, she delivered the final blow, each word cutting deep: "As for you—you’re right, you’re not as good-looking as me. So, you’ll never be the campus beauty."

"*Pfft—HAHAHA!*"

Meng Lin was the first to lose it, her laughter bursting out. Soon, Su Nan and Tan Shuyin were also bent over, shoulders shaking.

Sang Luoluo’s strike was precise and brutal, hitting Wang Xiangru right where it hurt.

Everyone knew Wang Xiangru valued her looks more than her life.

She could go three days without food, but never a day without a face mask. She’d rather break her leg than smudge her makeup.

And Sang Luoluo had stomped right on that sore spot.

Meng Lin, still laughing, secretly gave Sang Luoluo a thumbs-up behind her back.

Wang Xiangru’s face turned the color of pig liver. "Sang Luoluo! I’ll fight you to the death!"

She completely forgot that she was facing four people, or that she had just come from a fight, disheveled and exhausted. Like a lit firecracker, she lunged at Sang Luoluo, reaching for her hair.

"You dare lay a hand on her!" Meng Lin reacted fastest, stepping forward to block and shove Wang Xiangru’s hand away.

Su Nan and Tan Shuyin also rushed in, one on each side, restraining Wang Xiangru’s flailing arms so she couldn’t hit anyone.

Meng Lin pulled Sang Luoluo behind her to keep her out of harm’s way.

Wang Xiangru had completely lost her mind. She struggled to lunge forward, kicking wildly, her voice shrill with curses: "Bitch! You pretentious bitch! I’ll scratch your face off!"

The commotion was too loud. Doors from the neighboring dorms and across the hall swung open one after another. People poked their heads out, their faces a mix of shock and glee at the spectacle.

"What’s going on? Why are they fighting again?"

"Isn’t that Wang Xiangru? My God, what’s she flipping out about now?"

"Quick, go get the counselor!"

......

More than an hour later, the four of them returned to their dorm.

Meng Lin threw herself into a chair with a heavy thud. "My God, did you see that? Counselor Li’s face was as black as the bottom of a pot. Whoever ends up with a student like Wang Xiangru is cursed for eight generations. Thank God she’s not in our department."

Sang Luoluo plugged her phone into the charger and added, "The way Counselor Li looked at her at the end—it wasn’t anger, it was despair. I bet his biggest wish right now is for Wang Xiangru to do something bad enough to get expelled, just so he can be free of her."

Tan Shuyin glanced at Sang Luoluo. "Even then, she’d have to actually cross the line. With her, it’s all thunder and no rain—difficult."

Su Nan sighed. "I just hope she moves out. Ideally, she’d get transferred to some empty place where she can live alone. Then we’d finally have some peace."

Meng Lin, hearing this, slumped back in defeat, shaking her head at the ceiling. "That’s a great idea, but it’s not happening. The school doesn’t have spare dorms to give her a single room. Unless she moves out herself."

"And that’s impossible—she spends all her money on her appearance."

"Ugh, don’t even mention her. Just hearing her name pisses me off. Who’s showering first?"

"I’ll go."

---

In another dorm room.

"What are you looking at? Not playing the game?" Lu Zhi’an asked.

"Just eating melon," Chen Ge didn’t look up, swiping on his phone. "The group chat’s blowing up—our campus beauty got into a fight. There’s a video of it."

Jingye was a little surprised. "The campus beauty? That Sang Luoluo? She seems so obedient—how could she get into a fight?"

"Here, see for yourself." Chen Ge turned his phone screen toward them, deliberately increasing the volume.

The video was clearly filmed secretly in the dorm hallway—shaky, with chaotic footsteps and gasps in the background.

In the footage, a disheveled girl was trying to lunge forward, her eyes wild, mouth spewing curses, while two other girls held her back from behind.

Meanwhile, a stunningly beautiful girl was shielded by another, her back straight as a board, her face showing no hint of panic.

chapters.title: She’s Really Too Obedient—So Obedient It Makes You Want to Take Her Home and Keep Her
chapters.content:
Jingye had been leaning back in his chair with his eyes closed, resting. When the video’s harsh shouting reached his ears, he slowly turned his head, his gaze falling on the screen. His expression darkened instantly.

"Who’s the campus beauty?" he asked.

Chen Ge pushed the phone closer to him and tapped the screen, pointing at the girl being protected. "This one. Sang Luoluo."

"You wouldn’t know, Wild Brother—you’ve been abroad for a year. She topped the campus beauty rankings as soon as she enrolled, knocking off Feng Wan’er, who’d been at the top for two years. Isn’t she gorgeous? And she’s a straight-A student too. Rumor has it she’s consistently first in her major—so many awards she could fill a room."

Shen Juan, recalling something, asked Chen Ge, "That internet café outside campus—is it her family’s?"

Chen Ge nodded rapidly. "Yeah, yeah! It’s hers. That place has practically become a must-visit for the guys in our school, just so they can catch a glimpse of her."

"Why did the fight start?" Jingye’s eyes didn’t leave the screen.

The video was too fragmented to make out the cause, only capturing the girl’s hysterical screams. His brows furrowed deeply, a cold glint flashing in his eyes.

Chen Ge: "Apparently, this crazy woman’s roommate gave you a love letter, and when she found out, she exploded. But how it involved Sang Luoluo, I’m not sure."

Lu Zhi’an looked at Jingye, teasing, "Did you hear that? You’re the root of all this trouble. These girls are only causing chaos because of you."

Chen Ge quickly scrolled through his phone, reading as he went. "Whoa, the comments are exploding. Everyone’s calling this girl the dorm building’s tumor, stirring up the whole floor. There’s a whole string of posts wishing she’d just move out—looks like she’s really pushed people to their limits."

Jingye listened, then took the phone to the balcony and made a call.

The balcony door was half-closed, so the details of the conversation couldn’t be heard—only his brief, low responses. After less than two minutes, he hung up.

He returned inside, his expression unchanged.

Chen Ge put down his phone and switched topics. "But seriously, I’m more curious—what’s the guy like that our campus beauty likes?"

Jingye’s gaze, which had been elsewhere, shifted slightly, settling back on Chen Ge’s face. "How do you know she likes someone?"

Chen Ge spread his hands. "She said it herself! Someone confessed to her, and she rejected them on the spot, clear as day: *‘I already like someone.’* There were a lot of people watching—it’s not a secret anymore."

Jingye lowered his gaze, his emotions unreadable.

Silently, he opened the campus forum and typed two characters into the search bar: *campus beauty*.

Chen Ge, seeing that Jingye wasn’t engaging, lost interest in gossiping. He shrugged and put down his phone, joining Lu Zhi’an and the others in a game.

On the screen, posts and photos about her quickly appeared.

At the top was a high-resolution side profile shot, the pixels sharp.

She was wearing a pale yellow floral dress, standing in front of the library’s glass window.

The lighting was perfect, clearly showing the clean lines from her nose to her lips. Her skin looked flawlessly fair in the natural light.

She was looking down at a book, her lashes casting dense shadows, her lips a natural cherry pink, pressed together in quiet concentration.

*—She’s really too obedient… so obedient it makes you want to take her home and keep her, pet her a little.*

He kept scrolling and found another video about her.

The title was eye-catching: **[Spotlight | The Only Underclassman! Sang Luoluo Shines at the National English Academic Forum]**.

He put on his headphones and clicked.

In the video, it was her freshman year, second semester.

She stood on stage, dressed in a simple blouse and knee-length skirt, her long hair neatly tied back, revealing her smooth forehead and calm, focused eyes. The usual softness was gone, replaced by a professional and capable demeanor.

She was striking.

The audience was packed with scholars and students, the camera panning over their rapt expressions.

She held no script, only a remote clicker, effortlessly controlling the PPT with composed ease.

Her entire presentation was in English, her voice clear and steady, every professional term pronounced with precision.

During the Q&A, she paused briefly to think before smiling and responding to each question with confidence, radiating brilliance. It was hard to believe she was just a first-year student.

The video was short and ended quickly.

Jingye removed his headphones, recalling the first time he saw her—his breath had caught unexpectedly.

In his usually silent world, there had suddenly been a heartbeat, just like now—his heartbeat was still out of rhythm.

---

The next day, at the cafeteria entrance.

Chen Ge clutched his stomach, laughing so hard he couldn’t straighten up. His finger trembled as he pointed at the newly posted notice, his voice distorted from laughter:

"Oh my God! I can’t—this is too much! Wild Brother, look!"
