**[Important Notice: Due to recent high foot traffic in the cafeteria, to maintain order, Jingye is requested to refrain from dining in the cafeteria for the time being. Thank you for your cooperation!]**

"I told you not to come here, but you insisted. Look—even the cafeteria manager had to personally ban you!" Chen Ge laughed, wiping tears from his eyes, his tone full of schadenfreude.

No one knew what had come over Jingye today—he had insisted on coming to the cafeteria.

The four of them rarely came here, maybe only a few times a year.

They weren’t short on money. Normally, they either ordered fancy takeout or went to off-campus restaurants. The crowded, noisy cafeteria was never their first choice.

Lu Zhi’an and Shen Juan weren’t any better off. They covered their mouths, stepping aside as tears of laughter welled in their eyes.

The cafeteria manager was a middle-aged man with a round face. He gave Jingye an apologetic, pained smile.

"Jing, my boy, I’m really sorry. These past few days, so many students have been coming here just for you. The lines wrap around the cafeteria three times over. The workload is just too much—our two aunts who serve the food have worked themselves to exhaustion and had to take leave. We simply don’t have the manpower to keep up."

"Could you please avoid eating here for a while? Once this craze dies down and things return to normal, you’re welcome anytime. I’ll personally arrange a window for you. How’s that sound?"

Jingye: "..."

Inside the cafeteria, Meng Lin was shoveling rice into her mouth when she suddenly spotted someone at the entrance. Her eyes lit up, and she elbowed the person next to her. "Look at the door! Jingye’s here!"

She remembered the freshly posted notice and couldn’t hold back her laughter.

Sang Luoluo, hearing this, turned her head instinctively.

Through the shifting crowd and the clear glass doors, she immediately saw Jingye standing at the entrance.

He was slightly tilting his head up, looking at the eye-catching notice on the wall.

From this distance, she couldn’t make out his expression, but she caught the faint lift of his eyebrow.

"That guy’s probably confused," Tan Shuyin, sitting beside her, had also noticed. She shook her head with a laugh. "But the cafeteria’s right to do this. If it’s this packed every day, I’d go crazy too. Who wants to eat the bottom of the pot every time?"

Right then, an exceptionally eye-catching girl, wearing high heels, swaying her hips, and holding a pink love letter, walked toward Jingye.

Sang Luoluo’s gaze followed the girl.

The girl was dressed in a red spaghetti-strap top and a black miniskirt so short it barely covered her backside. Every step she took oozed seduction, drawing the attention of everyone around.

She stopped in front of Jingye and, with absolute confidence and deliberate flattery, said:

"Senior, welcome back."

"This is my love letter. I really like you. You won’t regret making me your girlfriend. I’ll be very obedient, more obedient than an animal. I’ll do whatever you ask."

She said this without a shred of concern for the stares of others.

So what if Jingye had a girlfriend? Who said you couldn’t steal someone else’s man?

The cafeteria manager silently turned his head away, frowning up at the sky and shaking his head.

These young girls—why waste time on studies when they’ve got the nerve to be this shameless?

Publicly hitting on a guy like this, and with such boldness—no sense of shame at all.

If this were his daughter, he’d slap her dead.

Chen Ge and his friends, however, seemed unfazed, casually waiting a few steps away. Chen Ge raised his voice, urging, "Wild Brother, hurry up. We’re starving."

Jingye’s gaze didn’t leave the notice. He spoke indifferently:

"Then you’ll have to prove first—how are you better than an animal?"

chapters.title: Call Him Brother
chapters.content:
"Pfft—!"

Chen Ge was kicking a stone by the roadside, laughing so hard he bent over.

A few students eavesdropping nearby quickly turned their backs, covering their mouths to stifle their laughter.

The girl’s face darkened with embarrassment. She had just said that casually—it wasn’t like she was seriously comparing him to an animal.

When Jingye said those words, he never once glanced in her direction, not even for a second.

This complete and utter disregard hurt more than what he had just said.

She crumpled the love letter into a ball, clutching it tightly in her hand, biting her lip as she stormed out of the crowd without looking back.

Meng Lin clicked her tongue. "How did Jingye even reject her? Look how happy everyone is, and the girl’s face is all flushed with anger."

"She knew he had a girlfriend and still forced herself on him. She probably brought this on herself." Tan Shuyin shook her head.

As they spoke, Jingye had already turned and left with a few other boys outside.

Sang Luoluo was about to look away when Jingye, walking at the back, suddenly turned his head. His gaze swept precisely across the cafeteria’s glass window.

For a fleeting moment, their eyes met through the shifting crowd and the glass, as if they truly, tangibly collided.

Sang Luoluo’s heart skipped a beat. Almost reflexively, she turned back, her spine straightening.

—*Sang Luoluo, what are you panicking for?*

—*With this distance and so many people, there’s no way he could have noticed you peeking.*

"Everyone’s gone, let’s eat quickly." Su Nan urged, picking up a piece of greens with her chopsticks.

....

As soon as the four of them stepped into the dormitory hallway, they saw a group of people gathered outside the neighboring door, chattering away.

"Thank goodness, that plague goddess finally moved out!"

"Finally, our floor can have some peace."

"You should’ve seen it—just now, the dorm supervisor was directing people to help her move. Her expression was like she was getting rid of something filthy, as if she couldn’t wait for her to disappear."

"I heard she hit a wall. The principal personally warned her—if she causes any more trouble, she’ll be expelled. That’s why she’s finally behaving."

Sang Luoluo and Meng Lin exchanged a glance. The latter immediately jogged over and squeezed into the crowd. "Are you talking about Wang Xiangru moving out?"

A girl nodded. "Yeah, she just left. Her stuff’s all cleared out."

"Amazing! Our good days are finally here!" Meng Lin cheered, then curiously asked, "But where did she move to? Did she find a new dorm so quickly?"

A girl in the know sneered, "Hardly a proper dorm. They temporarily put her in that old, unused storage room by the west district. It’s quiet—perfect for her."

"I heard they even made her copy 'I am an ugly, old, shameless woman' a thousand times."

"Ha! That must’ve hit her where it hurts. Everyone knows how much she treasures her looks. This is way worse than any other punishment."

The hallway erupted in knowing laughter, the long-suppressed frustration finally dissipating.

Back in the room, Meng Lin excitedly swiped on her phone, slapping the table as she announced, "I’m treating you all today! Milk tea or fruit tea, ladies? We’ve been holding this in for a year—we *have* to celebrate properly."

Tan Shuyin said, "Milk tea. Everyone likes that. Same as usual."

"Got it, coming right up." Meng Lin agreed readily, her fingers flying across the screen.

Her phone buzzed in her pocket—it was her mother, Ye Rong, calling.

Sang Luoluo walked toward the balcony as she answered, "Mom!"

"Luoluo, your mother’s coming to pick you up from school tonight. Let’s go out for a nice meal." Ye Rong’s voice came through the receiver.

"Okay!" Sang Luoluo asked with a smile, "Aren’t you busy today?"

"Even if I’m busy, I have to make time for my daughter." Ye Rong’s tone was light and cheerful. "Oh, do you remember Aunt Tang?"

"Of course. Why bring her up suddenly?" Sang Luoluo had only met her once when she was very young.

"She’s back in the country. Her son’s also at Jingda University. We’ll all have dinner together tonight—you young people should get to know each other and look out for one another."

"Okay, see you tonight."

---

After class that evening, Sang Luoluo handed her bag over. "Linlin, my mom’s taking me out to eat. Can you take my bag back for me?"

"Sure." Meng Lin took the bag, slung it over her shoulder, and left with the other two.

Sang Luoluo walked to the school gate and immediately spotted Ye Rong standing with a well-dressed woman, the two of them chatting and smiling.

"Luoluo." Ye Rong waved her over.

She jogged toward them, her skirt swaying gently with each step. "Mom, Aunt Tang."

"Luoluo’s all grown up in the blink of an eye—she’s a young lady now." Tang Suqin replied with a smile, her gaze warm as it settled on the girl’s face, tinged with a hint of nostalgia from the passage of time.

"You’re back in the country this time—are you leaving again?" Ye Rong turned her head slightly, softly asking her old friend.

Tang Suqin was a dancer. Over the years, she had spent most of her time performing all over the world, with long separations and few reunions.

Tang Suqin shook her head. "No, I’m staying. I’ve danced half my life—my body can’t keep up anymore, and my heart’s tired too. I just want to settle down and live quietly here."

As she finished speaking, her eyes lit up, and she raised a hand toward the school gate. "Look, my son’s coming out too."

Sang Luoluo followed her gaze.

In the twilight, a tall, straight figure walked toward them at a leisurely pace.

When he fully came into view, her eyes flickered.

What a coincidence?

"Your son is really handsome." Ye Rong said, looking at the young man with a smile.

Jingye’s gaze lingered on Sang Luoluo’s face for a brief moment. His dark eyes flashed with a hint of amusement, and the corner of his lips lifted ambiguously.

*What a coincidence indeed.*

He walked up to them, his voice warm as he called out, "Mom."

"Xiao Ye," Tang Suqin introduced, "This is Aunt Ye, my old classmate. And this is her daughter, Sang Luoluo. You two go to the same university."

"Hello, Aunt Ye." Jingye nodded politely.

Ye Rong smiled in return.

Tang Suqin patted Sang Luoluo’s hand. "Luoluo, Xiao Ye is a year older than you. From now on, just call him *gege*."

Sang Luoluo pressed her lips together. Seeing both mothers smiling at her expectantly, she had no choice but to curve her lips into a perfectly measured smile. "Gege."

The word *gege* was soft and light, carrying the gentle, moist warmth of the southern waters. As it brushed past his ears, it sent a tingling sensation through him.

His gaze darkened slightly. He responded in a low voice, "Mm."

"Xiao Ye, let Luoluo ride with you. We’re going to Yuntian Pavilion Restaurant." Tang Suqin instructed.

Jingye nodded and turned to her. "Let’s go."

Sang Luoluo hesitated for a moment before nodding. Her heart felt like it was carrying a rabbit, thumping wildly as she silently followed behind him.

When they reached the black Bentley Mulsanne, Jingye bent down and got into the driver’s seat.

Sang Luoluo walked toward the back seat and reached for the door handle.

"Are you treating me like a chauffeur?" His voice came from inside the car, emotionless, but it made Sang Luoluo freeze.

Through the dark-tinted window, she couldn’t see his expression.

After a moment of hesitation, she closed the back door and opened the passenger door instead, sliding in.

Jingye turned his head.

The young girl sat upright, her hands folded neatly in her lap, her gaze fixed outside the window.

He leaned over, extending a hand toward her.

Sang Luoluo suddenly turned back, then hastily lowered her lashes, her breath catching for a moment.

His hand still hovered in the air in front of her. Her voice was a little tense. "Do you need to grab something?"

Jingye withdrew his hand. "You didn’t buckle your seatbelt."

Sang Luoluo blinked in surprise, then quickly reached for the seatbelt.

"Good. Now we can drive."

"Mm." He shifted his gaze back, started the car, and merged into the dazzling night.

The car was silent the whole way, with no conversation until they reached their destination.

---

chapters.title: Added on WeChat
chapters.content:
After getting out of the car, Sang Luoluo linked arms with Ye Rong.

The four of them walked into the restaurant’s private room together, following the waiter’s lead to their seats.

Sang Luoluo and Ye Rong sat on one side, with Tang Suqin and Jingye across from them.

After ordering, Ye Rong and Tang Suqin started chatting.

Sang Luoluo picked up her cup and took a sip, her peripheral vision casually sweeping over Jingye.

He was looking down at his phone, the dim blue light of the screen casting a glow on his pale, cold face.

During the meal, he was very quiet, barely making a sound. He ate slowly and deliberately, every movement exuding an elegant, leisurely nobility.

Tang Suqin set down her teacup. "You and Sang Xiu have been separated for so many years. Aren’t you thinking of finding someone new?"

Ye Rong waved her hand, her smile carrying a calm acceptance. "At this age, having Luoluo by my side is good enough. Life is going smoothly—I don’t need to add unnecessary complications."

Jingye heard this and lifted his gaze. He saw the usually quiet girl across from him looking somewhat distracted, her lowered lashes trembling slightly, a faint, almost imperceptible shadow flickering in her eyes.

Sang Luoluo bit her lip. Her parents had divorced when she was in junior high.

The reason was simple and cruel: her father had already been with someone else, and even had another son.

Since then, Ye Rong had devoted all her energy to Sang Luoluo, raising her alone, working hard, and taking meticulous care of her. She never brought up her own love life again.

As for her father, after the divorce, he had reportedly moved abroad with that mistress and their son, cutting off all contact and completely disappearing from their lives.

Tang Suqin asked with concern, "When Luoluo gets married in the future, what will you do?"

"If she needs me, I’ll help with the children. If she’s living comfortably on her own, I’ll just travel around and see the world." Ye Rong said, turning to look at her daughter, her eyes shining. "In this life, however you live it, isn’t it just living? It’s best to go with the flow."

Sang Luoluo looked up, meeting her mother’s smiling gaze.

The tender part of her heart was warmed by these words, yet a faint, bittersweet ache spread through her.

"Mom, if you meet someone suitable, just give it a try. I hope there’s someone to keep you company."

Ye Rong gently rubbed her daughter’s hair. "Silly child, I’m really fine the way I am. I have you, and I have work I love. My heart is full—I don’t feel like I’m missing anything."

Sang Luoluo saw the sincerity and tranquility in Ye Rong’s expression. The light in her mother’s eyes was genuine—she truly lived a fulfilling and content life. So Sang Luoluo didn’t say more and just picked up another bite of her favorite dish.

Tang Suqin understood her friend’s nature and knew she had made up her mind, so she dropped the subject.

Ye Rong smiled at Jingye. "Xiao Ye, Luoluo is soft-hearted. In the future, I hope you can look out for her at school. Don’t let anyone bully her."

"Of course, Aunt Ye." Jingye nodded in agreement. He pulled out a QR code and held it in front of her. "Add me on WeChat. It’ll be convenient if you need to contact me."

Sang Luoluo was slightly taken aback. She had never imagined she’d have the chance to add him on WeChat.

She tried to keep her hands steady as she unlocked her phone and opened WeChat to scan the code.

The camera focused, recognized the code, and with a soft *ding*, the friend request was sent.

His profile picture was pure black, and his nickname was simply the letter "J."

She didn’t dare look for long. She quickly turned off the screen, put her phone back in her pocket, and lowered her head to continue eating.

Jingye clicked into her Moments.

There wasn’t much content—just a few sparse posts lying quietly on her timeline.

He scrolled through them one by one.

Autumn: A stone path covered in ginkgo leaves, a thick layer of golden foliage. In the corner of the photo, a small white shoe caught a whole leaf, the toe slightly lifted—kind of cute.

Spring: Under a cherry blossom tree, petals falling like snow. A slender, fair hand entered the frame, palm up, catching a falling pink petal. The wrist was delicate, the bones slightly prominent, the skin so white it was dazzling.

Summer: A rose-colored evening sky, with the dark silhouette of a teaching building below. A hand holding a transparent cup of lemon water rested on the windowsill, the fingertips tinged red by the sunset, the nails neatly trimmed, exuding a fresh, girlish charm.

Winter: Fresh snow covered the windowsill, a thin layer. The glass was fogged, faintly reflecting the side profile of someone reading a book, long hair falling, the curve of the lashes blurred yet gentle—so quiet it was like a painting.

No captions, no full-face photos, not even a single emoji.

She quietly left traces of herself in the scenery of the four seasons, as light as a whisper.

He had never met someone so quiet in his life.

So quiet that even her sharing felt like talking to herself, expecting no response.

He looked up. Across the table, the girl was eating her rice in small, delicate bites, her cheeks soft, her eyes gentle. Something in his chest pricked him, and he couldn’t describe the feeling.

After dinner, the four of them walked out of the restaurant together.

Tang Suqin said to Sang Luoluo, "Your mom’s wedding planning companies are swamped during holidays. From now on, when you’re on break, come back with your brother. I’ve prepared a room for you. Whatever you want to eat, Aunt Tang will make it for you."

Ye Rong also smiled and nodded beside her. "Yes, listen to Aunt Tang. Consider that place your second home—don’t be a stranger."

Sang Luoluo nodded politely. "Thank you, Aunt Tang."

Tang Suqin then turned to Jingye. "Xiao Ye, you two head back to school together. Drive carefully—don’t go too fast."

Ye Rong added, "Luoluo, get in the car. Send me a message when you arrive."

"Mom, Aunt Tang, we’ll go now." Sang Luoluo said her goodbyes, then opened the passenger door and got in. This time, she remembered to buckle her seatbelt and didn’t repeat her earlier embarrassment.

The ride back was just as quiet.

They weren’t familiar with each other, so they didn’t know what to talk about. It was fine this way.

Sang Luoluo subtly turned her gaze to the side. All she could see was his hand resting on the steering wheel.

*What a beautiful hand.*

She thought aimlessly. Just looking at these hands, one might mistake him for a girl.

The car stopped near the school gate.

She softly said, "Thank you." Her fingertips had just touched the door handle when his voice suddenly came, "You can reach out to me if you need anything."

Sang Luoluo paused for two seconds before replying, "Okay."

She pushed the door open, and the night wind rushed at her face.

There were many students coming and going at the gate. Not wanting to cause unnecessary misunderstandings, she didn’t wait for him and quickly merged into the flowing crowd.

When she returned to the dorm, Meng Lin was sitting cross-legged on a chair, typing on her keyboard. Hearing the movement, she turned her head. "Back?"

"Mm." Sang Luoluo changed her shoes and sat at her desk.

She opened WeChat and went to his Moments. It was completely blank—nothing at all.

*Well, he didn’t seem like the type to post on Moments anyway.*

She stared at his profile picture for a long time, her fingertip lightly brushing the cold letter.

Su Nan noticed Meng Lin was still at it and reminded her, "Linlin, shouldn’t you be doing your homework?"

Meng Lin’s hands froze on the keyboard, her eyes wide. "Oh no, I forgot!"

Tan Shuyin, who was doing her homework, didn’t even look up as she said coolly, "I *did* remind you. I don’t know who you were talking to, but you were smiling so hard the screen was reflecting light."

Sang Luoluo lowered her emotions and put her phone down. Lately, she had noticed that whenever Meng Lin was on her computer, the corners of her eyes and mouth were always curved in a smile—clearly, something good was happening.

"You’re not dating someone, are you?"

"Not yet," Meng Lin said, pressing her lips together, her eyes sparkling. "But if I do, I’ll definitely tell you first."

"*Not... yet?*" Tan Shuyin drew out the words. "So there *is* something going on. You’re in the ambiguous phase, huh?"

Meng Lin blinked, not denying it. "Well, you’re not wrong. But anyway, homework comes first. If I don’t finish it by tomorrow, I’m doomed."

Sang Luoluo had already done most of her homework in class—only a little was left.

She flipped open her notebook, picked up her pen, and, like Meng Lin, sat properly at her desk to finish her work.

chapters.title: He Calls Her to Eat
chapters.content:
The next day after class, as they reached the stairwell corner, they noticed something unusual in the air.

A crowd had gathered in the lobby downstairs and the open space outside, all staring toward the adjacent Finance College building.

Murmurs rippled up the stairs like waves on water.

"What's going on down there?" Menglin leaned over the railing to look.

Sang Luoluo stopped walking and peered through the glass window of the stairwell.

In the open space in front of the Finance College building, Jing Ye stood with one hand in his pocket, wearing a high-quality black silk shirt that shimmered with his movements.

He was idly flipping a silver lighter between his fingers.

In front of him stood an older professor from the department, speaking to him.

Jing Ye listened, occasionally nodding.

His posture didn’t resemble that of a student, but rather someone in charge listening to a subordinate’s report.

The afternoon breeze tousled the black hair at his forehead, a few loose strands falling over his brows.

Jing Ye didn’t bother fixing it. He casually slipped the lighter back into his pocket, his gaze lazily scanning the gathered crowd.

As his eyes passed over them, they were both wild and indifferent.

A few girls who had been stealing glances blushed to the roots of their ears and quickly averted their eyes.

He tilted his head back, stretching his neck, the long line of his throat taut, his Adam’s apple sliding under his fair skin.

His gaze swept through the air in a careless arc.

Without deviation, it barely grazed the window of the stairwell.

Sang Luoluo felt as if the lingering warmth of that gaze had lightly scalded her heart. She quickly lowered her lashes and tugged at Menglin’s sleeve.

"Let’s go. If we don’t hurry, there won’t be any seats left."

She didn’t look out the window again. Turning, she descended the stairs faster than usual.

The three behind her hurried to keep up.

Exiting the teaching building, Sang Luoluo didn’t look back. She led them toward the cafeteria without a moment’s hesitation.

The professor finally patted his shoulder. "Depart the day after tomorrow. The others going with you will meet you at the airport."

"Okay." Jing Ye responded, his gaze sweeping past the bustling crowd, following the hurriedly retreating figure.

After the professor left, he faced that direction and called out lazily, "Sang Luoluo."

Menglin was the first to turn around, her eyes widening in shock, her mouth left agape.

Jing Ye was walking toward them.

She poked Sang Luoluo’s arm hard, unable to contain her excitement. "Luoluo! It’s Senior Jing! He seems to be calling you!"

Sang Luoluo froze mid-step, stiffly turning around.

Jing Ye was already within three steps, his presence carrying the warmth of the sunlight as it rushed toward them.

Behind him followed three equally striking young men—tall, long-legged, each with distinct auras. Together, they looked like an unretouched fashion spread.

The four of them effortlessly commanded all the oxygen and attention in the vicinity.

She met his gaze, softly calling out, "Gege."

"Gege?!"

Menglin gasped, looking at Jing Ye, then at Sang Luoluo, her face filled with shock that almost spilled over.

She grabbed Tan Shuyin’s sleeve. "Did I just hallucinate? What did Luoluo call him?"

It wasn’t just Menglin and the others—everyone within earshot had caught the shocking address, and the whispers around them instantly grew louder.

Chen Ge let out a whistle, teasing, "Yo, Brother Ye, how did the campus beauty suddenly become your sister? You’ve been hiding this well."

Earlier, when Jing Ye had been asked about Sang Luoluo, he had acted as if he didn’t know her at all. How had she suddenly become "gege"?

Jing Ye ignored his remark, his eyes fixed on Sang Luoluo. "Let’s go eat."

"Where to?" Sang Luoluo asked instinctively, her mind still a little dazed.

"Sister, do you even need to ask?" Chen Ge enthusiastically took over, sweeping his gaze over Menglin and the others. "Of course we’re going out to eat. These are your roommates, right? All of you, our treat."

Menglin’s eyes lit up immediately. She tightly grabbed Sang Luoluo’s arm—eating with Jing Ye was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity!

Sang Luoluo looked at her roommates’ eager expressions, then glanced at Jing Ye. Seeing no objection from him, she gave a slight nod.

"Let’s go." Chen Shu raised his hand in a grand gesture, and the four young men led the way, walking casually and chatting.

The four girls followed behind them like little tails.

Menglin stayed close to Sang Luoluo, lowering her voice to ask, "Are you and Jing Ye cousins or something?"

Sang Luoluo’s gaze remained fixed on the tall figure ahead. "Nothing like that!"

"What do you mean? Explain!" Menglin’s curiosity was piqued even more.

Sang Luoluo: "My mom and his mom are best friends. That’s the only connection."

Menglin let out an "Oh," understanding. "I see."

"Then yesterday, when your mom called you out to eat, was he there too?" Su Nan asked.

Sang Luoluo nodded, her eyes still locked on the figure ahead. His shoulders seemed much broader than she remembered.

Tan Shuyin linked arms with Sang Luoluo from the other side. "Thanks to you, we get to eat at the same table as the most popular figures on campus. This VIP experience card isn’t easy to come by."

Menglin’s curiosity had reached its peak. "Yesterday, when you were chatting, did you ask Jing Ye about his girlfriend? Is it true, like the forums say, that she’s a rich, beautiful woman studying abroad?"

Sang Luoluo pressed her lips together, her lashes lowering. "No, I didn’t ask."

They weren’t close enough for that kind of question. Just being able to sit and eat with him was enough for her.

Menglin looked at her as if she were wasting a golden opportunity. "Sang Luoluo, you’re literally squandering top-tier gossip material! You have the ultimate resource and no intention of using it!"

Su Nan: "Menglin, don’t you know Luoluo’s personality by now? When has she ever proactively asked about things like that?"

Walking ahead, Chen Ge grinned, half-jokingly bumping Jing Ye’s shoulder. "Not bad, Brother Ye. How did the campus beauty end up as your sister? You’ve kept this well hidden."

"Her mother and my mother were college classmates. They’re close." Jing Ye kept it brief.

Chen Ge drew out his tone, "Oh~ I see, fate, fate."

They reached the restaurant entrance. The men laughed and entered first, the women following behind.

Jing Ye walked at the rear, watching the figure ahead.

Today, she wore a white fitted dress, her demeanor like an ethereal fairy untouched by worldly concerns.

That waist—so slender he could easily wrap both hands around it.

He wondered, if he really did grip her waist like that and pull her into his embrace, would she still be this obedient? Would she meekly let him... flip her like a pancake?

Sang Luoluo kept feeling like the person behind her was watching her. Whether it was her imagination or not, her back had grown stiff.

She didn’t dare to look back, maintaining her forward march stiffly until the waiter led them into a private room, where she finally let out a breath.

Chen Ge, familiar with the place, picked up the electronic menu and handed it to the girls first, smiling warmly. "Ladies, take a look and order whatever you like. Don’t hold back—Brother Ye’s treating today."

Menglin took the menu and huddled with the others to pick their usual favorites.

The men ordered even faster, going straight for the most expensive dishes.

Chen Ge clapped his hands cheerfully, "Alright, let’s officially introduce ourselves."

"I’m Chen Ge. This is Lu Zhi’an and Shen Juan."

He gestured to the two distinct figures beside him.

"We four have been close since we were kids, practically grew up together in diapers."

"Nice to meet you, seniors." Menglin introduced them confidently. "I’m Menglin. This is Tan Shuyin, Su Nan, and her—Sang Luoluo."

"Let’s add each other!" Chen Ge enthusiastically took out his phone, its wallpaper a photo of a race car.

"You’re Sang’s friends, so from now on, you’re all our friends too. If you ever need anything at school, just let us know."

Under his lead, the slightly awkward atmosphere quickly livened up.

The girls also took out their phones, smiling as they scanned each other’s QR codes, the mood gradually warming.

---

chapters.title: He Calls Her Heartless
chapters.content:
Sang Luoluo quietly added Chen Ge and the other two as well.

When it came to Jing Ye, he was looking down, his fingertips sliding across his phone screen, seemingly absorbed in something.

Menglin hesitated, unsure how to ask.

Chen Ge, noticing her gaze, waved his hand dismissively. "Don’t bother with him, little sister. Our Brother Ye doesn’t add people on WeChat."

"Oh, right, got it." Menglin’s face showed a flicker of understanding, as if it were only natural.

If Jing Ye were the type to hand out his WeChat so easily, would he still be Jing Ye?

But in the next second, Jing Ye calmly placed his phone in the center of the table. On the screen, a QR code was displayed openly.

"Add me."

Two words, said lightly, yet they plunged the entire private room into an eerie silence.

Chen Ge stared at him as if he were an alien, his eyes nearly popping out, his mouth forming a perfect "O."

"O-oh! Okay!"

Menglin was the first to react, practically lunging forward to scan the code so quickly her fingers left afterimages, as if afraid he’d change his mind the next second.

Tan Shuyin and Su Nan immediately followed, the glow of their phone screens reflecting their excitement.

Lu Zhi’an nudged Shen Juan, lowering his voice. "What’s going on? The sun’s rising from the west?"

Chen Ge leaned in, ears perked up, his face filled with a thirst for knowledge.

Shen Juan glanced at Jing Ye, whose expression remained unchanged, then at Sang Luoluo, sitting quietly. "Love extends to the crows? That reason seems a bit far-fetched."

Lu Zhi’an analyzed, "It has to be that. Their mothers know each other, so Aunt Tang must’ve told him a hundred times to take good care of Sang Luoluo. Adding her roommates is probably for convenience. If anything happens to Sang Luoluo, he can at least find out from them."

Chen Ge listened, nodding thoughtfully as if accepting the explanation.

He straightened up and stared at Sang Luoluo, gossiping, "Little sister, what’s it like having Jing Ye as your brother?"

Sang Luoluo’s fingertips secretly tightened around her dress. "No particular feeling."

From being complete strangers to being this close to him—of course she was happy, secretly thrilled even. But she couldn’t say that.

Lu Zhi’an adjusted his glasses, his tone teasing. "Jing Ye, what kind of heavenly sin did you commit to make a junior’s opinion of you as blank as a sheet of paper?"

Chen Ge laughed, slapping his thigh. "Ha! First time seeing someone immune to our Brother Ye. A rare species!"

He tilted his chin toward Jing Ye. "Which girl doesn’t light up like she’s got a level-10 beauty filter on when she sees him? Your reaction is refreshingly natural. Precious, very precious."

Menglin, seeing that they had both finished scanning, pushed Jing Ye’s phone back to him, smiling to smooth things over. "Seniors, you’ve misunderstood. Our Luoluo is like this with all guys—very boundaried. It’s not personal."

Jing Ye didn’t respond. He took back his phone, tapped the screen a few times, and sent a message.

Chen Ge was still nodding, putting on a big brother act. "Little sister, if you ever run into trouble at school, just find your brother. He’ll handle it for you. No one will dare bully you!"

"Okay, senior." Sang Luoluo replied, her lips curving politely.

As soon as she finished speaking, her phone buzzed.

Jing Ye: 【Do you dislike me?】

Sang Luoluo looked up, meeting Jing Ye’s direct gaze. His almond-shaped eyes held a hint of a smile, making her heart skip a beat.

She bit her lip and replied: 【No.】

Jing Ye: 【Then your review was hurtful. Why did I add your roommates? Can’t you tell? Heartless little thing.】

She hovered over the screen, typing and deleting.

Finally, she replied with a dry: 【I can tell. Thank you, gege.】

Jing Ye: 【That’s it?】

Sang Luoluo thought for a moment, then added: 【Then I’ll rephrase—I’m happy.】

Jing Ye: 【Good girl.】

Sang Luoluo: "......"

This tone—was he really treating her like a little sister?

She suddenly didn’t know how to reply. Just then, the waiter knocked on the door and began serving the dishes, so she turned off her screen.

Jing Ye, sitting across from her, didn’t send any more messages upon seeing this.

The porcelain plates landed softly on the tablecloth, each dish plated like a work of art.

The stir-fried seasonal vegetables resembled an ink painting, the braised pork was served in a custom coarse ceramic bowl, and even the rice was molded into a smooth oval.

Chen Ge raised his glass first, his smile bright. "Come on, first toast—to welcome Sang little sister, and all you beautiful ladies. Let’s get together more often!"

Glasses clinked, producing a crisp sound.

Sang Luoluo picked up her glass of fresh orange juice and took a small sip.

*Knock knock!* The private room door was tapped twice.

"Come in!" Chen Ge called out.

The door opened, and a girl in a light beige dress walked in.

She wore thin high heels, her makeup flawless, long hair cascading over her shoulders, exuding an elegant aura. The moment she entered, she captured everyone’s attention.

Feng Wan’er’s gaze swept across the room before settling on Jing Ye, her smile perfectly radiant.

"I heard you brought your sister out to eat. I was just next door, so I came over to see."

Chen Ge teased, raising an eyebrow. "Feng Wan’er, your information network is impressive. We haven’t even warmed our seats yet, and you already know Jing Ye has a sister?"

Feng Wan’er stepped inside, her skirt swaying gracefully with each step. "You know how it is—any little rumor on campus spreads faster than anything else."

Her gaze seemingly casually passed over Sang Luoluo, who was sitting across from Jing Ye.

She knew this girl—the one who had taken her title of campus beauty for two consecutive years.

She just didn’t know how this girl had suddenly become Jing Ye’s sister. When she’d heard the news, she’d been stunned.

Maintaining her smile, she took the initiative to speak. "You must be Jing Ye’s sister? You’re really beautiful."

Sang Luoluo had recognized her the moment she heard her name.

Feng Wan’er from the Music College—one of the most prominent figures on campus, known for her beauty and talent, with countless admirers.

There were many forum posts about her, the most notable being her very public pursuit of Jing Ye, which had once caused a sensation across the entire campus.

Sang Luoluo gave a slight nod, her tone calm. "Hello."

Feng Wan’er’s gaze quickly returned to Jing Ye.

Since she’d entered, he hadn’t once looked up, busily peeling a shrimp with deliberate slowness.

His long fingers held the deep red shrimp shell, moving neither too fast nor too slow, even removing the vein with precision.

She leaned in slightly, her voice soft and intimate. "Jing Ye, are you free tonight? A new high-end Japanese restaurant just opened downtown. I was thinking of inviting you to try it."

"No."

Jing Ye placed the peeled shrimp into Sang Luoluo’s small plate.

Then, he pulled out a wet wipe, meticulously cleaning each finger from tip to web, his movements thorough.

Sang Luoluo stared at the extra shrimp in her plate, somewhat dazed.

She looked up.

The man across from her—even a simple act like wiping his hands—somehow exuded a forbidden allure.

The wet wipe folded and turned between his fingers before being crumpled into a small ball and set aside.

Feng Wan’er’s smile froze for a moment, a flicker of embarrassment flashing in her eyes before she quickly regained her composure. "Then another time. Enjoy your meal—I won’t disturb you."

She turned and left, the sound of her high heels clicking against the floor gradually fading as the door gently closed behind her.

The room was silent for a few seconds.

Sang Luoluo took a small bite of the shrimp—its texture was fresh, sweet, and firm.

Maybe because he had peeled it himself, it seemed even more delicious than usual.

From the corner of her eye, she saw that Jing Ye had already picked up his chopsticks and started eating his own food.

His expression was as usual, as if the previous scene had never happened.

chapters.title: He's Back
chapters.content:
Lu Zhi'an was the first to laugh, breaking the silence, his eyes behind the gold-rimmed glasses carrying a teasing glint.

"Haven't seen you in a year. The moment you return, Feng Wan'er catches wind and comes running. That 'stay away' aura of yours hasn't faded one bit—how come it's even more alluring now?"

Chen Ge swung his chopsticks, grinning as he chimed in, "That's what you don't get. Miss Feng has a thing for this exact vibe—cold and indifferent. The colder he is, the more she's into it. Classic case of always wanting what you can't have."

Lu Zhi'an chuckled, about to add more fuel to the fire.

*Tap.*

Jing Ye placed his chopsticks down on the edge of his plate with deliberate lightness.

"Can't even a meal shut you two up? Maybe I should move you to the table by the entrance. Join the guard dogs there—bark at each other, have a good time."

Chen Ge: "......"

Lu Zhi'an: "......"

How had this man’s words become even more lethal? Downright choking.

The girls, including Sang Luoluo, who had been quietly listening, all lowered their heads at once, stifling laughter until their cheeks burned, barely able to hold their chopsticks.

Chen Ge caught the girls' amused expressions and rubbed his nose, awkwardly joining Lu Zhi'an in silently eating, shoveling food into his mouth at a faster pace.

What if that guy over there spouted something even harsher? Did he want to keep any face at all?

Shen Juan added lazily, "You two are something else. In the time it takes to eat a meal, you’ve managed to attract girls to watch a free monkey show."

Chen Ge’s chest tightened further. He buried his head in his food. "Enough. Let’s just eat."

Jing Ye glanced across the table. The little girl had her head down, her lips subtly curved, the faint dimple at the corner of her cheek betraying the laughter she couldn’t quite hide.

It didn’t last long before Chen Ge, unable to restrain his nature, loudly started a new topic.

With Meng Lin playing along, the atmosphere at the table quickly livened up again. Others laughed and joined in, filling the private room with youthful chatter.

At the entire table, only Sang Luoluo and Jing Ye remained quietly, as if existing on a different frequency.

---

Meng Lin shut the dormitory door, tossed her bag onto a chair, and immediately spoke, "That Jing Ye—is he always this stingy with words? Throughout the whole meal, the things he said could be counted on one hand."

Tan Shuyin: "You like talkative people? I don’t. Too noisy."

Meng Lin: "Well, I *am* talkative, so of course I think it’s more fun to chat with someone who can keep up. But honestly, his presence is too strong. Even when he’s silent, you can’t ignore him."

Su Nan turned to Sang Luoluo, who had been unusually quiet. "Luoluo, you still owe us an explanation. Why didn’t you mention last night that you came back? And that you have this connection with Jing Ye."

Sang Luoluo, who had been climbing onto her bunk, paused. "I never thought I’d have any contact with him."

She had assumed that as long as she didn’t have any issues at school and didn’t seek him out, he would never take the initiative to find her. So she hadn’t brought it up.

His invitation to eat today had caught her completely off guard.

"Fine, I’ll let it slide this time." Su Nan yawned twice in succession, her eyes heavy with fatigue. "I’m so full I’m sleepy. I can still nap for ten minutes. Wake me up when it’s time."

She had stayed up too late last night chatting with her boyfriend, and now her eyelids were drooping, as if she could collapse at any moment.

"You can fall asleep in ten minutes?" Meng Lin laughed.

"I fall asleep fast, you know that." With that, Su Nan closed her eyes and was out in seconds, her steady breathing filling the room.

Sang Luoluo and the other two: "..."

When they had first moved in together, there was a time when they were all chatting, and one second Su Nan was still responding, the next they heard her light snores.

They had all stared at each other in disbelief—how could someone be talking one moment and asleep the next?

Later, they realized that Su Nan truly had a gift: she could sleep sitting, standing, propping her chin during class, or leaning against a railing while waiting for the subway. Whenever she wanted to sleep, she didn’t care about time or place—her instant-sleep skill activated on demand.

Over time, they had all grown used to it.

Still, every time they witnessed her "going offline" in an instant, they couldn’t help but sigh in their hearts: *What a talent.*

---

In the days that followed, Sang Luoluo didn’t run into Jing Ye again.

The day after their meal, he had sent a brief message saying he’d be out of town for a few days on business, and if there was an emergency, she could contact Chen Ge.

It wasn’t until today that she heard from others that he had been invited to the coastal city of F as a youth representative to attend the International Young Financial Leaders Forum.

His name was always tied to those exclusive, high-threshold events that even senior students struggled to access.

The news that she was Jing Ye’s sister had long since spread across Jing University. The looks she received now carried a subtle mix of curiosity and politeness.

She had just left the library, returning the books she had borrowed last time.

As she walked along the tree-shaded path, after turning two corners, her gaze was suddenly captured by a stark white figure at the edge of the ginkgo grove.

*He’s back.*

The man leaned against a thick, ancient ginkgo tree that would take two people to encircle, sitting on the ground.

One leg was casually bent, the other stretched out long. His head tilted to one side, pressed against the mottled bark, eyes closed, the fringe of his hair stirred by the breeze.

Even from a few steps away, she could see the faint bluish exhaustion under his eyelids, the weariness seeping into his brows.

This tranquility was abruptly shattered by a sharp, piercing shout nearby.

Sang Luoluo started, looking in the direction of the noise.

Not far away, near a newly erected campus bulletin board, a thin, small boy clutching old art supplies was surrounded by a group of student council members—upperclassmen, by the look of it.

Several drawings were scattered on the ground, marred by obvious footprints.

The leading student council officer, pointing at the boy, had spittle flying as he shouted, "How many times do I have to tell you? Non-designated exhibition areas are strictly off-limits for posting personal work! What’s with these tacky drawings, all colorful and plastered on the bulletin board? It ruins the campus image! Clean it up *now*!"

The boy tried to bend down to pick up the drawings, stubborn. "These are public welfare posters advocating for the adoption of stray animals. The content is positive—how is this a problem?"

"Less nonsense with me! Rules are rules!" The leader cut him off impatiently, reaching out to grab the boy’s collar. "Can’t you understand plain words? *Now.* Clean it up and get out of here! Or I’m reporting you for a disciplinary violation!"

Just as that hand was about to touch the boy’s collar—

"Take your hand back."

Jing Ye had opened his eyes beneath the ginkgo tree.

With a slight push against the tree, he stood up, tall and poised.

He raised a hand to rub the back of his neck, where the bark had pressed into his skin, the movement carrying the laziness of someone just woken up.

He lifted his cold, pale eyelids, scanning the name tags on the student council members’ chests before settling on the leader’s face.

"Those posters? I drew them. Any objections?" His voice was light, laced with the irritation of being woken up.

These past few days in F City, the originally booked hotel had been overcrowded due to the forum, forcing him to share a room with another attendee.

Unfortunately, his roommate snored like thunder. He hadn’t had a full night’s sleep in days.

He had just returned, found this scenic spot, and decided to lean against the tree for a quick nap—only to have this commotion disrupt his peace.

The thin boy clutching the art supplies looked up in shock, his lips parting but no sound coming out.

Sang Luoluo had seen those posters before. The delicate, gentle brushstrokes depicted small animals curled up in various corners, their eyes glistening, accompanied by the words *Give them a home*. They were unmistakably the style of the boy on the ground.

Jing Ye was stepping in to help him.

---

chapters.title: She’s the Only One He Has Eyes For
chapters.content:
The leader’s face flushed red, his words stuttering, his earlier arrogance vanishing. "J-Jing... Young Master Jing, this violates the rules. We were just following procedure..."

Jing Ye ignored his stammering explanation. He strolled over to the thin boy.

Bending down, he picked up the most damaged drawing with his clean, long fingers.

The small cat’s eye was half-covered by a footprint, the once-vivid image now a mess.

His fingertip brushed over the gray-black stain, but instead of removing it, the smear only made the dirty mark stand out more against the fine paper.

He lifted his eyelids, his cold, sinking gaze sweeping over the uneasy faces.

"The regulations say to maintain campus cleanliness and promote positive values. Not to use your shoe soles as stamps to trample on others’ hard work."

"You should be picking up the drawings one by one, organizing them properly, and apologizing."

He paused briefly before adding the final three words:

"—Then, get lost."

The group didn’t dare say another word. They hastily crouched down, scrambling to gather the scattered drawings and shove them back into the boy’s arms. They squeezed out a muffled "Sorry" before fleeing the scene as if their tails were on fire, disappearing in an instant at the end of the tree-lined path.

Jing Ye returned the drawing to the boy, then raised his hand again, rubbing the back of his neck with a hint of weariness. His face was expressionless, as if his interest had been drained by the disturbance.

Sang Luoluo suddenly came to her senses—she had been standing there the whole time, watching the entire scene unfold.

She hurried to turn around, intending to leave quickly before he noticed her.

Before she could take two steps, the back of her collar was gently tugged from behind.

She stumbled slightly but, not giving up, tried to keep moving forward.

The collar was firmly pulled back again, like a cat whose scruff had been grabbed.

Jing Ye’s voice came from above her, half-amused: "Finished watching the show and now you want to run? My performance fee isn’t cheap."

Sang Luoluo froze, took a deep breath to steady herself, and turned around with a practiced smile already on her face.

Jing Ye released his grip. "See me and run—what’s that about?"

"Not at all, you misunderstood." Sang Luoluo adjusted her collar, then pointed in the distance, her tone a little guilty. "I was just about to go back to the dorm. That direction is the girls’ dormitory."

Jing Ye, half-lowering his eyelids as he looked at her, said, "It’s on the way. I’ll walk you back."

Sang Luoluo: "......"

When she didn’t move, he took the first step.

She had no choice but to follow, maintaining a precise two-step distance between them.

The path stretched forward in the twilight.

The shadows of sycamore leaves filtered through the branches, swaying delicately on the bluestone path like underwater seaweed.

As she watched, it struck her as strangely familiar.

It reminded her of the road from No. 2 Middle School to No. 1 Middle School.

After the basketball game, for some inexplicable reason, she had taken the long way home, passing by No. 1 Middle School’s side gate.

Later, it became a habit.

Every day after school, she would walk an extra stretch along that road, pretending to casually scan the crowd in different uniforms.

Even though she knew the chances were slim, she couldn’t help but search through the moving heads for that tall figure.

When she found him, her heart would skip a beat. When she didn’t, she would silently walk the rest of the way.

The way her heart raced back then felt no different from now.

Both times, it was suspended in midair, never quite landing.

Jing Ye noticed she was still absentmindedly walking ahead, her direction clearly veering off course.

His gaze shifted slightly. With a long stride, he stepped in front of her and raised his hand.

Sure enough, her lowered head, lost in thought, collided solidly with his chest.

As if anticipating it, his hand had already wrapped around her waist—startlingly slender, soft to the touch.

"I’m sorry, I’m sorry, I was distracted." Sang Luoluo snapped back to reality, hastily stepping back, her cheeks flushing red.

Jing Ye withdrew his hand into his pocket, his fingertips still lingering with the curve of her waist. He raised an eyebrow. "What were you thinking about? Not even watching where you’re going."

"Just... homework." Sang Luoluo made up an excuse.

"Let’s go." Jing Ye slowed his pace, walking beside her.

By the time they reached the dormitory building, the twilight had deepened. A few girls had gathered in twos and threes at the entrance.

Some carried books, others chatted arm in arm, their gazes all unconsciously drawn to the tall figure.

Sang Luoluo spoke softly, "Thank you."

"Tomorrow’s Saturday," Jing Ye’s voice was a shade deeper than the evening breeze. "My mom wants you to come over for dinner. Nine in the morning. I’ll wait for you at the school gate."

She hesitated. An invitation from an elder wasn’t easy to refuse. In the end, she simply nodded.

"Don’t bring anything. She’ll be upset. Just come as you are."

"Okay. Then I’ll go up now."

"Mm. Go on."

Sang Luoluo finally turned to head upstairs.

Jing Ye only left after her figure disappeared from sight.

---

As soon as Sang Luoluo returned, Meng Lin leapt to the center of the dormitory, unable to contain her excitement, clapping her hands.

"Quiet! Sisters, I have big news to announce!"

Tan Shuyin, from the upper bunk, asked, "What’s with all the shouting? You scared me."

Sang Luoluo set down her bag and, along with the others, turned to Meng Lin.

Meng Lin cleared her throat, her eyes sparkling as if they held stars. "I announce—I! Am! No! Longer! Single!"

Sang Luoluo had already guessed as much. She smiled, her eyes curving. "Congratulations."

Tan Shuyin raised an eyebrow. "Now you can tell us, right? Who’s the hero who finally won you over?"

"It’s a senior from the Computer Science department, third year." Meng Lin pressed her lips together, her ears slightly red. "We just made it official this afternoon. Once things are more stable, I’ll bring him out for you all to meet."

Su Nan: "We *have* to have a celebration meal! We’ll pick the place, we’ll order the food. No objections?"

"No problem!" Meng Lin agreed immediately, then swung her head smugly. "Ah, now only you two are single dogs. Better hurry up!"

Sang Luoluo and Tan Shuyin exchanged a glance, both falling silent: "..."

"You just got into a relationship," Sang Luoluo said helplessly, smiling, "and you’re already lording it over us?"

Meng Lin lifted her chin. "Of course! If not now, then when?"

Su Nan began pressing for details, and Sang Luoluo and Tan Shuyin pricked up their ears.

The dormitory instantly became lively.

---

That night, in the boys’ dormitory, the sounds of game effects and keyboard clicks filled the air.

After finishing a match, Chen Ge took off his headphones and turned to Jing Ye, who had just finished showering and was drying his hair.

"How was the forum? Meet anyone interesting? Like a beautiful and talented colleague?"

"No."

Chen Ge clicked his tongue. "Your standards are *way* too high. I really wonder who’ll ever catch your eye."

Jing Ye’s hand, rubbing his hair, imperceptibly paused. An image of Sang Luoluo flashed in his mind.

His standards *were* high.

Which was why she was the only one he had eyes for.

He walked to his desk, casually draping the towel over the back of the chair.

Tipping his head back to look at the ceiling, the light was a little blinding.

The thought of her heart belonging to someone else sent an unfamiliar pang of jealousy surging through him, fierce and sharp, stabbing at his chest.

He unconsciously furrowed his brows.

This was the first time in his life he’d tasted such a bitter feeling.

After a long while, he picked up his phone and typed: 【Watching a show comes with a fee. Say something nice to settle the debt.】

Sang Luoluo saw the message and replied immediately: 【Brother, you’re very kind.】

His appearance was cold, his brows and eyes like frost.

But today, when he had wiped the dirt off the drawing, his fingertips had been so gentle.

Jing Ye’s expression softened slightly, his mood improving greatly: 【When are you going to bed?】

Sang Luoluo: 【Right now.】

Jing Ye glanced at the time—just past ten.

Even her sleep schedule was punctual. She really was a well-behaved girl through and through.

Jing Ye: 【Go to sleep.】

Sang Luoluo: 【Mm.】

Jing Ye: 【Good night. Sweet dreams.】

Sang Luoluo: 【Good night. Sweet dreams to you too.】

That night, both of them had a good dream—one about an inescapable, life-and-death entanglement.

chapters.title: Washing Pants Early in the Morning
chapters.content:
In her dream, the light was dim and blurred.

Two figures were tangled fiercely in the messy bedding, as if he wanted to embed her into his very bones.

Those almond-shaped eyes, always glistening with moisture, were now completely unfocused due to his forceful intrusion, veiled with a physiological mist and an unmaskable flush of arousal.

The dark desire in the young man’s eyes surged once more.

He ground harshly against her slightly swollen lips, prying open her teeth, and ruthlessly plundered the last remnants of her breath and sanity.

The hand gripping her waist was shockingly forceful, branding her with scorching control.

His heavy panting mixed with her fragmented moans, forming the most potent aphrodisiac, like tossing a torch into a sea of oil, instantly igniting all his suppressed malice and possessiveness.

His thin lips brushed against her ear as his voice rasped dangerously low:

"Look at me and say, who am I?"

"Get it wrong, and you won’t sleep tonight."

She squeezed out two words in broken gasps:

"Jing... Ye..."

...

"Luoluo? Luoluo! Are you dreaming?"

Her arm was gently shaken, and Sang Luoluo opened her eyes, her chest heaving violently.

Meng Lin was crouched by the bed, watching her with concern. The sunlight streaming through the window stung her eyes, leaving her disoriented.

"What kind of dream did you have? You kept saying 'Jing Ye' over and over, so soft and trembling, like your mouth was full of water, or like you were begging for mercy."

Sang Luoluo instantly sobered up, unable to meet Meng Lin’s probing gaze. Acting on instinct, she grabbed the safest excuse in her panic: "He scared me with his Tibetan mastiff. I was afraid."

Meng Lin let out an "oh" and teased, "I thought you had a *springtime* dream!"

Sang Luoluo forced herself to stay calm, shaking her head in denial: "No, you’re overthinking it."

Tan Shuyin, who was on the opposite bunk, had been watching Sang Luoluo the whole time. "It’s not just her. We all think so. The way you sounded just now..."

She paused slightly, as if choosing her words carefully.

"Ai, and here we call you *sister*—what’s there to be shy about?" Su Nan finished, then turned back to Sang Luoluo: "The way you sounded... like you were begging a man who’d been rough with you."

Sang Luoluo’s lashes trembled. She *had* been treated roughly.

In her dream, she was like a paper doll, folded and pressed this way and that.

Further proof that his bed manners were terrible.

A person’s true nature in reality carried over into their dreams.

"It was the dog. It was too fierce—I was just scared."

"Alright, alright, we won’t tease you anymore!" Meng Lin quickly climbed down the ladder, then reminded her, "Didn’t you say you had something important today? Hurry up and get ready, or you’ll be late."

At those words, Sang Luoluo instinctively turned to the digital clock on the bedside table—08:30.

She had half an hour left. She immediately threw off the blankets and got out of bed.

---

The boys’ dormitory was in a deep, quiet slumber. Everyone was buried under their blankets, lost in sleep, unaware of the continuous sound of running water coming from the bathroom.

Jing Ye stood in front of the sink, scrubbing a pair of dirty pants.

After washing them clean, he braced his hands on the edge of the sink, staring at his reflection in the mirror. A trace of languid satisfaction still lingered in his eyes.

Tsk.

He’d been thinking about *her* again.

He closed his eyes briefly, then turned and twisted the faucet open again, splashing a handful of cold water on his face.

Only after barely suppressing that restless heat did he pick up the washed pants and walk to the balcony, spreading them out on the drying rack.

The slight noise of the rack being adjusted woke Chen Ge. He frowned as he opened his eyes, and his gaze happened to land on the dark pants being hoisted up.

He snapped fully awake, all sleepiness gone.

"Yo—"

He drew out the syllable, leaning over the edge of his bed with a mischievous grin.

"Our Brother Ye has finally developed some worldly desires, huh? Washing pants first thing in the morning?"

Jing Ye pressed the upward button, watching the rack rise before turning back into the room. "Forgot to take them off before showering. They got wet."

Lu Zhi’an and Shen Juan also woke up one after another. Seeing the pants, their eyes filled with amused curiosity.

Chen Ge wasn’t buying it. He smirked, "You? Forgot to take off your pants *before showering*? Since when do you, Jing Ye, make such a rookie mistake?"

He wiggled his eyebrows. "Come on, bro, no need to pretend. It’s normal for a man to take care of himself. What’s the big deal?"

Lu Zhi’an put on his glasses, teasing, "If you’ve got the itch, just get a girlfriend. Keeping it all bottled up like this isn’t healthy in the long run."

Jing Ye’s gaze swept over the three mocking faces one by one.

First, he looked at Chen Ge. "One, who’s peed the bed so many times it could fill a gallery."

Then, his gaze shifted to Lu Zhi’an. "One, who looks refined but has nothing but depravity in his mind."

Finally, he landed on Shen Juan. "And one, who acts like he’s above it all, but secretly practices his *skills* all the time."

He pulled his gaze back, took out a paper towel, and wiped his hands.

"Three men who can’t even sort out their own pants," he said, tossing the towel before picking up his phone and car keys, "and yet you have the time to meddle in my business."

The door slammed shut.

Chen Ge: "..."Lu Zhi’an: "..."Shen Juan: "...How did he know I didn’t sleep last night?"

Chen Ge & Lu Zhi’an: "?"

---

Sang Luoluo had just reached the school gate when someone called out to her. She turned toward the voice.

A young man holding a large, eye-catching bouquet of red roses was striding toward her.

It was the same guy who had pursued her multiple times, each rejection seemingly falling on deaf ears.

Sang Luoluo’s delicate brows immediately furrowed.

The man had originally planned to wait for her outside her dormitory but had unexpectedly run into her at the school gate.

He glanced around. It was breakfast time, and the area was bustling with students coming and going from the cafeteria, many carrying soy milk and steamed buns.

The crowd was perfect.

He quickly adjusted his expression, putting on what he believed was his most heartfelt look as he approached, raising his voice:

"Sang Luoluo! Be my girlfriend! You won’t have to study so hard anymore—I’ll take care of you!"

Sang Luoluo’s face turned cold. "I’ve rejected you many times. Please stop this."

The man acted as if he hadn’t heard her, thrusting the bouquet in front of her.

Sang Luoluo took a few steps back, her eyes growing even more distant.

"Sang Luoluo! I really like you. You’re so beautiful—you deserve a man like me!"

"Look, I’m confessing to you in front of all these people. Give me some face and say yes, or how will I save mine?"

The crowd of onlookers grew larger, and the man’s heart swelled with triumph. He felt victory was within his grasp.

His previous confessions had been in secluded corners, each time met with her gentle but firm rejections.

This time, he had wised up and chosen the busiest time of the morning, when the most people would be around.

He had even coordinated with his roommates, who were waiting outside her dormitory with a megaphone to amplify the moment.

But plans never survive first contact with reality—he had run into her right at the school gate.

Still, there were enough people here.

He was certain that a girl like her, with such a thin skin, wouldn’t be able to handle the public pressure. If she showed even the slightest hesitation or panic, he could use the growing encouragement from the crowd to corner her into a vague, reluctant acceptance.

From his perspective, the situation was practically a sure win.

The crowd erupted into whistles and laughter.

"Sang Luoluo, he’s going all out for you—give the guy a chance!"

"Yeah, how romantic! Just say yes already!"

"Those flowers must’ve cost a fortune. Don’t be so cold!"

"..."

The crowd formed a semicircle, their eager gazes fixed on her. Neck craned, they waited breathlessly for the happy ending, not a single one of them caring whether the girl at the center of it all was willing or not.

Sang Luoluo stood in place, the hem of her skirt lifting slightly in the breeze.

Her eyes were icy as she spoke, her voice like shattering ice: "Don’t you dare—"

—use this to kidnap me. She hadn’t even finished her sentence before she was interrupted.

---

chapters.title: Let Him Unfold and Fold Her
chapters.content:
"Come here."

Everyone turned their heads at the voice.

Jing Ye had appeared at some point, a double portion of breakfast in his hands.

His presence silenced the once-noisy crowd.

Without hesitation, Sang Luoluo lifted her foot and walked toward him.

As she neared, Jing Ye reached out and grabbed her wrist.

His gaze locked onto the man holding the flowers, his voice frigid: "What makes you think you’re worthy of her?"

Sang Luoluo lowered her head, feeling the heat of his palm through her wrist.

That warmth traveled along her pulse, all the way to her heart, dispelling much of the embarrassment and discomfort from being the center of attention.

The man’s eyes fell on their clasped wrists, his mind racing.

Jing Ye was protecting her so fiercely—at the very least, it meant he truly saw her as family, like a little sister.

If he could get close to her, even if it was just a tenuous connection to the Jing family, it would be an immeasurable opportunity for him and his entire family.

He toned down his attitude slightly. "Young Master Jing, my conditions are decent in every aspect. I’m more than good enough for Sang Luoluo."

Jing Ye let out a soft, derisive chuckle, the mockery in his voice unmistakable.

He examined the man from head to toe with a slow, evaluating gaze.

"What gives you that confidence? Is it because of this bouquet you bought from a roadside stand? Or is it because of this pathetic, pressure-filled public stunt?"

"From your taste to your methods, from head to toe, you don’t even qualify as mediocre. How dare you think you’re *good enough*?"

The man’s face flushed red and pale in turn, his fingers whitening from gripping the bouquet too tightly.

He was, after all, a wealthy young master—when had he ever been publicly humiliated like this?

Intimidated by Jing Ye’s status, he didn’t dare utter a single word in retort. He could only bite down hard, swallowing his humiliation and embarrassment.

The once-rowdy crowd now stood in stunned silence, as if their throats had been squeezed shut. Even their breathing had grown lighter.

Jing Ye’s lips twitched, his eyes devoid of any warmth. "Reach too far, and you might lose a hand."

The man’s face turned ashen in an instant. The flowers slipped from his grasp, scattering across the ground. His hands instinctively hid behind his back, as if truly afraid the word "lose" would manifest upon his own body.

Jing Ye’s eyes flickered with contempt. He pulled her into the car, and soon, the vehicle drove away under the watchful eyes of the crowd.

He kept his gaze forward, his fingers tapping lightly on the steering wheel. "I bought breakfast. See if there’s anything you like. I’ll find a place to park, and we can eat before driving again."

"Okay." Sang Luoluo reached for the paper bag on the back seat.

Inside were: a plate of pre-mixed Wuhan hot dry noodles, a steaming box of soup dumplings, a vegetable and chicken roll, and a warm cup of soy milk.

The variety was impressive—clearly not a random purchase.

Sang Luoluo picked up the hot dry noodles, surprised. "You like eating hot dry noodles?"

It didn’t seem to fit his usual image.

"I saw a lot of girls lining up for it when I was buying," he said, signaling a turn and steering the car toward a quiet temporary parking spot on the side of the road. "I was afraid you’d like it, so I got some."

The car came to a stop.

He unbuckled his seatbelt, turned to face her, and looked at the hot dry noodles in her hand. "Want to try some?"

"Yes, I really like it. This place has good flavor." Sang Luoluo ate it often.

Jing Ye lifted the lid off the soup dumplings for her and handed her a pair of disposable chopsticks he had already separated.

Then he picked up the cup of soy milk, inserted a straw, and placed it in the circular cup holder on the central console.

"Be careful, it’s hot." he said.

"Mmm." Sang Luoluo picked up a chopstick-full of the fragrant hot dry noodles, taking a small bite. The rich aroma of sesame paste melted in her mouth.

Jing Ye opened his own box of soup dumplings and picked one up with his chopsticks.

Just before bringing it to his mouth, he asked casually, "Seems like a lot of people are after you? I heard even Xiao Sinian from the Economics Department pursued you."

Sang Luoluo was in the middle of chewing, her cheeks puffed out. She shot him a sidelong glance.

After swallowing her food and taking a sip of soy milk to wash it down, she replied slowly, "Not as many as you."

Jing Ye put the soup dumpling in his mouth, chewing and swallowing deliberately before his gaze settled out the window.

"Can’t compare to your grand gestures—flowers, public confessions, the whole spectacle. Quite lively."

Sang Luoluo’s chopsticks paused mid-air.

—That sounded... a little sour?

The thought was quickly swept away by the rich aroma of the hot dry noodles. Right now, she didn’t want to talk. She just wanted to focus on the delicious bowl of noodles in front of her.

Jing Ye: "..."

She ate with such single-minded focus, her cheeks puffing in and out, that the subtle emotion in his eyes gradually faded, replaced by something softer.

After finishing the noodles, Sang Luoluo contentedly cleaned up.

Jing Ye handed her the untouched vegetable and chicken roll. "Eat this too."

"I can’t," Sang Luoluo quickly pushed it back, rubbing her stomach. "A bowl of noodles and half a cup of soy milk already filled me up."

Jing Ye glanced at her slightly rounded belly and didn’t insist, picking up his chopsticks to eat it himself.

As he chewed, his Adam’s apple moved slightly. Sang Luoluo’s gaze, against her will, was drawn to that subtle motion.

On the way here, she had already pressed down the memory of that dream countless times.

But now, as soon as her eyes landed on his throat...

The wet, sticky details from last night’s dream came rushing back without warning.

His Adam’s apple, strained and rolling with effort.

The taut lines of his shoulders, tense to the extreme.

The sweat beads gathering and rolling down his sharp jaw.

And that deep, sensual voice that made her spine tingle, the heavy panting that sent electric shocks through her entire body.

This man in bed...

Was worse than Daji, the fox spirit who brought down dynasties.

He had her so bewitched, her entire body soft as cotton, letting him unfold and fold her as he pleased.

"What are you looking at?" Jing Ye’s voice interrupted her wandering, lustful thoughts.

Sang Luoluo’s gaze flickered away. She grabbed the soy milk cup, pretending to drink, her voice muffled against the rim. "Nothing."

Jing Ye gave her a long look before dropping the subject.

He gathered the empty food containers and plastic bags, carefully tidying them up before restarting the car.

He casually turned on the car stereo. A soothing piano melody flowed through the cabin like water, the volume set just low enough to avoid noise without making the silence oppressive.

Sang Luoluo leaned back against the seat, quietly watching the scenery outside, trying to clear her mind of those seductive images.

The car wove through the bustling streets, gradually heading toward a quieter part of the city.

The scenery outside began to change: the noisy commercial district faded away, replaced by dense French plane trees interlacing into canopies. Low, gray-brick walls peeked through the shifting shadows of the leaves.

Eventually, the car glided into a gated villa community with strict security. There were no flashy signs, only uniformed guards silently saluting as they passed.

The villas were spaced generously, each surrounded by expansive gardens.

The architectural styles varied, but they all shared the same quiet dominance, as if looking down upon the world.

This place had long surpassed the concept of "expensive."

Money was merely the entry fee here.

What truly allowed someone to stay was the intricate web of connections beneath the surface, the power to stir winds and clouds, and most importantly, the kind of existence that, after generations of sedimentation, was as unshakable as a mountain—and in itself, the rule.

chapters.title: Sang Luoluo, You Are My Future Daughter-in-Law
chapters.content:
The car came to a silent stop in front of one of the villas with a distinct new Chinese-style architecture.

Sang Luoluo pushed the door open and stepped out, gazing at the grand courtyard house. Once again, she saw the difference between them.

This villa alone was worth over a billion yuan.

Tang Suqin had already hurried out to greet her.

Today, she wore a pearl-white Xiangyun gauze qipao, with a jade button at the collar, glowing with a warm, translucent green. Her movements were light and graceful, her eyes and brows filled with smiles.

"Luoluo." Tang Suqin took her hand, her smile gentle.

"Aunt Tang." Sang Luoluo obediently called out, letting her hold her hand.

"Come, let's go inside. It's too sunny out here." Tang Suqin affectionately patted the back of her hand, completely forgetting the man standing behind her. She led Sang Luoluo inside without hesitation.

Jing Ye lagged a couple of steps behind, his eyes sweeping over the two intimate figures ahead, like mother and daughter.

His mother had always wanted a daughter.

On the day he was born, Tang Suqin, dazed from the pain in the delivery room, had woken up and repeatedly asked the doctor, pulling at him, "Are you sure you didn't mix up the babies? I clearly dreamed of a lovely little girl..."

Fine.

There was no daughter.

But Sang Luoluo—she would be his future daughter-in-law.

Same thing.

---

Inside, there was a carefully calculated coolness.

The walls were a warm beige, the furniture lines simple and smooth, with no intricate carvings, yet exorbitantly expensive.

In the seat of honor sat a middle-aged man. He wore a dark gray ramie Chinese-style shirt, the sleeves rolled up once, revealing a string of dark beads on his wrist whose material was indistinguishable.

His face was warm and gentle, his gaze calm.

Jing Ye's outstanding brows and bone structure clearly took after his father.

Sang Luoluo greeted politely, "Hello, Uncle."

"Welcome to our home. Make yourself at home."

Tang Suqin had already pulled Sang Luoluo onto the long sofa.

"Dad."

Jing Ye sat on the single sofa diagonally across from them.

The sofa was dark gray velvet. As he sank into it, his long legs bent casually, his left elbow resting on the armrest. The lines of his forearm bulged slightly from the relaxed position, and the bones of his wrist formed a clean arc.

When the servant brought the tea tray, their footsteps were as light as a cat’s, almost inaudible.

The white porcelain lidded bowls were so thin they were translucent. The tea was a clear amber color, with a faint tea fragrance wafting through the rising steam.

Sang Luoluo took the cup with both hands, her fingertips touching the perfectly warm surface.

It wasn't too hot, nor would it cool too quickly.

Tang Suqin said, "Luoluo, your mother said you love sweet and sour pork the most. Today, Auntie cooked it herself. You must try it."

Sang Luoluo replied, "Thank you, Aunt Tang. You didn’t have to go through so much trouble for me."

"It’s no trouble," Tang Suqin said with a smile in her eyes. "After dancing for half my life, my greatest joy now is cooking."

"As long as you don’t mix up the sugar and salt jars like last time." Jing Ye lazily chimed in from the side without even lifting his eyelids.

"You!" Tang Suqin laughed in mock anger, pretending to swat at him. "Can’t you save some face for your mother in front of Luoluo?"

Sang Luoluo smiled slightly, pressing her lips together. Jing Ye seemed more talkative at home, even saying a few more words than usual.

Jing Shouren pushed a black card to the edge of the tea table. "Luoluo, this is a small gift from your uncle. Take it."

Sang Luoluo was startled and quickly waved her hands. "Uncle, no, thank you."

Tang Suqin reached out, took the card, and directly placed it in her palm. "Child, don’t refuse your uncle’s gift. Take it. Buy more pretty dresses in the future."

Sang Luoluo’s fingers stiffened slightly, holding the card awkwardly.

"I’ve known your mother for a long time. No need to be polite." Jing Shouren said with a kind smile.

"Dad, she thinks it’s too little." Jing Ye said slowly.

"No, Uncle, I didn’t mean that." Sang Luoluo hurried to explain, her ears slightly burning.

"Then take it." Jing Ye looked at her flustered appearance, the corner of his lips curling into a faint, almost smile.

Sang Luoluo had no choice but to tighten her grip on the card and softly said, "Thank you, Uncle."

"Luoluo, your room is ready. It’s right next to Xiao Ye’s, facing south with great lighting." Tang Suqin said, then looked at Jing Ye. "Xiao Ye, take Luoluo upstairs to see it, then show her around the garden. I’ll go prepare lunch."

Jing Ye stood up and said briefly, "Follow me."

Sang Luoluo quickly followed.

The second-floor hallway was quiet and bright.

He pushed open one of the doors and stepped aside.

Sang Luoluo stepped inside.

Sunlight filtered through the light goose-yellow curtains, casting warm patches on the floor.

The bedding was the same light goose-yellow, with tiny, almost invisible jasmine patterns embroidered on the pillows.

A desk was placed by the window, with a new laptop on it. In the corner, there was a comfortable single sofa and a small side table.

Sang Luoluo looked around the overly perfect space, a warm, indescribable feeling welling up in her heart.

She hadn’t expected to stay overnight, let alone that they would prepare a room so thoughtfully.

"Let me know if you need anything." Jing Ye didn’t come in, just leaned against the doorway.

"This is already perfect. I have everything I need." She turned around and smiled at him, her eyes curving.

Last night, when she had called her mother, Ye Rong had laughed on the other end of the phone:

"Your Aunt Tang really cares about you. Treat it like your own home, don’t hold back. We were as close as sisters when we were young."

"Mom will prepare the gift. You don’t know what she likes, so leave it to me."

"Come, I’ll take you to the garden." He said.

Sang Luoluo followed him downstairs. As they passed the open kitchen, she unconsciously slowed her steps.

She saw Jing Shouren standing beside Tang Suqin, slightly leaning toward her. He held a small bowl, patiently catching the blanched greens that Tang Suqin scooped from the pot.

Tang Suqin moved while softly saying something, and Jing Shouren leaned in to listen carefully, nodding occasionally, a gentle smile on his lips.

When Tang Suqin reached for a distant seasoning bottle, Jing Shouren had already stretched out his hand to take it and pass it to her first. Their tacit understanding was as if they were one person.

Sang Luoluo felt a pang in her heart.

She had once had parents who were this affectionate.

Jing Ye noticed the fleeting darkness in her gaze and his expression deepened.

He had asked Tang Suqin before. Her parents had divorced when she was in the first year of junior high.

It started with her father’s affair. The scandal had been quite ugly, dealing a significant blow to her and her mother.

Tang Suqin had also said that Sang Luoluo used to be very lively as a child, always smiling and making noise.

After her parents’ divorce, her personality gradually changed. She became unusually quiet, more obedient and sensible, hiding all her emotions deep inside.

Jing Ye soothingly squeezed her wrist and led her to continue toward the garden.

The garden was spacious, and in a few steps, they entered a flower garden.

The hibiscus was in full bloom, the leaves of the jasmine plant were lush and green. Clusters of hydrangeas crowded together—blue, purple, pink—forming one soft, dreamy blur after another. The wind blew, and the entire garden seemed to sway with tenderness.

Further ahead was a meticulously maintained water feature.

A shallow pool reflected the sky and clouds. A few green stones were scattered along the shore, and the water’s surface mirrored the trees and flowers. Occasionally, a dragonfly would skim the water, sending out ripple after ripple.

---

chapters.title: He Kissed Her Through His Thumb
chapters.content:
