Sang Luoluo stood by the water, where several koi fish swam slowly, breaking the reflections on the surface.

Jing Ye stood beside her, his gaze also on the water, his voice a few notes deeper than usual.

"The water may be muddy for a while, but the fish still swim. Flowers may wither this year, but their roots remain in the soil, ready to bloom again next year."

"Life moves forward; it’s not meant to be ruminated over. Look at this garden—when the season comes, every flower that should bloom will."

He turned his head, fixing his gaze on her profile.

"Some people, some things—once they’re in the past, they’re just old signposts. They can’t direct your future path. What matters is that you and Aunt Ye are living so well now. That’s more important than anything."

"You have a long road ahead. The best scenery is still waiting for you."

Sang Luoluo turned her head to look at him.

Their eyes met, and in each other’s clear pupils, they saw their own reflections.

She was surprised that he could comfort her like this.

He was a man of few words, and it was rare for him to show such a delicate side.

The darkness in her eyes was quietly dispelled by this unexpected warmth. She curved her eyes and smiled sincerely. "I know. Thank you, Jing Ye."

The sunlight fell on her smiling eyes and brows, and into the depths of his dark gaze.

He casually bent down in front of her, aligning his gaze with hers.

The distance suddenly closed. She could see his distinct lashes and the tiny reflection of herself in his eyes.

"Why don’t you call me ‘Brother’ anymore?"

This was the first time he had heard her call him by his name.

The two syllables rolled off her lips softly, the tail of the word "Ye" short and sweet.

It sounded... nice.

Sang Luoluo tilted her neck and flashed him a playful smile, deliberately drawing out the word: "Broooother~"

Jing Ye’s almond-shaped eyes narrowed slightly, and his Adam’s apple rolled uncontrollably.

Too coquettish.

Just like last night... when she had whimpered in his arms.

Beyond the carved railing, Feng Wan’er had heard that Jing Ye was back and had come to find him.

She frowned, looking at the two figures in the distance.

Jing Ye never stood this close to any girl. He was always stingy with his attention, never letting his gaze linger on anyone for more than two seconds.

She had looked into it before. This Sang Luoluo was only receiving some favor because their mothers knew each other.

She had thought that, given Jing Ye’s personality, he would at most go through the motions out of respect for his elders. He would never truly care about someone like her.

But now, he was bending his tall, straight back for her, matching her height.

He was looking at her face with such focused attention, with something she had never seen in him before—something that could be called tenderness.

What exactly did he take Sang Luoluo for?

This thought made her inexplicably flustered.

She suppressed the panic in her heart, steadied herself, and called out calmly, "Jing Ye."

Inside the carved railing, Sang Luoluo and Jing Ye both turned to look.

When she saw it was Feng Wan’er, Sang Luoluo was slightly taken aback.

The fact that she could appear here meant she was more than just a schoolmate to the Jing family—they were old acquaintances.

Feng Wan’er pressed her lips together. "Jing Ye, I need to talk to you."

Jing Ye straightened up, putting his hands back into his pockets. His back was ramrod straight, and the tenderness around him vanished instantly. He had no intention of inviting her in. "What is it?"

"Can’t you let me in?" Feng Wan’er’s voice carried a hint of displeasure at being ignored. "Let’s talk in private."

"No." Jing Ye refused bluntly, his reason even more straightforward and harsh. "I’m afraid you’ll harass me."

Sang Luoluo’s lips twitched almost imperceptibly.

Feng Wan’er’s expression turned ugly. "Jing Ye, you know I really like you. I’ve chased you for so long. Can’t you just say yes to me once?"

Sang Luoluo was shocked. Did Feng Wan’er mean that Jing Ye didn’t have a girlfriend at all?

The next second, his arm suddenly wrapped around her shoulders.

Her body was forced against his chest. The faint mint scent around him filled her nose, and his deep voice sounded in her ear: "Play along."

Then, he looked up at Feng Wan’er. "I have a girlfriend now. I can’t say yes to you."

Feng Wan’er’s gaze locked onto his arm around Sang Luoluo, her nails almost digging into the soft flesh of her palm.

He actually... had feelings for Sang Luoluo?

Sang Luoluo, a girl from an ordinary family—how could she possibly—

How could she possibly deserve to be in their sight?

To their circle, who had grown up surrounded by fame and fortune, accustomed to judging people by their family background, Sang Luoluo was so ordinary she was almost invisible. She wasn’t even interesting enough to be gossip.

And Jing Ye—he was supposed to be the untouchable peak of their golden circle, the one who should naturally uphold these rules.

The top-tier resources he had seen, the world he had access to—it was something Sang Luoluo couldn’t even imagine.

How could he... lower himself to set his sights on such an uneventful, ordinary scene?

Jing Ye lowered his gaze to the person in his arms, who was clearly still confused.

They were extremely close, close enough to see the fine, soft fuzz on her face.

She had a very faint scent, not like any artificial fragrance. It was a natural sweetness that seemed to come from her skin, sweet but not cloying.

His gaze slid down from her small, delicate nose to her lips, which were slightly parted in surprise.

Soft in color, perfectly shaped.

"She doesn’t believe us. Let’s prove it to her."

"How do we prove it?" Sang Luoluo subconsciously murmured. They were just pretending.

As she spoke, Jing Ye’s arm around her shoulder didn’t loosen. His other hand gripped her waist, pulling her more securely in front of him.

Then, he lowered his head.

Just as their lips were about to touch, a warm hand cupped her cheek first, his thumb pressing against her soft lips.

His kiss landed through his thumb.

Sang Luoluo froze completely, her eyes widening as she stared at his magnified lashes and the light in his eyes.

From Feng Wan’er’s perspective, this was undoubtedly a real kiss.

She gripped the carved railing, her nails scraping against the stone, producing a light, grating sound.

Inside the railing, Jing Ye and the girl in his arms stared at each other.

The corner of his eye twitched, and a hint of roguishness mixed with a possessiveness that Sang Luoluo couldn’t detect.

Sang Luoluo felt her cheeks burning under his gaze. She nervously pressed her lips together.

With this movement, her lips brushed against his thumb.

To an onlooker, it looked like she was actively responding, even deepening the kiss.

Feng Wan’er didn’t throw a tantrum. She turned around and left gracefully.

When the footsteps faded, Sang Luoluo quickly stepped back and hurried into the living room.

As soon as she entered, she ran into Tang Suqin, who was carrying a dish from the kitchen.

"Luoluo, perfect timing. Lunch is almost ready."

Tang Suqin smiled as she greeted her, but halfway through her sentence, she noticed Sang Luoluo’s cheeks were flushed. She couldn’t help but ask with concern, "What’s wrong? Why is your face so red? Did you get too much sun outside?"

"Mmm, a little," Sang Luoluo mumbled, her gaze evasive. She didn’t dare to look Tang Suqin in the eye and quickly made an excuse. "Aunt Tang, I need to wash my hands."

"Okay, let Xiao Ye take you to the bathroom."

Tang Suqin set down the dish and glanced at her son, who clearly seemed to be in a good mood. Then she looked back at Sang Luoluo.

This boy... he wouldn’t have been teasing the poor girl, would he?

He was usually so cold and indifferent to everyone. It wasn’t just about teasing girls—he even found it tedious to say a few extra words.

Regardless of the reason, it was good to see her son acting a little more human.

chapters.title: Sang Luoluo, You're So Lustful
chapters.content:
Sang Luoluo: "No need, Aunt Tang. I can go by myself."

"You know where it is?" Jingye's voice came from behind, unhurried.

Sang Luoluo paused mid-step. She really didn't know.

The first floor was spacious, but she wasn't familiar with the layout and couldn't spot the restroom door.

"If you don't know, come with me." Jingye had already passed her, heading toward the corridor.

Sang Luoluo pressed her lips together and silently followed.

In the restroom, after turning on the faucet for her, Jingye leaned lazily against the door frame, his elbow propped against the wall. His long, well-defined fingers hung at his side, the tips lightly tapping the door, producing a soft *tok tok* sound.

His gaze fell openly on her, like an invisible net, making her entire body uncomfortable.

Sang Luoluo put her hands under the water, even the motion of rubbing her palms together seemed clumsy.

To break the excessively quiet and subtle atmosphere, she forced herself to find a topic: "I thought you had a girlfriend."

Jingye raised an eyebrow, the arc of his brow sharp and handsome: "Why would you think that?"

"Everyone at school is saying you have a girlfriend." Sang Luoluo turned off the faucet, water droplets sliding down her slender fingers. "Don't you know?"

"I don't." Jingye took a clean towel from the nearby rack and handed it to her. "I just returned to the country not long ago. I don't have time to pay attention to such gossip. How is it being spread? Tell me."

"They say you went on exchange to be with your foreign girlfriend," Sang Luoluo said, stepping aside from the sink and taking the towel to dry her hands. "And that... she's a dancer."

A dancer?

Wasn't Aunt Tang a dancer who had danced for half her life?

So everyone had misunderstood.

Jingye genuinely didn't know the rumors had spread this far, and no one had ever mentioned it in front of him.

He washed his hands slowly, his long fingers rubbing gently under the water. The back of his hand, with its distinct knuckles, showed faint blue veins.

The water flowed through his fingers, splashing tiny droplets.

He lowered his eyes and smiled slightly: "A dancer? They sure know how to make things up. That's my mom. I don't have a girlfriend yet."

After turning off the faucet, he straightened up and looked at her. "Also, I went on exchange for myself, not for anyone else."

Sang Luoluo clutched the towel, her heart joyfully skipping a beat.

"Mhm, I know. I'll go out first."

Jingye took the towel and wiped his hands.

She had already walked toward the door. The moment she turned her back to him, the corners of her lips could no longer be restrained and curved into a bright, dazzling arc.

Like a sky that had been overcast for a long time, suddenly parting to reveal the sun, golden sunlight spilling everywhere.

During the meal, Tang Suqin and Jing Shouren sat on one side, while Sang Luoluo and Jingye sat across from them.

Throughout the meal, Tang Suqin barely ate, her serving chopsticks never stopping as she kept adding food to Sang Luoluo's bowl.

"Try this sweet and sour pork. I practiced making it several times, see if the taste is right."

"Have another bowl of soup. It's nourishing. You young people always stay up late..."

Before long, Sang Luoluo's bowl and plates were piled high.

Overwhelmed by the hospitality, she looked at the overflowing dishes in front of her, then at Jingye's clean and restrained plate beside her, feeling at a loss.

"Mom, if you keep adding, she might not dare to come back next time." Jingye intervened at the right moment.

Tang Suqin laughed: "Alright, alright, I won't add any more. Luoluo, you serve yourself. Eat whatever you like."

Sang Luoluo secretly let out a breath of relief. As she glanced sideways, she met Jingye's gaze.

He slightly raised his eyebrows, not speaking, but his eyes signaled her to "eat."

She lowered her head and took a small bite of the golden sweet and sour pork in her bowl.

It was tangy, sweet, crispy, and perfectly cooked.

There was also a large, irregularly shaped meatball in her bowl, clearly handmade by Aunt Tang.

She picked it up and put it in her mouth. At the edge of her vision, a hand suddenly reached over, seemingly to grab something in front of her.

She instinctively turned her head to look at him.

In that instant, she bit into the meatball.

With a soft *pop*, the scalding juice inside sprayed out unexpectedly, landing precisely on his T-shirt.

The dark oil stain quickly spread, extremely conspicuous.

Sang Luoluo froze, her chopsticks still suspended in mid-air, the meatball in her mouth, her cheeks flushed red.

She quickly put down her chopsticks and mumbled an apology through the meatball: "Sorry."

Her hand nervously reached for a tissue, and as soon as she pulled one out, she started wiping at the stain on his chest. Her fingertips, separated by the thin tissue, touched his warm chest. The heat made her fingers tremble, her movements becoming even more flustered as she rubbed haphazardly against his chest.

Each touch made Jingye's breath hitch for a moment, his Adam's apple rolling unconsciously.

If his parents weren't sitting across from them, Jingye wouldn't have minded letting her "wipe" a little longer.

He reached out and grabbed her slender wrist, taking the tissue from her hand.

"It's dirty, so it's dirty. I'll go change clothes later. Eat first."

After saying that, he casually tossed the oil-stained tissue into the trash bin at his feet.

Across the table, Tang Suqin and Jing Shouren silently exchanged a glance, their eyes both on their son.

They knew their son best.

He had a cleanliness obsession and a temper that was far from good.

If his clothes were messed up like this, in the past, he would have definitely darkened his face. Even if he didn't lose his temper on the spot, the atmosphere would have been tense for a long time.

But now, not only was he not angry, he even gently comforted the little girl. He had really grown up and become more gentle.

At this moment, Sang Luoluo wished she could bury her head in her bowl. She was so embarrassed.

---

After the meal, Jingye walked Sang Luoluo back to her room. "I'm going to take a shower and change clothes."

Sang Luoluo looked at the oil stain on his clothes, feeling guilty. She fiddled with the hem of her shirt: "How much was the shirt? I'll compensate you."

"Did you do it on purpose?" Jingye's tone was unreadable.

"Ah? No!" Sang Luoluo quickly shook her head. "I really didn't..."

"I still don't quite believe you." He leaned in slightly, his calm gaze locking onto her. "The old man just gave you a gift, and then you splashed me all over. Could it be that you're trying to find an excuse to return the card?"

"......"

She did want to return it.

But not in this way, and certainly not... to be misunderstood by him like this.

Jingye didn't give her a chance to speak and continued, "The old man values face a lot. If you return the gift he gave, he might sulk for days."

"I finally have such a cute dad. Do me a favor, don't torment him."

"Keep the card. Don't bring up returning it again."

With that, he left, giving her no chance to respond.

Sang Luoluo sat down on the sofa.

Forget it. Let her mother handle the card.

Her gaze, as if it had grown legs, drifted toward the wall connecting to the next room.

Certain scenes suddenly popped into her mind—

Water sliding over broad shoulders, a firm waistline, disappearing...

Sang Luoluo patted her heated cheeks.

"Sang Luoluo, you're so lustful."

She grabbed the nearby throw pillow and covered her face.

This dream had quite the aftereffect.

She took out her phone, plugged in her earphones, and randomly selected a playlist, forcing herself to listen to several songs before her mind finally calmed down.

She turned off the music, removed her earphones, and stood up, walking toward the floor-to-ceiling window. She slid open the glass door.

The balcony was spacious. The wind hit her face, carrying the damp scent of grass and soil from the courtyard, dispersing the inexplicable restlessness in her heart.

---

chapters.title: That Look, Three Parts Casual, Seven Parts Roguish
chapters.content:
She leaned on the railing and looked down. As her gaze shifted to the side, it suddenly stopped.

The neighboring balcony was connected to hers, separated only by a waist-high white dwarf wall.

At this moment, someone was leaning against the wall.

Jingye leaned against it with a relaxed and weary posture, his hair half-damp, exuding a lazy, at-home vibe.

He had changed into a high-quality white shirt, thin and slightly loose, the collar casually unbuttoned into a shallow V, extending down to just below his collarbone.

A silver cross necklace hung from his neck, resting against his chest.

One hand hung naturally at his side, while the other, with its bony and cold fingers, held a hint of crimson. Thin wisps of smoke curled and dispersed around his fingers.

That look was three parts casual, seven parts roguish.

He turned his head.

Their eyes met.

Sang Luoluo's heartbeat uncooperatively quickened, and she averted her gaze.

"Didn't take a nap?" he asked.

"No, I'm not sleepy." Sang Luoluo looked down at the courtyard below as she answered.

Jingye gave a slight nod, bringing the cigarette to his lips. He took a shallow drag, then exhaled the thin smoke with slightly narrowed eyes.

"Are you staying here tonight or going back to the dorm?"

"I want to go back to the dorm." Sang Luoluo answered quickly.

Staying here, she was afraid she might have another dream.

What if, in the dream, she called out his name again and he heard it?

It was strange. She had never dreamed of him before, but now that school had started, it was as if some floodgate had been opened.

"Mhm, juice or tea? I'll go get it."

"Juice, please."

"Alright, wait here." He responded and turned to go downstairs.

On either side of the waist-high white dwarf wall, comfortable wicker chairs were placed, each with a small round table beside them.

She didn't sit on the outer chair on her side but chose the inner one instead.

This way, separated by the dwarf wall, she was a little closer to his side.

After a while, steady footsteps approached.

Jingye came over with a glass of orange juice.

He handed the glass over the dwarf wall, and Sang Luoluo reached out to take it.

He didn't sit on the outer side either, choosing the inner wicker chair as well.

The two of them sat like this, each on their own balcony's inner side, gazing together at the greenery and sunlight filling the courtyard.

Time, at this moment, became slow and tranquil.

Sang Luoluo held her juice, suddenly understanding the most comforting form of companionship.

There was no need for the other person to do anything special, nor was there a need to rack one's brain for topics.

Just like this, quietly staying where they could see each other, sharing the same scenery, the same stretch of time.

Knowing he was nearby was enough.

She didn't notice that Jingye had been watching her the whole time.

---

Jingye walked Sang Luoluo to the dormitory building, watching her enter before turning to leave.

Sang Luoluo went to the window on the second floor and watched the departing figure.

Everything that had happened during this time felt like walking on cotton, with an unreal, unsteady sensation.

If it was a dream, she hoped this dream would last a little longer.

Inside the dorm, Sang Luoluo looked around but didn't see Menglin or Sunan.

"Where are Linlin and Sunan?" she asked.

Tan Shuyin, who was hugging a tablet and watching a drama, didn't even look up: "Sunan ran off somewhere to video call her boyfriend. As for Menglin, of course she went on a date. She's someone with a boyfriend now. She can't be like us, spending the weekend with the dorm leader like a mushroom."

Sang Luoluo: "......"

She put down her bag, changing her shoes as she casually asked, "Tan Jie, you're so outstanding. Why aren't you in a relationship either? I've never heard you mention anyone you like."

Tan Shuyin had a cool, clean-cut appearance, with shoulder-length short hair that was neat and tidy. She usually didn't talk much, always giving off a faint sense of detachment.

Tan Shuyin paused the video, put down the tablet, and stared straight at her: "Haven't you noticed? I like you!"

Sang Luoluo froze in the middle of changing her shoes, turning back in astonishment, her eyes wide.

Tan Shuyin immediately followed up: "Be honest, do you already have someone you like? Otherwise, why do you reject every confession so decisively, without a second of hesitation?"

The grand confession scene at the school gate had long since spread, and she had seen the video.

Sang Luoluo admitted: "Yes, I do have someone I like."

Tan Shuyin tilted her head: "If I were you, I'd say if you've liked someone for so long without results, you might as well let it go and have a fling with me that won't lead to marriage?"

"!!!"

Sang Luoluo felt a creeping chill down her back.

But at that moment, Tan Shuyin playfully winked, the corners of her mouth lifting slightly: "Scared you?"

"You're teasing me again." Sang Luoluo breathed a sigh of relief and laughed helplessly.

"Ah, you saw through me." Tan Shuyin raised her eyebrows. "But seriously, when it comes to love, it's better to have none than to settle. Until I meet someone who makes me think 'he's the one,' being single is fine."

Sang Luoluo nodded in agreement.

Tan Shuyin: "That confession video I watched. Isn't that guy's brain damaged? Publicly morally blackmailing someone and thinking he's romantic?"

Sang Luoluo: "I guess he won't dare to come find me again."

Tan Shuyin nodded: "This kind of thing really needs someone like Jingye to step in and shut it down. Luoluo, take my advice. In the future, you should really try to get on your brother's good side. With him as your gatekeeper, you can avoid at least half of these rotten peaches."

Sang Luoluo vaguely responded: "Mhm, I know."

Tan Shuyin frowned and muttered a few more curses at the boy's behavior before sitting back down to continue her drama.

Listening to her indignant grumbling, Sang Luoluo felt a warmth in her heart.

In the evening, when Menglin and Sunan returned and learned about the whole thing, they took turns criticizing the boy.

---

Weekend.

The dorm was quiet, with no alarm clocks blaring, no morning classes to rush to.

The curtains were drawn, the light dim and heavy.

Everyone slept until late, almost 11 a.m., before waking up one by one.

After lunch, Sang Luoluo stood by the window, watching the rain. She turned back and asked them: "Are you going to the internet cafe?"

Tan Shuyin hugged her pillow and rolled over. "No, it's raining outside. It's better to lie in the dorm. This weather calls for milk tea and movies."

"I'm not going either. Luoluo, are you going to the shop?" Sunan poked her head out from the bed.

"Yeah, I might as well go take a look since I'm free." Seeing that Menglin also shook her head, Sang Luoluo said, "Then I'll go."

"Luoluo, put on a jacket. It's gotten colder because of the rain." Menglin reminded her.

"Okay."

Sang Luoluo took a short, beige outer jacket and put it on, then took a transparent long-handled umbrella before leaving.

The rain wasn't heavy, just a light drizzle.

This summer had been strange. During the hottest two months, the weather had been so dry it could crack, yet not a single proper drop of rain had fallen.

But now that the weather had cooled down, this rain had leisurely arrived.

As the wind picked up, it carried a damp chill, seeping into her exposed skin with a cold, thread-like sensation.

She held her umbrella and walked slowly forward, carefully avoiding small puddles with her canvas shoes.

Droplets gathered along the umbrella's ribs, forming thin streams that continuously rolled off.

Through the hazy rain, she saw two familiar figures squeezed under a black umbrella.

It was Jingye and Chen...

chapters.title: Walking Side by Side in the Rain
chapters.content:
Jingye held an umbrella, his face displeased, as he pushed Chen Ge, who was trying to squeeze under it, back out.

The black umbrella tilted, and raindrops slid down his sharp jawline.

"If you don’t like holding an umbrella, just get wet. Don’t crowd me." His voice cut through the rain, colder than the downpour.

"Ah, I’m just being lazy."

Chen Ge grinned, letting himself be pushed out a little before trying to edge back in, indifferent to the cold rain.

"Sharing your umbrella saves me the trouble of holding one. It’s easier this way."

As he spoke, he turned his head and spotted Sang Luoluo not far behind, holding a clear umbrella.

"Hey! Little sister! What a coincidence!"

Jingye turned at the sound of his voice.

Through the curtain of rain, the girl stood quietly under her transparent umbrella, like a gardenia washed clean by the rain—delicate and soft.

She wore a short, off-white outer jacket over a light yellow short-sleeved top, revealing a slender, fair waist.

Her lower half was a pair of high-waisted, straight-leg light blue jeans, hugging her straight legs tightly. The cuffs were slightly rolled up, exposing her delicate ankles.

In the gloomy, rainy day, she stood out like a bright, vivid splash of color.

The kind that, with just one glance, could dispel the gloom.

Jingye left Chen Ge behind without a word and strode toward her.

"Hey, wait for me!"

Chen Ge covered his head with his hands and jogged after him, splashing up tiny droplets.

Jingye reached Sang Luoluo in a few steps, closing the distance between them.

Tall as he was, the black umbrella naturally tilted forward, sheltering both of them beneath it.

With his other hand, he took the clear umbrella from her without a word and handed it to Chen Ge, who had just caught up. "Use this."

Chen Ge instinctively took it, then looked up at the two of them standing side by side under the black umbrella. His expression blanked for a moment. "Huh? I have to hold it myself?"

Sang Luoluo tilted her head back. He was very tall, about 1.9 meters, so she always had to look up at him.

He was already standing beside her, close.

The umbrella clearly tilted toward her, completely shielding her from the swaying rain.

"Where are you going?" As he spoke, the minty scent on his breath brushed against the loose strands of hair on her forehead.

"To the internet café."

"Perfect, we’re going there too! Let’s go!"

Chen Ge, upon hearing this, quickly opened the clear umbrella and hurried ahead.

Jingye matched her pace as they walked forward.

Raindrops strung together on the umbrella’s ribs, leaving a shimmering trail behind them.

The two walked side by side in the rain.

His arm occasionally brushed against the sleeve of her jacket.

The fabric rustled softly with each touch, and every time, her arm tensed silently.

Before, she had secretly imagined countless times what it would feel like to walk slowly beside him.

Back then, she thought it must be the sweetest thing in the world—even the wind would taste sweet.

Now that the fantasy had become reality, happiness bubbled up from the depths of her heart like tiny bubbles, filling her entire chest.

Sweeter than all the sugar in the world combined.

The dark strands of his hair were slightly lifted by the wind, a few strands coiling around the arm holding the umbrella.

A faint tickle traveled up his spine.

A light, sweet peach fragrance wafted over, lingering at the tip of his nose.

It was the scent of her shampoo.

Jingye lowered his gaze, his eyes falling on her profile.

He caught the faint dimple that appeared as she smiled.

The small indentation held the dim light under the umbrella, sweet as honey brewed for an entire season.

"What are you smiling about?"

The dimple vanished instantly.

She looked up, meeting his deep, tranquil eyes.

Those eyes were wet, carrying a hint of flustered helplessness, like a young deer in the forest suddenly discovering a hunter.

"Nothing." She murmured softly.

As she averted her gaze, she noticed that his left shoulder, where the black T-shirt fabric had been soaked by the diagonally flying raindrops, was sticking to his skin, outlining the sharp line of his shoulder.

Sang Luoluo pushed the umbrella a little toward him.

As soon as she did, the umbrella returned to its original position, even tilting more toward her side.

"I’m a man."

Sang Luoluo didn’t insist further because they were almost there.

The group stepped into the shop and placed their folded umbrellas in the bucket by the door.

The internet café was bustling on the weekend.

Students filled the hall, the sound of keyboards clacking, game sound effects, and excited shouts blending into one.

The air was filled with the faint scent of smoke, instant noodles, and the heat from the computers.

He Fang was at the front desk, busy registering new customers, her head never lifting.

Sang Luoluo skillfully maneuvered behind the counter and said to the two of them, "Give me your IDs to register first."

Chen Ge was a little surprised. "Little sister, do you work here part-time?"

"No, this is my mom’s place. I just come by to play when I have nothing to do." Sang Luoluo explained.

"Oh, I see." Chen Ge nodded.

Jingye handed over his ID.

Sang Luoluo took it, and her fingertips accidentally brushed against his finger pads.

Cool and dry.

She quickly pulled her hand back and then reached for Chen Ge’s ID.

Chen Ge leaned against the counter with a grin, his elbow propped on the surface. "Little sister, get us a private room."

"Okay." Sang Luoluo agreed.

"Luoluo, on a rainy day like this, just stay in your dorm. Why did you come here?" He Fang finished her task and turned around, scolding while reaching for the IDs in Sang Luoluo’s hand.

Sang Luoluo dodged her hand. "Sister He, it’s fine. I’ll handle the registration. There are a few drink and snack orders waiting to be delivered. You go take care of those first."

He Fang nodded and turned to prepare the orders.

Sang Luoluo picked up Jingye’s ID.

In the photo, the boy wore a neat shirt, his hair shorter than now, his brows furrowed, and his gaze direct at the camera.

There was a sharp, unguarded brightness in his eyes—both roguish and wild.

Compared to now, he had softened those glaring edges.

She didn’t dare look for long and quickly registered them.

"Done. You’re in VIP Room 1, at the end of the hallway."

She returned their IDs, then took two ice-cold drinks from the fridge behind her. She also grabbed a pile of snacks from the counter and pushed them over.

Chen Ge raised his eyebrows. "Little sister, are you treating us?"

Sang Luoluo: "Mm. If you want anything else, I’ll get it for you."

"No need, little sister. This is enough." Chen Ge unceremoniously gathered the drinks and snacks in his arms.

---

After a while, He Fang took a sip from her cup and asked Sang Luoluo, who was organizing the shelves.

"Those two guys earlier—are they your friends? They don’t look like ordinary classmates. Especially the tall one. He’s got a special aura. Just standing there, he doesn’t quite fit in with the vibe of this place."

Sang Luoluo was pushing a bag of chips into a gap on the shelf. "Mm. If they come again, don’t charge them. Just put it on my tab."

"Got it." He Fang agreed, then couldn’t help but add with a smile, "I was just thinking earlier—maybe he’s your boyfriend. You two look pretty good together."

Sang Luoluo pressed her lips together. "No, don’t guess randomly."

"Alright, alright." He Fang glanced toward the VIP rooms, "But that boy is really something. You didn’t notice? Ever since they went in, a lot of girls in the hall have been looking that way. The bolder ones even deliberately take a detour past there."

Sang Luoluo had already seen it when she delivered an order earlier.

chapters.title: His Touch Awakens
chapters.content:
The door of the private room had a ten-centimeter transparent glass panel through which the people inside could be seen.

Jingye leaned back in the gaming chair, his long legs casually propped up, his slender fingers tapping on the keyboard. The glow of the screen illuminated his cold, pale profile.

Chen Ge was beside him, excitedly saying something with animated gestures, while Jingye only occasionally gave the faintest hint of a smile.

She had always known how dazzling he was.

He didn’t need to do anything. Just sitting there, he naturally became the focus.

A WeChat notification sounded, and she looked down at her phone.

Jingye: [We’re being watched. Do you have a poster? Lend it to me to block the view.]

She replied: [Wait a minute.]

She took an old poster from the cabinet and a roll of transparent tape, then headed toward the private room.

The decision to have glass panels on the private room doors was for safety reasons.

If a customer played for too long and felt unwell or had an accident, they could be seen from the outside and helped in time.

*Knock knock!*

"Come in."

Sang Luoluo pushed the door open. Jingye immediately took off his headphones, took the poster and tape from her, and swiftly taped the poster over the transparent glass panel on the door.

After finishing, he turned back. "You go out first."

Chen Ge, wearing headphones, hadn’t heard. He was completely absorbed in the game, muttering, "Charge! Get him!"

The next second, his screen suddenly went black.

"What the— who touched my—"

Chen Ge’s roar was cut off halfway when he saw Sang Luoluo standing at the door. His voice abruptly stopped, and his expression shifted from anger to confusion.

Jingye, unfazed, repeated to Chen Ge, "You go out first."

"Huh?" Chen Ge was confused, his face saying, "Are you kidding me?" "What’s going on that I need to leave?"

Sang Luoluo stood at the door, equally puzzled.

"Do I need to ask you to leave?" Jingye lifted his eyelids slightly. His tone was calm, but the underlying malice was unmistakable.

"I’m leaving! Right now!" Chen Ge jolted, wasted no time, took off his headphones, and quickly slipped out of the room, closing the door behind him.

The room fell silent, leaving just the two of them.

Jingye pointed to his seat and said, "Sit."

"Hm?" Sang Luoluo didn’t react immediately, blinking in confusion.

Jingye lifted his right hand, his index finger and thumb lightly pinching the bone of his left wrist. "My hand hurts. Sit down."

Sang Luoluo lowered her gaze to his hands.

His knuckles were long and well-proportioned, his nails neatly trimmed. Even the lines of his wrist bones exuded a cold, striking beauty.

This man was not only blessed with a good face but also impossibly beautiful hands.

When God created him, He must have been especially partial.

By the time she came back to her senses, her body had already obeyed before her mind could catch up, and she sat down in his seat.

Only after sitting did she belatedly blink, wondering what this had to do with his hand hurting.

"Help me play a couple of rounds." Jingye sat down in Chen Ge’s seat and nodded toward the brightly lit game screen.

Sang Luoluo looked at the complex interface filled with skill icons and honestly shook her head. "I don’t know how."

She had only played simple games like Snake, Match-Match, and QQ Racing. She had never played anything like this.

"I’ll teach you." He gave her no time to hesitate.

As he spoke, his gaming chair rolled softly on its casters, moving closer to her.

The distance between them suddenly shrank, and the crisp, cool scent from him silently enveloped her, so pleasant it made her a little dizzy.

The next second, his palm covered hers, completely enclosing her small hand as he guided it toward the mouse.

"Left hand here." Jingye took her left hand and placed it on the keyboard. His other hand held her right hand, controlling the mouse as it moved slowly. "The mouse controls the direction."

Sang Luoluo was so nervous that she barely dared to breathe.

Jingye slightly lowered his body, his gaze passing over her shoulder to the screen, his voice even closer. "Do you see the person in front? Yes, click on him."

His lowered voice brushed against her ear, sending a tingling warmth through her. Sang Luoluo uncomfortably tilted her head slightly.

With this movement, she belatedly realized she was enclosed in his arms, and her back could even feel the warmth and slight vibrations of his chest.

She stared at the dazzling skill effects exploding on the screen, her mind blank.

Her heart was beating wildly, like a rabbit frantically hopping, and she desperately tried to suppress it, afraid he would notice.

She followed his instructions in a daze, her entire being suspended in a foggy, weightless sensation. She didn’t even know where the mouse cursor was.

Jingye quickly let go of her hands and leaned back a bit, putting some distance between them.

The enveloping warmth and touch suddenly withdrew, and Sang Luoluo finally regained her breathing rhythm.

She forced herself to keep her eyes fixed on the screen, pretending to be completely focused.

The cursor hesitated in the center of the screen.

The screen was filled with character names and health bars. Which one was the one Jingye had told her to click?

She couldn’t remember at all. She didn’t dare to ask, afraid he would think she was too stupid.

Based on her vague memory, was it the one with the longest name?

Yes, it must be that one.

Its health bar was almost empty. It had to be the right one.

She moved the cursor over and clicked carefully.

The character fell to the ground, killed in one hit.

A small smile of accomplishment just began to form on Sang Luoluo’s lips.

Above the "defeated" character’s head, a resentful interaction bubble slowly floated up:

[Bro… we’re in the same guild… why are you killing me???]

"......"

Sang Luoluo instantly turned to stone, not daring to turn around to see Jingye’s expression.

"Wrong target." A short, low chuckle came from behind her.

"It’s the one next to it." His arm reached over her shoulder, his long index finger lightly tapping on another character on the screen. "Short name, full health bar. That’s the one you should kill."

"Oh… oh!"

Sang Luoluo nodded hastily, afraid of making another mistake.

This time, she focused intently, locking the cursor onto the target.

Then—click, click, click!

The enemy on the screen fell, dropping a pile of equipment.

This time, she had killed the right one.

She quickly picked up the equipment, then immediately let go of the mouse and stood up abruptly. "I’ll just—"

Before she could finish, her foot slipped, and she stumbled forward, tripping over herself.

She instinctively grabbed the armrest of Jingye’s gaming chair to steady herself, but the casters rolled back sharply with the force—

It was too fast. Jingye’s hand, which had been about to grab her, barely grazed her fingertips before missing.

As a result—

His touch awakened.

Burning hot, pressing against her forehead.

Sang Luoluo’s mind went blank for a moment, and she blinked.

Wait, was that... rising and falling powerfully?

Immediately after, her forehead was gently pushed away by a hand. Jingye glanced down casually. "Interested?"

"Huh?" She stared at him blankly.

"You were staring without blinking. So curious. I could, reluctantly, let you take a look." There was an indistinct hint in his tone.

Her soul snapped back into place. A scorching wave of embarrassment burned from her spine to her eartips. She jumped up. "I didn’t… I really didn’t mean that!"

"Mm," Jingye leaned back slowly in his chair, the corner of his lips hooking up slightly in a non-committal smile. "Then what did you mean?"

Sang Luoluo: "..."

She was stuck.

She couldn’t exactly say it was too... impressive, could she?

Jingye tilted his head seriously, as if considering. "Maybe you’re hungry?"

"!!!"

Sang Luoluo lifted her hand to pat her ear, muttering softly, "That’s strange. I didn’t hit it… why does it feel like I can’t hear clearly?"

As she spoke, she quickly turned around and fled out the door with awkward, hurried steps.

chapters.title: She Couldn’t Count How Many Times She’d Lost Face
chapters.content:
At the front desk, He Fang was checking accounts with her head down when she heard rapid footsteps. She looked up to see Sang Luoluo walking quickly toward her.

The girl’s cheeks were flushed crimson, and even the tips of her ears were tinged a deep pink, strikingly obvious under the lights.

He Fang instinctively glanced at the air conditioning display on the wall—26 degrees.

"Luoluo, are you very hot?" she couldn’t help but ask.

"Mm… a little." Sang Luoluo replied vaguely.

Though He Fang found it strange, she still took an iced drink from the fridge, twisted off the cap, and handed it to her. "Drink something cold to cool down."

"Thank you." Sang Luoluo took the water, lowered her eyes, and immediately tilted her head back to take several large gulps.

The icy liquid slid down her throat, slightly extinguishing the excessive heat on her face.

He Fang noticed Jing Ye approaching with his phone, so she raised her voice with a smile: "Hello, your friend insisted on paying, so you don’t need to pay again."

Sang Luoluo played dead, slowly lowering her head.

Jing Ye had already walked over. He raised his hand to loosely cover the phone’s microphone, gave He Fang a slight nod, then turned to the quail-like, shrinking Sang Luoluo and said, "I have something to do. I’ll leave first."

Sang Luoluo nodded, still not daring to look up. Her voice was as soft as a mosquito’s buzz: "Oh… okay, be careful on the road."

"Your leg alright?"

"It’s fine, not bruised."

Seeing this, Jing Ye turned and walked to the door. He saw his umbrella was still there; Chen Ge hadn’t used it.

Fine raindrops, carried by the wind, slanted down, drenching him in a cool dampness.

He opened the black umbrella and stepped into the fading rain, his silhouette quickly blurring in the mist.

Sang Luoluo lifted her head, watching through the glass door as the tall, straight back under the black umbrella grew farther and farther away.

She kind of wanted to die.

She couldn’t count how many times she’d lost face.

She stayed in the shop a little longer.

By evening, the rain had stopped.

The sky looked as if it had been carefully scrubbed, revealing a clear gray-blue. Behind the clouds in the west, a faint rainbow hung, its colors hazy and fleeting.

Sang Luoluo folded the transparent umbrella, shaking off the droplets.

She slipped it into the thin plastic bag that came with the umbrella, carefully rolled it up, and placed it in the side pocket of her canvas bag.

She had only taken a few steps out of the shop when her phone vibrated in her pocket.

"Hello, Linlin."

"Luoluo, the rain stopped. Eating barbecue in this weather is the best. My treat. Hurry back."

"I’m on my way back to school."

"Got it! Then wait for us at the school gate. We’ll be there soon!"

"Mm."

After hanging up, Sang Luoluo slowly made her way toward the school gate.

She hadn’t waited long at the spot when Meng Lin and Tan Shuyin came jogging from the direction of the dormitory area.

Sang Luoluo looked past them. "Is Su Nan not coming?"

Meng Lin shrugged, her tone a bit helpless. "She suddenly got her period right before leaving. Her lower back hurt so much she said she couldn’t come."

At the words "period," Sang Luoluo’s eyelashes trembled slightly. She couldn’t help but recall the embarrassing conversation from earlier.

"Should we pack some food for her to take back?"

"No need. I just ordered her some hot congee. She’ll eat and then go to sleep. Come on, just the three of us. Let’s eat our fill tonight!"

Meng Lin pulled Sang Luoluo and Tan Shuyin toward a nearby barbecue stall, its lively, smoky atmosphere unmistakably vibrant.

A few tables of students were already seated around, their laughter, clinking glasses, and cheerful chatter blending into the usual, lively noise of a campus evening.

The three found a spot near the edge and sat down. Meng Lin, familiar with the place, ordered a large spread from the owner—lamb skewers, chicken wings, leeks, enoki mushrooms… the list went on until the order sheet was full.

The charcoal crackled, and the skewers sizzled on the iron rack, their aroma mixed with cumin and chili powder wafting through the air, dispelling the slight chill left by the rain.

Tan Shuyin opened a bottle of beer and poured a glass for each of them. "Drink a little. You’ll sleep well."

Sang Luoluo clinked glasses with them.

With the cool beer and the steaming skewers, the three chatted casually, the atmosphere relaxed and pleasant.

When they had eaten most of it, the used bamboo skewers piled up in a small heap on the plate in front of them.

Meng Lin looked at the nearly empty plates and licked the chili powder from the corner of her mouth, still unsatisfied. "Want to eat anything else? I’ll go order more."

Before she could finish her sentence—

A loud male voice came from the neighboring table: "Yang Chao, nice! New girlfriend? She’s really pretty!"

Meng Lin’s smile froze on her face. She followed the voice and looked over.

Two tables away, her boyfriend of only a short while was now embracing a strange, meticulously made-up girl, sitting with a group of friends, laughing and chatting. The table was piled high with skewers and beer bottles.

He hadn’t even noticed this side. With his arm around the girl’s waist, amid the teasing, he raised his voice, introducing her with a boastful intimacy:

"Let me formally introduce her. This is my girlfriend, Fu Jing. She’s from the Music College, studying dance."

The girl nestled in his arms, smiling with bent eyes.

*Slap!*

Meng Lin slammed the chicken wing in her hand onto the table with a thud, brimming with rage as she charged toward that table.

Sang Luoluo and Tan Shuyin exchanged a glance, sensing trouble. They immediately stood up and rushed after her.

Meng Lin reached the table in a few strides. Without a word, she reached out and flipped the iron grill with all her might!

The grill, along with the sizzling skewers and vegetables, crashed to the ground with a clatter, scalding oil and food scraps splashing all over Yang Chao and his "new girlfriend."

"Ah—!"

The girl named Fu Jing shrieked and jumped back.

"Yang Chao, what the hell do you think you’re doing?" Meng Lin pointed at him, her chest heaving violently.

Yang Chao, scalded and in pain, his light-colored T-shirt stained with oil and food scraps, looked disheveled and embarrassed.

At first, he was stunned. When he realized it was Meng Lin, he felt humiliated in front of his friends and Fu Jing. His embarrassment turned to rage, and he pointed at Meng Lin, shouting, "Meng Lin! Are you crazy? What the hell are you doing here, causing a scene?!"

Meng Lin laughed in anger, pointing back at him. "I’m the crazy one?"

"You just confirmed our relationship, and now you’re here with someone else, telling everyone she’s your girlfriend? Then what am I? Huh?!"

Fu Jing’s expression changed. She frowned and asked, "Yang Chao, are you two-timing?"

"Baby, don’t listen to her nonsense!" Yang Chao quickly defended himself, reaching out to pull Fu Jing closer, but she dodged.

Humiliated, his expression turned contemptuous as he pointed at Meng Lin’s round, cute face and slightly plump figure.

"Fu Jing, just look at her. Anyone with eyes would know how to choose. Do you think I’d go for her? What a joke!"

Meng Lin had a cute, round face with a bit of baby fat, and though her figure was slightly plump, it was proportionate. To her roommates, she was like a sunflower.

His words were like a poisoned dagger, stabbing straight into Meng Lin’s heart in front of everyone.

Her face turned deathly pale, and even her lips trembled. The immense humiliation and heartbreak left her momentarily speechless.

Sang Luoluo shielded the trembling Meng Lin behind her, her voice sharp: "That face of yours—kicking others down to lift yourself up like a scumbag—is even more disgusting than a toad that’s been scalded, fished out, and left to rot. No responsibility, no manners. You’ve really disgraced all men."

"You—!"

Yang Chao’s face turned a pig-liver red from the public humiliation. Blind with rage, he raised his hand and shoved Sang Luoluo hard!

Caught off guard, Sang Luoluo staggered sideways. Fortunately, Tan Shuyin reacted quickly, grabbing her firmly from the side to keep her from falling.

"Are you even a man? You dare to hit a woman?!" Tan Shuyin shouted sternly, her gaze sharp.

---

chapters.title: Three Girls Fighting
chapters.content:
Meng Lin was already on the verge of exploding. Seeing Sang Luoluo get pushed for protecting her, she completely lost it.

In the dormitory, they all treated Sang Luoluo, the softest and most obedient among them, like a treasure, unwilling to let her suffer the slightest grievance.

And now this scumbag had actually pushed Sang Luoluo?

Her mind buzzed, all rationality gone. Like a thoroughly enraged little beast, she grabbed an empty beer bottle from a nearby table and charged forward, smashing it at Yang Chao without hesitation.

"Yang Chao, you bastard! I’ll fight you to the death!"

"Meng Lin!" Tan Shuyin tried to stop her, but it was too late.

Yang Chao hadn’t expected her to resort to violence so quickly. Caught off guard, the bottle struck his shoulder and arm with a solid *thud*, the pain making him yell. Instinctively, he pushed Meng Lin back hard.

Meng Lin nearly fell but was fueled by even greater rage. She charged again, reaching out to scratch Yang Chao’s face.

"Yang Chao, you son of a bitch! I won’t stop until I tear your face apart, or I’m not a Meng!"

The two immediately grappled, knocking over plastic tables and chairs around them. Plates and bottles crashed to the ground, and the surrounding diners exclaimed as they scrambled away.

Sang Luoluo and Tan Shuyin rushed forward.

Their goal was clear—not to break up the fight, but to help Meng Lin teach this scumbag a lesson.

Tan Shuyin seized the moment, grabbing Yang Chao’s hair from the side and yanking hard backward!

"Ah!" Yang Chao’s scalp tightened, forcing his head back.

"Who do you think you’re bullying?" Tan Shuyin showed no mercy, even delivering a hard punch to his back.

Sang Luoluo took advantage of this opening. As Yang Chao was pulled off balance, she lifted her foot, clad in a white canvas shoe, and with all her strength, kicked his unguarded shinbone!

*Thud.*

Yang Chao lost his balance and crashed to his knees on the ground.

Clutching his knee, the cold sweat poured down as he winced in pain, temporarily losing the ability to fight back.

Meng Lin was still not satisfied. She pushed her disheveled hair out of her face and charged again, kicking Yang Chao’s back and shoulders several times as he knelt on the ground. "Bastard! Scum! Trash!"

The entire process took no more than ten seconds.

Yang Chao’s friends at the table were stunned. None of them had ever seen three girls beating up a guy before. The novelty left them frozen in place.

By the time they reacted and thought to step in to help—

Sang Luoluo and Tan Shuyin had already quickly positioned themselves on either side of the breathless, still-cursing Meng Lin. They retreated a few steps, putting distance between them and Yang Chao’s group. The three stood side by side like porcupines with their quills raised.

"What, hitting a woman isn’t enough? You want to gang up on us?"

Tan Shuyin lifted her chin, her icy gaze sweeping over the several men who were itching to join in, showing no fear.

"Who hit a woman?"

A familiar male voice suddenly interjected, carrying a natural penetration that quieted the noisy scene slightly.

The barbecue stall owner, who had just been about to dial the police on his phone, also instinctively looked over at the sound.

Sang Luoluo followed the voice and saw Jing Ye striding in with his long legs, parting the crowd that had automatically made way for him.

His expression was cold, his gaze sweeping over the messy scene and the few girls.

His eyes settled on Sang Luoluo, who lowered her head, her gaze flitting away in panic.

Sang Luoluo furrowed her delicate brows, her heart pounding.

Had he seen her reckless, even somewhat ferocious fighting just now? What would he think of her?

Yang Chao’s friends, upon seeing Jing Ye, immediately deflated. Their earlier aggressive postures vanished, replaced by hesitation. They exchanged glances, none daring to step forward. Some even quietly retreated, their faces pale.

Who in Jing City didn’t know Jing Ye’s background?

In the circles of Jing City, no one dared to offend him lightly.

Offend him? Forget about staying in school—you wouldn’t have a good life in Jing City.

Yang Chao himself had sobered up considerably. The cold sweat on his back stuck to his shirt, the icy sensation against his skin sending a shiver down his spine.

He had met Meng Lin in a game. Later, when they revealed their real identities, his interest in her had faded.

He preferred girls who were slender yet curvaceous, not the cute, slightly plump type like Meng Lin.

After learning that Sang Luoluo had become Jing Ye’s sister, he had originally wanted to pursue her. But she was too hard to get, so he settled for Meng Lin instead.

He thought that through Meng Lin, he could get to know Sang Luoluo, and then maybe connect with Jing Ye, climbing up that high branch. Who in the school would dare to provoke him then?

He had only recently met Fu Jing, who happened to fit his tastes perfectly.

He wanted to sleep with her, so he figured he could keep both relationships going.

If Meng Lin found out, he could just apologize and break up with her. It wasn’t a big deal—he’d already gotten what he wanted from her.

He never expected that right after winning Fu Jing over, he’d get caught red-handed.

If Meng Lin hadn’t rushed over and flipped the table, if she had just given him a little face, he wouldn’t have said those harsh words.

He had been so angry just now that he even pushed Sang Luoluo.

Now, recalling it, Yang Chao regretted it so much his intestines turned green.

He gritted his teeth against the sharp pain in his leg, forcing himself to say something to ease the tension, even if it was begging for mercy.

With a pained smile that looked worse than crying, his lips trembling as he tried to explain: "Young Master Jing, it’s a misunderstanding, we were just joking around…"

Before he could finish his sentence—

A sudden, explosive pain in his abdomen hit him like a speeding truck, nearly blacking out his vision.

He hadn’t even seen Jing Ye move.

All he saw was a swift black shadow flashing before him, followed by a brutal, overpowering force slamming into the softest part of his abdomen.

His body flew backward through the air, crashing heavily onto the concrete several meters away with a *bang*, kicking up a small cloud of dust.

He curled up, clutching his stomach, gasping for air like a broken bellows, unable to move for a long time.

The surroundings fell into a deathly silence, broken only by the occasional crackle of the charcoal.

Jing Ye casually retracted his long leg.

The pale back of his hand flipped over, his thin skin at the base of his fingers brushing over the fabric as if removing nonexistent dust.

His expression was frosted over. He lazily lifted his eyelids, coldly eyeing the shrimp-like, sweat-drenched Yang Chao on the ground.

"I was just joking around with you too. Don’t take it personally."

Yang Chao’s body trembled violently, whether from pain or fear, it was unclear.

He clutched his abdomen tightly, his lips quivering as he looked at Jing Ye with terror in his eyes, unable to utter a single word.

Jing Ye reached into his pocket, pulling out a cigarette case.

The black matte case spun a small half-circle in his long fingers. He flicked open the lid with his thumb, leisurely tapping out a cigarette with his knuckle, then loosely placed it between his lips.

Chen Ge’s eyes lit up at the sight.

He took small, eager steps forward, pulling a lighter from his own pocket. *Click.* The flame flickered to life.

To an outsider, it might have looked like his sole purpose was to light cigarettes.

He hadn’t seen Jing Ye this genuinely angry in a long time.

The last time was because of Lu Zhi’an. He still remembered that scene vividly.

The swift, ruthless movements, the brutal force without mercy—every frame was steeped in a violent, humid beauty that sent chills down the spine, yet it also made the adrenaline surge uncontrollably.

Jing Ye looked so damn cool when he fought—with that absolute dominance and deadly elegance, mixed with a ferocity that was just too damn thrilling.

So, whenever Jing Ye was in a similar situation, showing signs of needing nicotine to suppress the restless, violent energy in his bones, Chen Ge would instinctively switch into this underling standby mode.

Of course, he would never dare say this out loud—he’d rather die than let those words leave his mouth.

chapters.title: Violent, Damp, and Aesthetic
chapters.content:
Jing Ye tilted his head slightly, his jaw to his neck drawing a smooth arc.

In the cluster of flames, he took a light breath.

The firelight flickered in his fathomless eyes for an instant before quickly fading.

White, ethereal smoke wafted over his cold and sharp face, blurring his current expression and seemingly softening the chilling, predatory aura in his peach blossom eyes.

Unfortunately, the slight comfort of nicotine was no match for the surging anger in his bones.

As the smoke dissipated, he kept one hand in his pocket while the other casually held a cigarette between his fingers, dangling by his side.

He looked down at the man with a disdainful gaze, as if examining a pile of revolting garbage.

"Dare to lay a hand on a woman. How do you want to die, you scum?"

Upon hearing this, Chen Ge immediately wrapped his arms around Jing Ye’s waist.

Not even the cigarette could suppress his rage—if he continued, Yang Chao would definitely be ruined today.

With so many classmates around and everything being recorded, it wouldn’t end well.

Jing Ye glanced at the man on the ground, his voice dripping with disgust: "Still not gone?"

Yang Chao and his companions, as if granted amnesty, were overwhelmed with fear that temporarily overshadowed their pain. They hastily helped each other up, stumbling and crawling away from the barbecue stall without daring to look back.

The noise subsided, leaving only the occasional crackle of the charcoal fire.

Chen Ge let go of him and patted his tense back. "Brother Ye, it’s not worth getting angry over this scum. Your sister didn’t suffer."

Jing Ye turned his tall figure around.

The dim yellow light from the streetlamp behind him spilled over, outlining his imposing silhouette and clearly illuminating Sang Luoluo, who stood a few steps away, looking somewhat at a loss.

The girl’s hair was slightly disheveled, her light blue pants splattered with dark oil stains, and the toe of her white sneaker smeared with a patch of dull dirt.

She looked a bit disheveled.

Finally, his gaze settled on her right hand, which had been hanging by her side, slightly curled.

On the fair, jade-like back of her hand were several red abrasions, and one edge was slightly broken, oozing a tiny bead of blood.

His voice was deeper and colder than before.

"Come here."

With that, he strode forward with his long legs.

Sang Luoluo pressed her cherry lips together, glanced at Tan Shuyin and Meng Lin beside her, and whispered, "Wait for me," before jogging after him.

The two walked in silence, one in front and the other behind.

Jing Ye stopped in front of a 24-hour chain pharmacy, extinguishing the half-finished cigarette between his fingers on a nearby trash can before pushing the door open and walking in.

Sang Luoluo hesitated at the entrance for a moment before deciding not to follow.

Through the glass door, the bright white light inside revealed his tall figure moving swiftly between the shelves. He grabbed a few items with purpose and headed straight to the checkout.

Only when he came out with a small white plastic bag did she silently follow.

They arrived at a relatively quiet flower bed nearby.

Jing Ye sat down on the stone edge, opened the plastic bag, and took out iodophor, cotton swabs, and a band-aid.

Without looking at her, he unscrewed the cap of the iodophor bottle.

"Hand."

Sang Luoluo looked down and only then noticed the red marks on the back of her hand, as well as the broken skin oozing a thin thread of blood.

She slowly extended her hand.

Jing Ye took her wrist.

It was slender to an extreme, the wristbone fragile like fine porcelain that could snap at the slightest pressure.

—*Such a thin wrist, yet she dared to rush forward and fight.*

Sang Luoluo felt the pressure around him drop even lower, and she didn’t dare to breathe freely.

The temperature of his palm was much warmer than her skin, and that warmth climbed up her wrist, scorching her to the point of wanting to pull back.

The moment her wrist twitched, it was firmly held in place by his unyielding grip.

"Don’t move."

He took a cotton swab dipped in iodophor and carefully applied it to the wound on the back of her hand.

The iodophor stung the broken skin, causing a slight pain.

Sang Luoluo’s gaze shifted from her restrained wrist, slowly moving upward, settling on his lowered face.

Fringe obscured his brows and eyes, perfectly concealing his usual wildness.

His nose was high, with a hint of Western sculpture-like prominence.

His lips were thin, with a distinct shape, currently slightly pursed, his expression focused and cold.

"You’ve got quite the nerve, even daring to fight."

"They were bullying Meng Lin." Sang Luoluo explained softly, her gaze drifting toward the pharmacy sign.

Jing Ye used the cotton swab to symbolically dab at the back of her other uninjured hand, confirming there were no other wounds before tossing the used swab into the nearby trash can.

The cool, overpowering restraint around her wrist disappeared, and an inexplicable emptiness surged in some corner of Sang Luoluo’s heart.

He lifted his pale eyelids from beneath his brow bone, his tone indifferent: "You don’t know how to use my name?"

Sang Luoluo was taken aback, not reacting immediately.

He was referring to just now... using his name to pressure Yang Chao?

"I... didn’t think it could be used like that." Her eyelashes trembled slightly.

"Next time you encounter something like this," Jing Ye pulled out a cigarette case from his pocket, "say my name first, then call me."

He paused, tapping his fingers lightly on the cigarette case: "You have my number, right?"

Sang Luoluo shook her head. "No."

Jing Ye recited a string of numbers, "1888XXXXXXX. Save it."

Sang Luoluo responded, pulling out her phone from her pocket and entering the numbers one by one.

Jing Ye knocked a cigarette out of the case, placed it between his lips, but didn’t light it.

"Mind if I have another cigarette?"

As he spoke, the cigarette between his lips swayed slightly with the movement of his mouth, exuding a casual, almost seductive allure.

"Not at all." Sang Luoluo shook her head.

She remembered seeing him once by chance in high school.

He leaned against the railing, his profile bathed in the dim light of the evening.

He lowered his head to light the cigarette, then tilted his chin upward, exhaling a straight line of smoke toward the gray-blue sky.

The smoke lingered and dispersed around his lips, his eyes half-lidded, his lashes casting faint shadows in the twilight. The lazy yet magnetic aura had captivated her, leaving her standing frozen in place, forgetting where she was headed.

At that time, Sang Luoluo had been stunned, completely mesmerized.

Jing Ye, having received her answer, tilted his neck slightly, his left palm forming a shield against the wind while his right hand struck the flint.

The night wind was strong, and the flame flickered several times before being blown out.

A faint crease briefly appeared between his brows, and then he turned his body slightly toward her, intending to use her figure to block the wind.

Just as he was about to try again, a slender hand entered the corner of his vision.

She used the hem of her off-white jacket to create a small windless space for him.

His movement paused, and he looked at her with half-lowered eyelids.

Sang Luoluo thought the wind was still strong and her shield wasn’t tight enough, so she leaned closer to him, intending to use her entire upper body to better protect the fragile flame.

The distance closed.

So close that Jing Ye’s gaze inevitably fell on the open neckline of her blouse, which had been exposed as she leaned forward.

The light-colored silk fabric was stretched taut by the full curve, forming a smooth tension that condensed into a voluptuous arc at the intersection of shadows.

His gaze darkened abruptly, his Adam’s apple rolled, and he quickly averted his eyes, speeding up his movements.

The crimson flame finally ignited, and the cigarette was lit.

Sang Luoluo stepped back to her original position, adjusting her jacket.

The smoke from his fingers had a unique scent—it wasn’t harsh or overpowering but carried a faint sweetness, like... honey.

She was a little surprised.

This scent seemed completely at odds with his sharp jawline and indifferent profile.

She had also seen him eating lollipops before—he seemed to like sweet things.

Jing Ye took a couple of drags, and the hostility between his brows dispersed significantly.

He stood up, forcefully extinguishing the cigarette, which was still more than half left, on top of the trash can.

"Let’s go."

Sang Luoluo nodded, her mind also on Meng Lin.

She picked up the unused medical bag and quickly followed, wondering if the other two had been harmed—

---

chapters.title: Night Smoke, Defending the Weak
chapters.content:
When they returned to the barbecue stall, the atmosphere had changed.

In front of Meng Lin, there were several empty beer bottles on the table. Her cheeks were flushed, and her eyes were slightly unfocused.

Chen Ge had already heard a rough account of what happened and was trying to comfort her in his usual joking manner.

"In my opinion, you really shouldn’t take what that scumbag said to heart. What’s all this about being fat or not? You’re fine the way you are—healthy, and you look... kind of cute."

Meng Lin, upon hearing this, stared straight at Chen Ge. "Do you really think I’m cute?"

Chen Ge nodded. "Yeah."

"Then be my boyfriend!" Meng Lin blurted out.

"Cough!"

Chen Ge had just taken a swig of beer, and it all came spouting out. He awkwardly grabbed a tissue to wipe his mouth, his face flushed red.

"Come on, sis, this is only the second time we’ve talked like this, right? You’re just so angry you’re not thinking straight, messing with me?"

"Don’t mention that scumbag!"

Meng Lin waved her hand in irritation, her body swaying as she steadied herself against the table. Her gaze locked onto Chen Ge’s face with unusual persistence.

"I’m just asking you—do you want to be my boyfriend?"

Sang Luoluo and Jing Ye approached just in time to hear this.

Tan Shuyin quickly stepped forward and covered Meng Lin’s mouth. "Meng Lin! You’re drunk, stop talking nonsense!"

"I’m not drunk!"

Meng Lin dodged, pointing directly at the bewildered Chen Ge, her logic surprisingly clear.

"Look at him—he’s rich, he’s a decent person, and he just called me cute. Isn’t he better than that bastard who only cares about other people’s figures?"

Chen Ge was amused by her straightforward and crude criteria for choosing a partner, but he also felt a bit at a loss. "So, what you value most is money?"

Meng Lin nodded vigorously, her eyes unusually bright under the influence of alcohol, and her words were shockingly blunt. "Otherwise, what? Love can disappear in an instant, but money won’t grow legs and run away. Money is way more reliable than men."

Chen Ge found this girl quite amusing and didn’t know how to respond.

Sang Luoluo’s heart ached, and she quickly walked over, wrapping her arm around Meng Lin’s shoulders and gently coaxing, "Linlin, stop talking. Let’s go back, okay?"

Tan Shuyin picked up her jacket and bag, and together with Sang Luoluo, they supported Meng Lin on either side.

Sang Luoluo turned to Jing Ye and Chen Ge. "We’ll take her back first."

"Do you need Chen Ge to carry her back?" Jing Ye asked.

"Yes!" Before anyone could react, Meng Lin had already raised her hand. "Chen Ge! Carry me!"

Sang Luoluo: "..."

"Alright, I’ll carry you."

Chen Ge was easygoing and walked up to Meng Lin. Before he could even crouch down properly, she had already thrown herself onto his back with both hands and feet.

He was caught off balance by her sudden leap and almost fell over with her. He quickly reached back to steady her.

"Hey, Auntie, at least give me a heads-up!" he said, half-laughing, half-complaining.

Meng Lin, draped over his broad back, rubbed her head against the back of his neck and mumbled something incoherently before her voice trailed off and she fell asleep.

"Let’s go."

Chen Ge resignedly adjusted his hold on her, shifting his position slightly before signaling to Sang Luoluo and the others.

Sang Luoluo and Tan Shuyin walked on either side, keeping an eye on her, while Jing Ye followed behind Sang Luoluo.

The night wind blew from the front, lifting Sang Luoluo’s long hair that had scattered over her shoulders.

A few strands of hair drifted in front of his eyes, and the air carried the peachy fragrance unique to her.

Sweet and clear, like a ripe summer fruit splitting open in the wind.

He reached out and gently gathered the cool strand of hair, winding it around his fingers.

Meng Lin suddenly shifted her body, and Sang Luoluo quickly reached out to steady her.

The strand of hair silently slipped from his fingers.

Jing Ye withdrew his hand, rubbing his fingertips together, his gaze still fixed on her back as she supported the other girl.

The road was quiet, with only the occasional soft breathing from Chen Ge as he adjusted his posture and Meng Lin’s muffled, incoherent sleep-talking.

They walked all the way to the girls’ dormitory building.

The dormitory auntie poked her head out of the window, saw that it was a girl being carried back with companions, and didn’t ask many questions. She only gave the tall and long-legged Jing Ye a couple of extra glances.

Sang Luoluo took the drowsy Meng Lin from Chen Ge’s back, and together with Tan Shuyin, they supported her on either side.

"Thanks." Tan Shuyin nodded at Chen Ge.

Chen Ge stretched his somewhat numb shoulders, waving his hand. "No need to thank me. Hurry up and go inside."

---

Sang Luoluo and Tan Shuyin helped the drunk Meng Lin into the dormitory. The two of them looked up at the upper bunk, exchanging helpless glances.

Sang Luoluo gently patted Meng Lin’s cheek. "Linlin, wake up. Can you climb up there yourself?"

"How did she end up like this?" Su Nan poked her head down from the upper bunk, lowering her voice to ask.

Tan Shuyin, while supporting Meng Lin’s sliding body, replied, "Don’t ask now. The question is how to get her up there—we can’t lift her."

Su Nan, seeing the situation, quickly climbed down from the bed to help.

The three girls surrounded the limp Meng Lin, at a loss for how to get her onto the high bunk.

"Or... maybe try tickling her?" Sang Luoluo suggested hesitantly. "Maybe it’ll wake her up a bit so she can move on her own."

"That makes sense." Tan Shuyin didn’t hesitate and immediately stretched out her free hand toward Meng Lin’s waist.

Meng Lin gave a start, mumbled an incoherent "mm," and twisted like an eel, sliding downward.

Sang Luoluo quickly propped her up again. "Let’s just push the chairs together and have her make do for the night."

Tan Shuyin sighed. "That’s the only option."

Su Nan quickly moved the chairs together.

With the combined effort of the three, they finally managed to half-drag, half-support Meng Lin onto the makeshift bed.

Sang Luoluo placed a pillow under her head, and Tan Shuyin draped a thin blanket over her.

The person on the chairs was already hugging the blanket, emitting steady snores, completely unaware of her surroundings.

"Something’s off with you two—what happened outside?" Su Nan asked.

"Don’t ask." Tan Shuyin lowered her voice and briefly recounted the events at the barbecue stall.

Su Nan listened, frowning. "Good for you for hitting him! If I’d known, I would’ve gone too and kicked that scumbag a few more times."

They all sighed, saying no more.

Sang Luoluo took Meng Lin’s hand to examine it, finding several prominent red marks on the back.

She opened the iodophor bottle, dipped a cotton swab, and gently applied it to the wounds.

"Tang Jie, did you get hurt?"

"I’m fine. Help her first. I’m sticky all over—I’m going to take a shower." Tan Shuyin finished speaking, took her change of clothes, and went into the bathroom.

"Okay." Sang Luoluo responded, her movements becoming even gentler.

By the time the dormitory returned to silence, everyone had already settled into their own beds.

In the darkness, only Meng Lin occasionally shifted or muttered in her sleep.

---

"Hey, Jing Ye, where are you going?" Chen Ge saw him walking away while on the phone and followed a few steps.

After hearing his brief words, Chen Ge’s heart skipped a beat.

*Damn, he’s still angry.*

Why did he have to provoke *this* guy?

"You go back first." Jing Ye hung up the phone.

Chen Ge, grinning, leaned in. "If there’s a show, I gotta watch. I’ll go with you and help keep lookout."

The two arrived at a dark, narrow alley behind the school.

The alley was so narrow that only two people could walk side by side. The walls on both sides were mottled and peeling, piled with discarded cardboard boxes. The damp, musty air mixed with the sour stench of garbage hit them in the face.

Inside, it was pitch black, except for a few dim yellow streaks of light from the streetlamp at the end, seeping through the cracks.

Sure enough, someone was lying at the far end, their head covered with a black cloth, pinned to the ground.

"Don’t draw blood—just teach him a lesson." Chen Ge didn’t go in, lighting a cigarette outside instead.

Before long, muffled thuds and suppressed grunts echoed from the alley.

Jing Ye thought of her disheveled appearance earlier, and his strikes grew heavier.

When he came back out, he had a cigarette between his fingers, walking slowly from the alley entrance.

The night wind carried the smoke past his jaw, and he raised his hand to his lips for a light drag. The flame illuminated half of his cold, pale face. The cigarette ash fell in fine fragments, and his tall, noble posture showed no trace of the earlier beating.

chapters.title: Taking a Break to Stay at His Place
chapters.content:
As soon as Chen Ge returned to the dorm, he shut the door and asked, "Hey, what do you think it feels like to like someone?"

Jing Ye hesitated for a moment before sitting down nonchalantly.

Lu Zhi'an lifted his head from behind the computer, adjusting his glasses. "What, has your heart finally started beating?"

"Cut the crap," Chen Ge laughed. "If it didn't beat, wouldn't I have kicked the bucket already? I'm serious, it just feels... weird. I can't explain it."

Shen Juan draped a towel over his shoulder and leaned against the bathroom doorframe.

"When you like someone, you stop being yourself. Your emotions are controlled by them—when they smile, the world brightens for you; when they frown, you start wondering what went wrong. If you see them getting close to someone else, the discomfort can keep you up all night."

"The worst part is, from then on, no one looks like them, yet everyone does."

"When you start having these pathetic reactions, that's probably when you're in love."

After listening, Chen Ge looked like he had caught someone red-handed.

"You make it sound so vivid. As someone who grew up with you since we were in diapers, how come I never knew you'd been in love before? Come clean—did you secretly fall for someone?"

Shen Juan: "Stop guessing. Just because I haven't eaten pork doesn't mean I haven't seen a pig run."

"Really never?" Chen Ge looked skeptical, eyeing him up and down. "Bro, I promise I won't laugh at you."

Shen Juan gave him a sidelong glance, half-smiling, and countered, "Tell me first—who have you fallen for?"

Chen Ge choked, turning back to his desk and flipping through a book aimlessly. "No one. Just asking casually."

Earlier, at the barbecue stall, when Meng Lin, drunk and bleary-eyed, asked, "Do you want to be my boyfriend?" his heart had actually skipped a beat.

He had never been in love before, which was why he wanted to ask the people around him what it felt like.

Seeing his guilty look, Shen Juan didn’t press further. He’d find out eventually.

Jing Ye didn’t listen any longer. Grabbing his change of clothes, he turned and went into the bathroom.

As the hot water poured over him, he propped one hand against the cold tiles and pressed the other to his chest.

Loving someone was like being lightly held in their palm, rising and falling with their every frown and smile.

---

Sang Luoluo had just lain down when her phone buzzed on the pillow.

In the darkness, she fumbled for it, and the screen lit up.

Jing Ye: 【I’m going to the cafeteria for lunch tomorrow. After class, wait for me downstairs.】

Sang Luoluo read the message, confused: 【But aren’t you banned from the cafeteria?】

Ever since that notice specifically for him had been posted, order in the cafeteria had been completely restored. The crazy long lines at the food windows had disappeared.

Jing Ye: 【The notice was taken down.】

Sang Luoluo curved her lips into a smile and replied with a cute, obedient cat emoji: 【Okay~】

Jing Ye: 【For National Day, are you coming to my apartment or going back to the Jing family home?】

During the National Day holiday, Ye Rong’s wedding planning company would be swamped; Tan Shuyin and Su Nan were from out of town and would go home; Meng Lin was local, so she’d naturally return home too.

That left only Sang Luoluo in the dorm.

That morning, Ye Rong had even called specifically to urge her to just go back to the Jing family mansion with Jing Ye so she wouldn’t be alone.

Sang Luoluo replied: 【I’ll go to your place.】

She wanted to see what his place looked like, where he lived alone.

Jing Ye: 【Good. The night before the holiday starts, we’ll go back.】

Sang Luoluo sent an "okay" emoji.

Jing Ye: 【Go to sleep.】

Putting down her phone, Sang Luoluo rolled over, her gaze falling on the window, where the night sky was dotted with stars.

In her heart, she silently bid goodnight to the person who had just sent the message.

She closed her eyes, letting the faint moonlight from the window spill in and settle on her peaceful, sleeping face.

---

Monday.

There was an 8 AM class, and the 7 AM alarm went off on time.

Sang Luoluo rubbed her eyes and sat up from the bed, her hair a little messy from sleep. The first thing she did was look at Meng Lin.

Meng Lin was already awake, staring blankly at the ceiling, her face pale, her brows tightly furrowed—clearly enduring the dull ache of a hangover.

Hearing the movement, Meng Lin slowly turned her head, her voice hoarse. "Sisters, my head is about to explode. Did I do anything embarrassing last night?"

Sang Luoluo, Tan Shuyin, and Su Nan exchanged glances.
