"No," Sang Luoluo lied without changing her expression, getting up to pour her some warm water. "You just drank too much. You were really well-behaved—passed out right away. We carried you back."

"That’s good." Meng Lin sighed in relief, taking the cup and sipping slowly, her brows finally loosening a little.

After finishing the water, she belatedly realized she had curled up on a chair to sleep, with a thin blanket draped over her—no wonder her back ached.

They took turns washing up before heading downstairs to the cafeteria for breakfast.

Walking in the morning sunlight, Sang Luoluo glanced sideways at Meng Lin.

Her complexion was still not great, with faint dark circles under her eyes and her lips pressed tightly together.

Though she forced herself to keep going, she seemed drained of energy, her steps slower than usual.

The three of them tacitly avoided any topics that might upset her.

She had just gone through a breakup; the wound was still fresh. Any mention of it would only make her hurt more.

Sang Luoluo looped her arm through Meng Lin’s and said gently, "The cafeteria has red bean buns today. Want me to get you a couple?"

Meng Lin nodded, softly replying, "Okay."

All morning, because Meng Lin was in low spirits, the three of them were unusually quiet as well.

Meng Lin was usually the chattiest and brightest, always bringing liveliness wherever she went.

But from the start of the morning class, she had kept her head down, her pen scratching aimlessly on the paper without writing a single word.

Sang Luoluo occasionally turned to look at her, only to see her staring blankly at a page in the textbook, her eyes slightly red, then quickly blinking away the moisture. Sang Luoluo silently pushed a pack of tissues toward Meng Lin.

Su Nan, meanwhile, slid her notes toward Meng Lin. "This page is important. I’ve highlighted the key points for you."

After class, Meng Lin forced a smile. "You guys go eat. I’m not hungry. My head still hurts a little. I want to go back and lie down."

"You have to eat," Sang Luoluo grabbed her backpack strap. "What do you want? I’ll bring it back for you."

"Really, no need," Meng Lin gently pulled away, her smile faltering. "I really can’t eat. You guys go ahead. Don’t worry about me."

With that, she turned and walked toward the dormitory building, her figure appearing especially thin in the crowd.

Sang Luoluo was about to follow, but Tan Shuyin grabbed her wrist.

"This is her first love, and it ended quickly with cheating. At times like this, having someone around might make her feel worse. Let her process it alone for a while."

Sang Luoluo nodded, her heart aching.

The teaching building of the neighboring Finance College had just let out, and the crowd was bustling.

The unobstructed afternoon sun spilled down, so bright that Jing Ye squinted.

Chen Ge, Lu Zhi'an, and Shen Juan walked beside him, still debating whether to have stir-fry or pasta for lunch.

Amid everyone’s noise, Jing Ye only had eyes for her.

Sang Luoluo was standing under a tree with her roommates, seemingly talking about something.

"...so it’s still pasta—"

Chen Ge was halfway through his sentence when he realized the person beside him was gone.

He turned his head and saw Sang Luoluo in the distance, along with Tan Shuyin and Su Nan. Only Meng Lin was missing.

Sang Luoluo seemed to sense something and turned around, spotting Jing Ye and the others approaching.

The fight last night had overshadowed the internet café incident considerably.

Now, seeing him, though her heart still fluttered a little, she could at least meet his gaze naturally.

---

chapters.title: Is My Wife Also Your Wife?
chapters.content:
"Hey, where’s Meng Lin? Why is it just the three of you?" Chen Ge asked, scanning the group.

"She’s not feeling well. She went back to the dorm to rest," Sang Luoluo explained.

The usual playful smirk on Chen Ge’s face faded. "Oh," he said softly.

"Let’s go." Jing Ye’s voice fell as he already started walking toward the cafeteria.

Sang Luoluo followed behind. Tan Shuyin nudged her and whispered, "What’s going on? Are we eating together?"

Sang Luoluo then remembered she hadn’t told them. "I forgot to mention—I’m having lunch with them in the cafeteria."

Tan Shuyin and Su Nan nodded.

Shen Juan glanced at the suddenly "wilted" "mushroom" beside him.

So, this Chen Ge kid had fallen for Meng Lin.

That girl, with her bright, curved eyes when she smiled, could stir up even more trouble than Chen Ge.

---

Jing Ye led the way into the cafeteria, once again drawing a flurry of attention.

While waiting in line, Jing Ye tilted his head toward Sang Luoluo. "Come here. Stand in front of me."

Sang Luoluo obeyed, moving to stand in front of him.

Not long after she settled into place, the person in front of her suddenly stepped back. She instinctively stepped back as well, her back pressing firmly against his chest.

Through the thin fabric, his body heat instantly seeped through, scorching her entire body.

There was no room to move forward, so she was about to step aside when Jing Ye’s hand settled on her shoulder.

"Don’t move." His voice came from behind her head, low and exceptionally clear amidst the noisy background.

She froze completely.

Her back was still pressed against his chest, and she could clearly feel the slight rise and fall of his chest as he breathed. The vibrations traveled through the fabric, colliding with her heartbeat.

Belatedly, she realized her heel seemed to be stepping on something slightly hard. She looked down.

The toe of his shoe was firmly under her foot, a small, faint gray mark left on the light-colored surface.

As if burned, she immediately moved away, stepping to the side, and instinctively bent down to wipe away the faint mark.

But a long-fingered hand grabbed hers first, his fingers closing around hers as he pulled her back up.

"What are you wiping? Your hand is cleaner than my shoe."

As soon as he spoke, the line moved forward.

"Go on," he let go of her hand, naturally gesturing for her to move forward. "Your turn."

Sang Luoluo quickly turned back and followed the line forward.

The lingering warmth from his hand still burned on hers, overlapping chaotically with the rhythm of her heartbeat.

Behind her, Jing Ye tucked his hand back into his pocket.

His fingertips subtly rubbed against the fabric inside.

—So small and soft.

The others behind them had seen the scene but didn’t think much of it.

She had stepped on his foot—he couldn’t exactly let the girl crouch down to wipe it, right?

It was normal for Jing Ye to stop her.

Everyone carried their trays and found an empty table to sit at.

Jing Ye sat across from Sang Luoluo, his long legs crossed, his posture relaxed.

Sang Luoluo kept her head down, but her eyes were disobedient.

Again and again, they secretly flickered toward the hand across from her that held the chopsticks—even the slight arc of his fingers as he picked up food was so good-looking.

That was the hand that had just pulled her up.

Not just his hand.

Every detail about him, from the slightly lowered lashes to the Adam’s apple that subtly moved as he ate, poked at her heart, making her unable to look away.

She sighed softly in her mind.

—How could she like him so much? Even the way he ate looked unbearably handsome.

Lost in thought, a pair of chopsticks reached over and placed a piece of cleanly deboned fish into her bowl.

She looked up in a daze, meeting his dark eyes.

Jing Ye had already withdrawn his hand, watching her with a half-smile. "If you want to eat it, just take it. No need to keep staring."

He probably thought she had been eyeing the food in his bowl.

"I, I wasn’t—"

Sang Luoluo wanted to explain, but the words died on her lips.

—She couldn’t exactly say, *I wasn’t eyeing your food; I was eyeing you.*

She silently lowered her gaze and obediently picked up the piece of fish.

Across from her, Jing Ye watched her slightly flushed face, the corners of his eyes curling with a hint of mischief, his gaze tinged with teasing.

"Hey, little sister, I’ve got sweet and sour pork ribs here, untouched. Take some if you want," Chen Ge enthusiastically pushed his tray toward Sang Luoluo.

Jing Ye raised his hand, using the other end of his chopsticks to gently nudge Chen Ge’s tray back. "She’s not your little sister. No need for you to offer."

Sang Luoluo quickly waved her hands. "No need, Senior. I have enough to eat."

This misunderstanding was huge—she wasn’t eyeing the food at all...

Chen Ge adjusted his tray and muttered under his breath, "If your little sister is my little sister, then—"

As soon as the words left his mouth, Jing Ye’s gaze swept over.

The corner of his mouth twitched almost imperceptibly, but there was no warmth in his eyes—instead, they were as cold as December frost.

"By that logic, my wife... is also your wife?"

The table fell silent instantly.

Everyone, including Sang Luoluo: "......"

Chen Ge was completely stunned, his eyes wide. "I was talking about little sisters! Why are you bringing wives into this?" His voice even cracked a little.

Jing Ye picked up his soup spoon and leisurely scooped up a spoonful of soup. "Same essence. They’re all mine."

This thief’s logic left Chen Ge speechless. After a long pause, he squeezed out, "Fine, fine! They’re all yours! Ancestor!"

Tan Shuyin stealthily leaned closer to Sang Luoluo and whispered, "Didn’t expect Jing Ye to be so possessive."

Sang Luoluo was surprised too and nodded in agreement.

The girl ate so obediently.

Her fair teeth carefully bit into the food, her soft pink lips puckering slightly as she held the food in her mouth, gently moving with each chew, like a dewy, plump, soft petal.

Jing Ye’s gaze darkened slightly.

He twisted open the mineral water beside him and drank it all in one go. The icy liquid slid down his throat but failed to suppress the slight restlessness rising within him.

---

The two groups parted ways at the fork between the boys’ and girls’ dormitories.

Before leaving the cafeteria, Sang Luoluo made a special trip to the window to take out a box of shrimp congee.

She carried the congee and pushed open the dormitory door. Meng Lin was lying on her side on the bed, her back to the door. She didn’t turn around even when she heard the noise.

"Linlin," Sang Luoluo placed the congee on her desk, "I brought you some congee. Sit up and have some. An empty stomach will make you feel worse."

The figure on the bed moved slightly. Meng Lin slowly rolled over, her eyes a little swollen, her voice muffled. "Thanks."

Sang Luoluo opened the congee box, and the fresh, fragrant steam rose into the air.

Meng Lin climbed off the bed, took the spoon, and sat at the desk.

She kept her head down, slowly sipping the congee, the steam swirling around her still slightly red and swollen lashes.

Sang Luoluo sat beside her without making a sound.

It was good that she was eating.

Emotions were like rain—only after it poured would the sky clear.

Crying wasn’t a bad thing. Holding it in was.

Tan Shuyin and Su Nan also sat quietly in their chairs, saying nothing.

The usually lively and energetic person now drooped like a plant without water. Everyone felt heavy-hearted.

chapters.title: The First Time She Saw That Side of Him
chapters.content:
A few days later.

The morning class was dull, with only the professor’s rhythmic voice echoing in the classroom.

Meng Lin’s mood continued to improve, the shadow over her brows mostly gone, and she had returned to her usual lively self.

She sat next to Sang Luoluo, and while the old professor at the podium turned to write on the blackboard, she lowered her voice to ask Tan Shuyin and Su Nan, "Hey, have you both bought your train tickets home?"

Su Nan: "I got mine ages ago. I booked them ten days in advance with lightning speed, terrified I wouldn’t get any."

Tan Shuyin sighed: "I managed to get one too, but it took days of trying—just a seat, no sleeper. I wanted to give up, but plane tickets are absurdly expensive."

Meng Lin nodded, then turned to Sang Luoluo: "Luoluo, your mom must be swamped during National Day, right? Why don’t you stay at my place? It’s no fun being alone."

Sang Luoluo curved her eyes into a smile and shook her head: "No need. I’m going to Jingye’s."

Tan Shuyin chimed in casually: "Isn’t he going abroad to be with his girlfriend?"

Sang Luoluo: "He doesn’t have a girlfriend. He’s single."

Meng Lin’s eyes widened: "What? He doesn’t have a girlfriend?!"

"Mm, no." Sang Luoluo repeated.

"But the forum posts were so detailed—they even mentioned his girlfriend studying dance!" Meng Lin still found it hard to believe.

Su Nan laughed from the side: "Isn’t it obvious? He must’ve made it up to ward off admirers. With so many people chasing him, wouldn’t anyone get annoyed? Just look at how Luoluo used to be hounded."

Sang Luoluo explained: "The person mentioned on the forum is his mom. She’s a famous dancer."

Meng Lin blinked, then realized: "Oh, that makes sense!"

The professor at the podium turned back, cleared his throat, and continued lecturing, his voice spreading evenly across the classroom.

Less than ten minutes later, the professor turned again, picking up the chalk to write on the blackboard.

Seizing the moment, Meng Lin stealthily pulled out her phone, lowered her head, and swiftly navigated to the campus forum with practiced ease.

After just a few swipes, she nudged Sang Luoluo, who was focused on taking notes, her voice excited: "Hey, Luoluo, look! That bastard Yang Chao dropped out!"

Sang Luoluo’s pen paused, a small ink blot spreading on the paper.

Meng Lin: "Do you think Jingye did this?"

"Maybe." Sang Luoluo said.

That night at the barbecue stall, the way he had kicked Yang Chao—decisive, ruthless, leaving no room for mercy.

That was the first time she had seen that side of him.

If someone asked her, *Are you afraid of him like that?*

She wasn’t.

Men should have spirit, protecting their own—there was nothing wrong with that.

She had once watched a video: a girl being harassed on the street, her boyfriend standing right beside her, just frozen, too scared to call the police or step in.

A man like that was worse than none at all.

Meng Lin seemed convinced: "It must be him! Who else has the power to make someone drop out just like that?"

"Jingye is really such a stand-up guy! He may seem cold and unapproachable, but when it counts, he’s there. So manly!"

The more she talked, the more excited she got. Then, half-joking, half-serious, she blurted: "I kinda want to pursue him. What do I do?"

Sang Luoluo: "..."

Tan Shuyin and Su Nan exchanged a look, both rolling their eyes at Meng Lin in unison, as if to say, *You’re beyond help.*

Tan Shuyin delivered the final blow without mercy: "Meng Lin, I suggest you get your brain checked."

Meng Lin refused to back down: "Why? I’m serious!"

"Serious about what?" Tan Shuyin tapped her notebook with her pen cap. "Jingye is on a whole other level. The kind of girls around him—what type *hasn’t* he seen? Do you really think he’d look your way?"

"He only stepped in that day because of Luoluo—he *had* to. If it were you, do you think he’d even acknowledge you? Snap out of it, don’t delude yourself over someone out of your league."

Meng Lin was left speechless, wilting over her desk, muttering softly: "I was just saying it randomly… Can’t I even *think* about it…?"

"You *can* think about it," Tan Shuyin shifted her tone, a sly glint flashing in her eyes, "but you’d be better off aiming for someone more realistic."

"Who?" Meng Lin asked weakly.

"Chen Ge."

At the name, Sang Luoluo and Su Nan exchanged a knowing smile, as if recalling something.

Meng Lin, confused, lifted her head: "What’s so funny? Why Chen Ge?"

This guy had been inexplicably messaging her a lot these past few days.

She hadn’t replied much, her mood being what it was, but he seemed oblivious, digging up all sorts of bizarre, hilarious videos and sending them her way in one go.

She had to admit, they *had* cheered her up a lot.

Tan Shuyin reminded her: "You got blackout drunk that night and demanded he be your boyfriend. Ring any bells? I think you should turn that drunken confession into reality. I support you going after him."

Meng Lin: "..."

"He didn’t call me crazy on the spot?"

"No, not only did he *not* call you crazy, he even kindly carried you all the way back to the dorm. Out of gratitude alone, you owe him a proper thank you."

Sang Luoluo added, a faint smile in her eyes.

Meng Lin replayed Chen Ge’s appearance in her mind.

Tall, a little goofy when he smiled, but with clean, honest eyes.

So… did he really take her drunken words seriously and start pursuing her?

*Uh…*

She rubbed her temples.

Her mood had just settled—why did she suddenly feel like she’d racked up some unexpected romantic debt?

"Though, to be fair," Su Nan chimed in with a laugh, "Meng Lin and Chen Ge *are* a good match in personality. Both are lively and unrestrained. If they got together, it’d be nonstop fun."

Tan Shuyin nodded in agreement: "One’s the instigator, the other’s the partner in crime. The mental image is already there."

Meng Lin’s cheeks warmed under their teasing. "We haven’t even started anything, and you’re talking like we’re already together."

At the podium, the professor finished writing on the board, turned around, and adjusted his glasses: "You students in the back, having such a lively discussion. Care to come up and share?"

All four of them fell silent instantly, lowering their heads in unison, pretending to take notes seriously.

---

That night, just past nine, Sang Luoluo finished the last character of her homework and set down her pen. Before she could react, Meng Lin swiftly snatched the notebook away.

Meng Lin flipped through it, muttering, "Let me see, for reference."

Su Nan immediately leaned in: "Yeah, yeah, let me check too."

Tan Shuyin, who had been halfway through her own work before going to shower, returned to see this and sighed: "You two copying Luoluo’s work *again*?"

"This isn’t copying," Meng Lin said self-righteously, "this is academic exchange."

Tan Shuyin had already sat down. "That’s a great excuse. Hurry up, let me *exchange* too."

Sang Luoluo looked at the three heads huddled together and laughed: "At least change a few words."

"Relax, relax," Meng Lin said, pen flying, "we know what we’re doing. The professor won’t notice a thing."

Sang Luoluo was the top student in the foreign language department, and the biggest advantage of sharing a dorm with her was this:

Homework came with a standard answer for reference—clear logic, all key points covered, and she never hoarded her knowledge.

It saved them so much time and effort that would’ve otherwise been spent scratching their heads over research.

chapters.title: Holding Her in the Rain
chapters.content:
Sang Luoluo climbed onto her bunk, cradling her phone, and tapped into his WeChat Moments.

To her surprise, there was a new post from two days ago.

No text, just a photo.

In the picture, a mulberry tree stood quietly in the twilight, its branches and leaves spread wide. The tree’s shadow stretched long under the setting sun, steeped in warm golden hues, exuding a serene, distant beauty.

*So beautiful,* she thought.

On impulse, her finger tapped the like button beneath the photo.

The red heart lit up—and then she froze. This was Jingye’s post.

Liking it was basically telling him, *I was secretly looking at your page.*

Panicked, she frantically tapped to unlike it.

*—I canceled it so fast, he couldn’t have noticed, right?*

But just then, the screen suddenly lit up. A new message notification popped up.

From Jingye: 【I’m pretty handsome.】

Sang Luoluo stared at the words, confused.

Why was he suddenly complimenting himself?

Did he want her to compliment him too?

Probably.

After a moment’s hesitation, she replied seriously: 【Yeah, you’re very handsome.】

Jingye: 【I’m not scary.】

Sang Luoluo hadn’t thought he was scary to begin with: 【You’re not scary.】

Jingye: 【I really am not scary.】

Sang Luoluo was thoroughly baffled. What was he trying to say?

She thought and rethought, deleting and rewriting, before finally settling on an emoji.

A white rabbit with long, drooping ears.

The rabbit blinked with innocent, wide eyes, its head topped with three obedient, confused words: 【I don’t get it.】

In the boys’ dorm, Chen Ge and the other two were wearing headphones, deeply engrossed in an intense gaming session.

Jingye wasn’t joining. He had one leg propped up, his ankle resting on the other knee, slouched bonelessly in his chair.

His eyelids were half-lowered as he stared at his phone screen.

The white rabbit stared blankly back at him, its long ears flopping, its expression dumb yet oddly endearing.

He stared at the emoji for two seconds, then the corner of his lips quirked up—so faint it was almost imperceptible.

【It was just a like. You think I’d track you down through the internet?】

Sang Luoluo: 【......】

One second later.

Sang Luoluo: 【I know.】

---

On the evening before National Day, the entire dormitory buzzed with the unique chaos of pre-holiday preparations.

The hallway was filled with students shouting farewells and reminders to one another. Suitcase wheels rattled urgently across the tiled floor, zippers opened and closed, doors slammed, laughter and goodbyes blending into a lively, noisy symphony.

Sang Luoluo packed a few changes of clothes and essentials into her small suitcase and zipped it shut.

"When are your trains?" she asked.

"I’m on the nine o’clock one, no rush. I’ll leave later." Su Nan was stuffing a power bank into her bag.

"Mine’s even later, around ten-thirty." Tan Shuyin crouched on the floor, counting the books she was taking home.

Sang Luoluo nodded, then turned to Meng Lin: "You? Are you leaving with me or waiting for your uncle to pick you up?"

"My dad’s still at work. I’ll wait for him to drive over." Meng Lin swung her legs from her chair, waving at her. "You go first. Don’t wait for me. Don’t keep Jingye waiting."

Sang Luoluo glanced at her silent phone.

He probably wasn’t back yet.

That morning, Jingye had specifically messaged her to say he had to take a professor to the airport in the afternoon but would hurry back to pick her up. He told her to wait for him at the school gate.

"Alright, I’ll head out first." Sang Luoluo pulled over her suitcase and waved at them. "Have a great holiday. Travel safe."

"You too! See you after the break!"

She dragged her small suitcase out of the dorm. The campus was filled with students rolling their luggage home.

Jingye had rushed back from the airport, his car barely squeezing into a parking spot at the school gate.

He quickly scanned the crowd coming and going but didn’t see the familiar figure. He pulled out his phone and called her.

"I’m back. Where are you? I’ll come get you."

On the other end, Sang Luoluo’s voice came through, accompanied by the faint sound of rolling suitcase wheels: "No need. I’m walking to the gate now. I’ll be there soon."

"Okay."

He put his phone away and noticed the brightly lit supermarket ahead, its glass doors glowing with warm yellow light, revealing shelves stocked with colorful goods.

She’d finished her lollipop, so he got out of the car to buy more.

As Sang Luoluo neared the school gate, the sky suddenly darkened. Heavy gray clouds pressed down ominously.

Almost simultaneously, large raindrops began to pelt down.

She hastily lifted her suitcase and quickened her pace toward the gate.

There were still many students like her without umbrellas, running through the rain while complaining:

"This damn weather! Perfect timing—right when we’re going home for the holiday!"

"My new shoes! I was gonna show them off at home, and now they’re ruined!"

"Don’t talk, just run!"

By the time she reached the awning at the gate, she heard a few girls whispering excitedly.

"Look over there! It’s Jingye! Oh my god…"

"Wet and tempting… that physique is insane. You can see every contour through his soaked white shirt. Who knew dodging the rain could come with such perks?"

Sang Luoluo subconsciously followed their heated gazes, looking past the white sheet of rain.

In the downpour, a tall, straight figure strode confidently through the rain.

His once-crisp white shirt was completely drenched, clinging to his skin, outlining every muscle of his abdomen with raw, primal allure—impossible to look away from.

He quickly reached his car, tossed the bag of colorful lollipops inside, then walked around to the trunk. He pulled out a long black umbrella.

The umbrella opened, creating a small dry space above him.

He turned and immediately spotted Sang Luoluo taking shelter at the edge. Holding the umbrella, he walked toward her.

Sang Luoluo’s eyes were fixed on him.

As he moved through the rain, closing the distance between them step by step, each one made her heart race.

Jingye stopped in front of her.

The black umbrella tilted forward, shielding her from head to toe.

Then, suddenly, he bent down. One hand still held the umbrella behind her shoulder, while the other slid under her knees. With a slight exertion, he lifted her horizontally off the wet ground.

Caught off guard, Sang Luoluo gasped, her hands instinctively gripping his broad, wet shoulders.

"There are a lot of puddles. Don’t want your shoes to get wet."

His thin lips were close to her ear, his breath cool and damp from the rain, brushing against her sensitive earlobe.

Sang Luoluo stiffened in his strong, powerful arms.

The warmth of his skin beneath the fabric, the hard contours of his chest muscles, and the aggressively masculine pheromones radiating from him invaded all her senses, making her cheeks burn. She didn’t dare look up at him.

"Wow—!!!"

"Is that how you treat your sister? Picking her up just so her shoes don’t get wet?"

"So Jingye has a gentle side too!"

"Holding the umbrella one-handed—so manly…"

Jingye placed her in the passenger seat, shut the door, then retrieved her suitcase and loaded it into the car before getting into the driver’s seat.

The engine started, the heater turned on, dispelling the chill of the rainy night.

chapters.title: Undressing to Tempt Her
chapters.content:
He drove the car away from the noisy school gate and merged into the slow-moving traffic caused by the heavy rain.

"There are clean shirts in the bag on the back seat. I'll find a secluded spot to park, and you can change into one to avoid catching a cold."

Sang Luoluo looked down at herself. Her light pink clothes were soaked in patches, but she didn’t look too disheveled.

"You should change instead. You're wetter than I am."

Jing Ye glanced at her, his eyes smiling, his tone slow and leisurely, but his tone was wicked: "If you're wet... I won’t be."

Sang Luoluo frowned, looking at him again.

He was clearly soaked from head to toe, but with that mischievous expression, his words...

Before she could figure it out, Jing Ye turned his gaze back to the road, his voice returning to normal: "There are two shirts in the bag. Enough for both of us."

As he spoke, he turned the car onto a relatively quiet side street and stopped at a corner.

Unbuckling his seatbelt, he leaned over to grab the paper bag from the back seat, took out a neatly folded white shirt, and handed it to her.

Pushing open the car door, he opened the black umbrella and got out.

He didn’t go far, just stood a few steps in front of the car, his back to the window, perfectly forming a barrier to block the view.

Inside the cramped car, only Sang Luoluo remained, holding the man’s shirt in her hands.

The windshield wipers swung back and forth, repeatedly sweeping away the raindrops on the windshield.

The tall and straight back facing her, standing still in the rain, came into focus and then blurred, over and over.

She quickly took off her own top and put on the oversized men’s shirt. The soft cotton fabric wrapped around her body, carrying an unfamiliar yet clean scent.

The sleeves were so long they covered her hands. She hastily rolled them up twice, revealing her slender wrists.

After changing, she knocked on the car window near the driver’s seat.

Jing Ye heard the sound, turned around with the umbrella, and opened the door to get back in.

Sang Luoluo handed him the other clean shirt. "You should change quickly. Give me the umbrella, and I’ll wait outside for you."

As she spoke, she reached for the umbrella he had set aside.

"Don’t move. Stay put."

Jing Ye didn’t take the shirt. Indifferently, he began unbuttoning his soaked shirt.

His fingers, with distinct knuckles, moved at a leisurely pace. The tip of his finger pinched the first button and flicked it open.

The button came undone, revealing a small patch of collarbone skin, made even paler by the rain.

The second button...

Droplets of water rolled down the clear lines of his collarbone, disappearing into the increasingly open neckline of his shirt, spreading a suggestive damp mark.

Sang Luoluo wanted to look away, but her eyes were disobedient, stubbornly fixed on the smooth muscle lines, unable to move.

He casually took off the soaked shirt, the weight of the water stains causing it to land on the back seat’s leather with a soft thud.

His bare upper body was exposed without any cover in the small car, far more shocking than the fleeting glimpse through the soaked fabric earlier or even in her dreams.

His seemingly slender frame was actually covered with a layer of symmetrical and firm muscles, exuding youthful strength everywhere.

Water stains followed the hollow of his collarbone, winding down his abs, and finally disappeared into the waistband of his still wet trousers, leaving behind a few tantalizing damp traces.

Sang Luoluo sluggishly closed her eyes, her long eyelashes trembling violently.

Jing Ye took a clean light gray towel from the car’s storage compartment. While casually wiping his still dripping black hair, he turned his head slightly, his gaze falling on her side profile, which was flushed red all the way to the roots of her ears.

He silently curled the corner of his mouth, the arc carrying a hint of indescribable roguishness.

Then, he handed her the towel he had used on his hair.

"Help me wipe the water droplets off my back. I can’t reach."

Sang Luoluo’s expression froze for a moment before she slowly opened her eyes.

Her gaze directly met that well-defined abdomen.

Before she could fully process the situation, his overwhelming body had already turned around, facing away from her toward the driver’s seat.

His hand pressed against the car window, leaving his entire broad back to her.

The muscles in his back tensed with the movement of his arms, and the groove of his spine deepened.

Sang Luoluo held the towel, her palms already sweating.

She bit her lower lip and pressed the soft towel against his skin.

Not daring to use force, she carefully followed the trail of water stains, gently wiping, her movements awkward and stiff.

Jing Ye maintained his position, leaning against the window, not moving at all.

Only when her fingertips occasionally brushed his skin did his back muscles tense slightly, and his Adam’s apple slide down in agitation.

"Okay... it’s done."

Sang Luoluo finally stopped, only to find her voice hoarse.

Jing Ye didn’t move. "It’s a bit itchy. Maybe the rainwater is uncomfortable. Use your hand to scratch it for me."

The skin on a man’s back was really fair.

Sang Luoluo thought inappropriately.

She had never seen a man with such fair skin—cool-toned, delicate, even fairer than all the women she had ever seen, like fine cold jade.

She hesitated before stretching out her hand, her fingertips lightly trailing down his spine.

"Not like that," he pressed the knuckles of the hand resting on the glass tighter, "...I can’t feel it. Use your nails."

Sang Luoluo paused.

She usually didn’t keep long nails, so she could only use the tiny, neatly trimmed edges to lightly scrape his skin.

A few faint red marks slowly appeared on the taut muscle texture.

Those marks... looked like the ambiguous traces left by a woman in the throes of passion.

"Is that enough?"

"Enough." Jing Ye turned back, pulling the clean shirt over himself.

Sang Luoluo turned her head, her gaze firmly locked on the water stains on the passenger side window, washed out by the rain.

Jing Ye buttoned the lower few buttons of his shirt, leaving the collar casually open, loosely forming a V-shape, exuding an air of careless sensuality.

His damp black hair was slightly messy, hanging over his forehead, obscuring part of his eyebrows and eyes, making the lingering sensuality from earlier even more striking.

The engine started with a low rumble, and the car slid into the rain.

A strand of loose hair fell by her ear. Sang Luoluo raised her hand to tuck it back, her fingertips accidentally brushing her earlobe—it was scorching hot.

She subtly moved the hair from her left side to cover her ear, trying to hide the suspicious flush, and quietly shifted her body a little closer to the car window.

On the window glass, her flushed profile and the figure of the man driving beside her were reflected.

He had one hand loosely resting on the steering wheel, the other on the gear shift.

His nose was straight, and the line from his jaw to his neck was taut.

The four corners of that cross pendant were sharply polished, glinting coldly in the dim light, looking a bit fierce.

Like him—superficially indifferent, but full of sharp edges deep down.

She said he wasn’t fierce, but that was because she liked him.

If she liked him, how could she possibly think he was fierce?

But others looked at him with obvious fear in their eyes.

"We’re here." Jing Ye’s voice pulled her back from her thoughts.

The car came to a stop. He leaned over to grab a bag from the back seat and placed it in her lap—it was a bag of colorful lollipops.

He pushed the door open and got out. His figure disappeared into the shadows of the garage.

Sang Luoluo held the bag of candy and followed him out. Jing Ye was already walking over with her suitcase in hand. "Let’s go."

The elevator ascended, the numbers quietly ticking upward.

When they exited the elevator at the top floor, he pressed his fingerprint to open the door. The light in the entrance hall automatically turned on.

---

chapters.title: Moving into His Home
chapters.content:
The apartment was very clean, with a simple modern style. The color scheme was mainly black, white, and gray, just like the impression he gave—calm and orderly.

Sang Luoluo’s gaze was unconsciously drawn to a spiral staircase inside.

Jing Ye followed her line of sight and explained, "It’s a duplex. The bedrooms are on the second floor, and there’s a small swimming pool on the third."

As he spoke, he took out a brand-new pair of pink slippers from the shoe cabinet and placed them at her feet.

"Change your shoes first."

Sang Luoluo changed into the slippers and followed him into the second-floor guest room.

The room was decorated in soft beige and light gray tones, with touches of lotus pink and misty blue.

The furnishings were simple, but every detail showed meticulous care, giving off a clean yet soft feminine vibe.

He stepped aside, gesturing for her to enter.

"The walk-in closet has clothes in different styles prepared in your size. The drawers below have underwear, all washed and ready to wear."

He paused, his dark peach blossom eyes falling on her somewhat stunned face, then added:

"So, no need to bring a bag."

"When you arrive, you can move in directly."

Even underwear was prepared?

Did he know her size?

Sang Luoluo’s gaze lingered on the walk-in closet for a moment before she ultimately didn’t ask.

She shifted her gaze and noticed something on the bed.

A plush rabbit wearing a pink vest was quietly leaning against the pillow, its ears softly drooping, looking obedient.

A subtle sting suddenly pierced her heart.

She walked over, picked up the rabbit, and hugged it to her chest, her fingers brushing against its soft fur. It felt nice.

Had another woman lived here before?

Did this overly cozy toy belong to her?

"Did another girl leave this rabbit behind?"

"The rabbit was bought by me. Everything in this room, from the bedsheets to the curtains, was prepared for you."

"This used to be a simple guest room. Chen Ge sometimes stayed here. I had it renovated recently. From now on, only you will stay here."

Jing Ye leaned against the doorframe as he explained.

After hearing this, the hint of jealousy that had just surfaced in Sang Luoluo’s heart instantly dissipated.

This rabbit was actually from the day she had sent him a rabbit emoji. Jing Ye had liked its cute appearance and had bought it.

His eyes lingered on her, unable to look away for a moment.

She was wearing his obviously oversized white men’s shirt. The sleeves were loosely rolled up several times, and the wide hem covered her mid-thighs, revealing only a small section of her jeans, also damp from the rain.

She didn’t look disheveled at all—instead, she had an unknowingly alluring charm.

Especially the way she wore his shirt... His gaze darkened.

Some clothes, once worn, truly made things difficult.

"You should take a hot shower first." He said hoarsely, then closed the door and left.

Sang Luoluo put down the rabbit, took out her pajamas from the suitcase, and went into the bathroom.

She took off his shirt and carefully hung it on a nearby hook.

Turning on the shower, the warm water cascaded down, washing over her skin.

She closed her eyes. In the steam, her mind uncontrollably replayed the scene from the car.

Abs, back muscles, waist muscles...

That waist—narrow and strong, so seductive...

Sang Luoluo’s face turned red. She shook her head hard, sending water droplets flying, trying to banish those images.

She quickly finished her shower and changed into her cotton loungewear.

Then she picked up his white shirt, which she had gotten wet, washed it carefully, wrung it out, and hung it in the bathroom’s ventilated area.

After finishing all this, she went to the second-floor hallway. His room door was closed, and she didn’t know if he had finished showering.

She went downstairs. The living room was empty, so she sat on the sofa and waited quietly.

Before long, footsteps came from the stairs.

He walked down, having changed into white cotton pants and a light blue T-shirt.

The extremely simple outfit, paired with his tall and straight frame, gave off a clean, youthful vibe.

His hair was half-dry, and the loose strands at his forehead hadn’t been combed back, softly draping over his brow.

He looked somewhat like a large, tamed animal, even his gaze carrying a tamed gentleness.

"I ordered food. It’ll be delivered soon." Jing Ye walked toward the open kitchen and pressed the water heating button.

"This is your home too. Do whatever you want. Don’t treat yourself like a guest."

Sang Luoluo obediently responded.

The water boiled quickly. He poured a glass of warm water and handed it to her.

The doorbell rang at that moment.

"The food is here." He said, turning to open the door.

Muffled voices came from the entrance as he spoke with someone, followed by the soft sound of the door closing.

He came back carrying several paper bags, the faint aroma of food spreading.

"Come eat."

He placed the bags on the dining table, unpacked them, revealing several light Cantonese dishes and two warm soups.

Sang Luoluo held her cup and sat across from him.

The two ate in silence, the only sound being the occasional clink of utensils.

"Where do you want to go tomorrow?" he asked.

Sang Luoluo took a small sip of soup and glanced out the window. "Who knows if it’ll rain tomorrow?"

"Then we’ll go indoors. Maybe watch a movie?"

"Okay."

---

In the living room, Jing Ye sat on the floor mat, one long leg stretched out casually, the other bent, his arm resting on his knee, and his back leaning against the edge of the sofa.

"The remote is on the coffee table." He pushed it toward her.

Sang Luoluo hesitated for a moment, then mimicked his posture, sitting next to him on the carpet, picking up the remote, and turning on the TV.

The light from the screen reflected on their faces as she flipped through the channels, settling on a lively variety show.

After watching for a while, her phone buzzed.

The screen lit up—her mother had transferred 50,000 yuan to her.

Soon after, a voice message arrived.

"Luoluo, your Aunt Tang said you’re staying at Xiao Ye’s place?"

Sang Luoluo instinctively glanced at the person beside her. He was looking down at his phone.

She typed a reply: [It’s more comfortable staying here.]

Another voice message from Ye Rong came, tinged with hesitant probing: "It might be comfortable, but you two are alone, and I..."

Before the voice message finished playing, Sang Luoluo quickly turned off the screen and secretly glanced at him.

He was still looking at his phone, showing no reaction.

She let out a sigh of relief and typed quickly: [Mom, don’t say things like that.]

Ye Rong: [Is he next to you?]

Sang Luoluo: [Yeah.]

Ye Rong: [Then okay, I won’t say more. Don’t just stay at home during National Day. Go out and have fun! I transferred you some pocket money. Spend it freely! The more you spend, the more motivated I am to earn money!]

Sang Luoluo’s lips curved into a smile. She pressed the voice message button and replied softly, "Got it, Mom. You take care of yourself too. Don’t work too hard."

Jing Ye turned his head, and the shallow dimples on her cheeks were dazzlingly sweet.

The girl was exceptionally beautiful.

Her skin was porcelain-white, almost translucent under the light. Her bone structure was delicate, as if painted stroke by stroke with a fine brush.

Her small face, especially her eyes, was incredibly clear—like almonds washed by rain, the black and white so distinct they seemed to hold light.

Her phone buzzed a few more times in succession.

Meng Lin: [Holy shit, Luoluo, Jing Ye is so damn handsome!!!]

Sang Luoluo: [???]

Su Nan: [The photo of him carrying you into the car is blowing up the school forum. It’s trending at the top with insane heat. Haven’t you seen it?]

Meng Lin: [That princess carry pose! That jawline arc! That wet body... no, that protective boyfriend energy is off the charts! I’m dead!]

Meng Lin immediately sent a screenshot.

Sang Luoluo opened the image.

The frame was frozen at the moment Jing Ye had lifted her up.

The rain curtain outside his black umbrella and the car body was blurred into a hazy background.

She was curled up in his arms, her face buried in his neck, only a small part of her side profile and wet long hair visible, making her appear particularly delicate.

chapters.title: A Man and a Woman Alone Together Should Burn with Passion
chapters.content:
And Jingye...

His arms were wrapped tightly around her, the taut lines of his muscles visible through the soaked shirt, pulling her firmly into his embrace.

The white shirt was drenched, clinging to his body, revealing his broad shoulders and narrow waist, every contour brimming with restrained strength.

An extreme cold detachment and an extreme protective dominance collided in the rain, creating a suffocating tension.

"Good shots."

A low, magnetic voice suddenly sounded near her ear, very close.

Sang Luoluo blinked, turning off the screen.

Jingye straightened up, his fingers sliding across his own phone, seemingly browsing something as well.

After a while, her phone vibrated again.

Another new screenshot from Meng Lin, followed by a string of exclamation marks.

Sang Luoluo opened it and zoomed in.

The image captured the latest comment under that trending post:

[999L] Digging deep for Jingye’s girlfriend! Whoever finds her gets a month of luxury cafeteria meals on me!

Right below it was a reply, the ID unmistakably the verified "Jingye": [I’m single.]

The reply timestamp showed it was posted just seconds ago.

Sang Luoluo said to Jingye, "I'm a bit tired. I'll go upstairs first."

Jingye nodded.

She turned and went upstairs, returning to her room and sitting at her desk. She reached into her bag and pulled out the envelope.

She had bought this the day she found out he was single.

She wanted to write a love letter, to finally confess the feelings she had hidden for so long.

These past few days, worried about Meng Lin, she hadn’t been able to focus on writing.

But the deeper reason was her hesitation.

Her current relationship with Jingye was so good it almost felt unreal—something she had never dared to hope for before.

She had seen and remembered every way he had taken care of her and accommodated her.

But the better it got, the more afraid she became.

Afraid that if she poked through that final layer, if she sent the letter and he rejected her...

This hard-won closeness would shatter like a soap bubble in the sunlight, vanishing without a trace, never to return.

After much deliberation, she still didn’t want to leave any regrets in this secret crush of hers.

Even if she was rejected, at least she had been brave, at least she had tried.

She opened her notebook and seriously wrote: Jingye, seeing this is like seeing me...

But after just this line, her pen stopped. It felt too stiff.

She gently tore the page out, crumpled it into a ball, and set it aside.

She flipped to a new page and wrote again: Jingye, maybe it’s presumptuous, but I still want to tell you...

She paused again, feeling it wasn’t quite right.

Frowning, she tore this page off too.

She repeated this several times, the crumpled balls of paper piling up beside the desk. Each one held an unfinished beginning and a heartfelt, yet clumsy, intention.

Late at night.

The entire apartment was shrouded in complete darkness.

Sang Luoluo stared at the pile of crumpled paper, her brows slightly furrowed.

None of the words she had written satisfied her.

This was the first time in her life she had taken the initiative to confess her feelings. Every word, every sentence, she wanted to be perfect.

Perhaps because they were only separated by a wall, her thoughts kept drifting uncontrollably to the room next door.

What was he doing right now?

Or had he already fallen asleep?

The chaotic thoughts made her restless, and the words she wrote seemed even more inadequate.

Forget it. She’d write it another day.

With a sigh, she stuffed all the crumpled paper into the deepest part of her bag, planning to find a corner to destroy them completely the next day.

She burrowed into her blankets, pulling them up to her nose, her eyes stubbornly fixed on the wall.

Next door.

Jingye sat on the rug at the foot of his bed, leaning back against the edge, also facing that wall in the darkness.

One on this side of the wall, one on the other.

A silent gaze between them.

*Click.*

The lighter cap snapped open, then shut.

A small spark flared to life in the darkness, then died as he released it.

Over and over, rhythmically, he repeated the motion, letting the flicker of light dance at his fingertips.

That fleeting flame, appearing and disappearing, was just like the thought repeatedly flashing in his mind: *A man and a woman alone together should burn with passion.*

Finally, he lit a cigarette, placed it between his lips, and discarded the lighter.

He glanced at his right hand—nice, suitable for doing something.

He leaned back, resting his head against the bed, and looked up at the pitch-black ceiling.

A wisp of smoke slowly rose, twisted, and dissipated in the air.

The red ember at his lips flickered, brightening and dimming.

In the moment it flared, it illuminated his clenched jaw, the taut line of his jaw, and his eyes—dark and bottomless with desire.

When the light faded, everything was swallowed by darkness again, leaving only his heavily suppressed, ragged breathing.

The lingering sensation of her fingernails scraping down his back was the only reality in the darkness.

He was thinking of her.

Thinking of her until even his fingertips burned.

...

-

Meng Lin was staying up late reading a novel when Chen Ge suddenly messaged her: [Want to go see a movie tomorrow?]

Did he really consider himself her boyfriend?!

She threw her phone aside, unable to understand—how could someone with his background end up stuck on her?

After rolling around on the bed a couple of times, she finally stopped, staring at the ceiling for a few seconds.

She reached out and pulled her phone back, tapping the screen a few times:

[Sure, I’ll pick the movie.]

On the other end, Chen Ge had only held onto a sliver of hope, fully prepared for a nine-out-of-ten chance of rejection.

Seeing the reply, he froze for a few seconds, almost unable to believe it.

[Great! You decide! I’ll pick you up tomorrow, send me your address.]

Meng Lin sent over her residential address.

Chen Ge immediately saved it, staring at the address like a fool, grinning.

Meanwhile, Meng Lin, after sending the address, placed her phone on her chest and stared at the ceiling, her heart filled with an inexplicable, subtle restlessness.

It... wasn’t so bad, was it?

...

The next day, the sky cleared, and the sun shone brightly.

The two of them still decided to go see a movie because Sang Luoluo wanted to watch one with him.

He had changed into a simple black shirt and pants.

Sang Luoluo wore a light-colored dress with a knitted cardigan over it, her long hair cascading softly over her shoulders.

At the cinema, Sang Luoluo looked at the huge screen displaying the schedule. "What genre do you want to watch?"

"Romance." Jingye answered decisively.

She turned to look at him in surprise.

"Who said men can’t watch romance movies?" He lowered his gaze to meet hers, calmly countering.

"No, of course they can." Sang Luoluo smiled slightly, turning back to seriously choose.

"What do you want to drink?" he asked.

"Coke."

"Popcorn?"

"Sure."

"Anything else?"

"Not really, just these."

"Look at them, as soon as they arrive, they ask what to eat and drink. I’ve been standing here for ages, and you haven’t asked me once." Behind them in line, a couple argued in hushed tones.

Sang Luoluo listened, turning to the man beside her.

He was lowering his gaze, ordering at the counter, his profile strikingly handsome.

After all this time with him, she had long since noticed how different he was from other men.

He didn’t talk much, but he always seemed to think of things before she did.

chapters.title: Does This... Count as an Indirect Kiss?
chapters.content:
The man noticed a few people around them had heard and felt embarrassed. He quickly tried to smooth things over: "Babe, what do you want to eat? I’ll go buy it right now."
The woman crossed her arms, her expression even colder. "Do you only do things after I say them? If I don’t say anything, would you just never think of it?"
The man was left speechless, and in the end, could only shoot Jingye a resentful glance. "Bro, you’re considerate, but don’t make me look bad in comparison!"
Jingye was in the middle of paying and lifted his gaze to glance at the man.
"If you’re someone’s boyfriend and don’t even have this much awareness, what’s the point of being in a relationship? A girlfriend is someone you cherish, not someone you win over and then forget about."
The man: "......"
The woman’s expression shifted, realizing Jingye made sense.
When he had been pursuing her, his messages were instant, he never missed a good morning or good night text, and on holidays, there were red envelopes and gifts—always generous, never stingy.
But after he got her, especially after they slept together...
His replies slowed, he asked her out less, and even forgot their anniversary.
Before, he would panic if she so much as furrowed her brow. Now, even if she cried, he just handed her a tissue and said, "Don’t make a fuss."
His passion hadn’t faded gradually—it was as if, once he had her, he couldn’t be bothered to keep up the act.
The more she thought about it, the angrier she got. She threw out, "We’re breaking up. You deal with it yourself." Then she turned and walked away.
The man stood there, watching his girlfriend’s resolute back, then glared at Jingye before hurriedly chasing after her. "Babe, wait for me... let me explain..."
Sang Luoluo clutched her popcorn bucket, feeling a little dazed.
They had just come to watch a movie, and Jingye’s single sentence had broken up a couple?
Wasn’t that a bit too powerful?
"Let’s go." Jingye led her toward the theater.
Sang Luoluo followed him through the dimly lit corridor into the flickering projection room, finding their seats.
Soon, the movie began, and the opening music played.
From the row in front, faint, familiar voices could be heard.
"Do you want anything to eat?" It was Meng Lin’s voice.
Chen Ge looked around. "Gum, maybe."
Sang Luoluo, by the light of the screen, indeed saw the two familiar backs in front of them.
What were these two doing here too?
Meng Lin shook out a piece and, seeing he was holding something, directly brought it to Chen Ge’s lips. Her fingertips accidentally brushed his mouth.
Chen Ge froze for a moment, his ears quickly turning a thin layer of red in the dim light.
Meng Lin obviously noticed too and couldn’t help but laugh. "No way, Chen the young master, you’re this innocent? Just touching your lips makes your ears turn red?"
"I......" Chen Ge felt embarrassed and, stiff-necked, tried to save face. The words "I’m experienced" were already on the tip of his tongue.
"Don’t lie!" Meng Lin cut him off before he could speak.
Chen Ge decided to go all in. "So what if I’m innocent? That just proves I’m clean. What’s wrong with that?"
"Oh—" Meng Lin drew out the sound, looking at him with interest. "So, you’ve never been in a relationship before?"
Chen Ge stared at her. "Does this count as being in a relationship?"
Meng Lin: "!!!"He really did consider himself her boyfriend.
Chen Ge, seeing her expression, spoke dissatisfiedly: "You’re the one who chased me and told me to be your boyfriend."
Meng Lin: "For someone from a family like yours, isn’t marriage usually arranged? Don’t you have to consider social standing? Can you really do whatever you want?"
Chen Ge: "My family dotes on me. I’m their only child. If they don’t agree, I’ll jump off a building to show them."
Meng Lin: "..."
"I don’t care. I’m your boyfriend now."
Chen Ge really liked Meng Lin’s personality—straightforward, unpretentious, with a nice smile. She suited him well.
Meng Lin blinked.
A free boyfriend who was rich, good-looking, and innocent?
Fine, no reason to refuse.
She curved her eyes into a smile, stretched out her hand openly, palm up, toward him, and said lightly, "Alright, boyfriend. Let’s get reacquainted."
Chen Ge immediately reached out his right hand, grasping hers firmly before quickly letting go.
Sang Luoluo and Jingye watched the entire exchange.
She couldn’t help but laugh, leaning forward to call out to Meng Lin.
But suddenly, her wrist was pulled back into her seat by a strong force.
Then, a low voice whispered near her ear, his breath brushing against her sensitive earlobe:
"Shh."
"If you call out now, how can they continue?"
Sang Luoluo’s ears turned a light red, and even the roots of her ears felt a tingling sensation.
Jingye reached into his pocket, fumbled for a moment, and pulled out a lollipop, offering it to her.
She abandoned the idea of calling Meng Lin.
She carefully unwrapped the candy and, quite naturally, placed the orange-yellow lollipop into her own mouth.
Jingye watched the disappearing lollipop in her mouth, his eyebrow subtly lifting.
"That was mine."
Sang Luoluo, with the candy in her mouth, froze. "...?"
The candy bulged slightly in her cheek. She blinked, looking a bit foolish.
She hastily took the candy out of her mouth.
"Do you have another one? If not, I..."
Before she could finish her sentence.
Jingye suddenly leaned down and, using her hand, took the lollipop from her.
The movement was too fast; Sang Luoluo didn’t even see his expression clearly.
She only heard a soft *crack*—the sound of the candy being bitten between his teeth.
He straightened up, his face showing no particular expression, as if he had simply retrieved something that had always belonged to him.
Sang Luoluo remained frozen, her mind blank.
"This... I already ate from it..."
Jingye, with the candy in his mouth, used his tongue to push it to the side of his cheek.
His gaze moved slowly from her shocked, speechless face down to her slightly parted, pink lips, which still glistened with a trace of sugar.
"I like this flavor."
Sang Luoluo stared at the lollipop.
—Does this... count as an indirect kiss?
"Didn’t want to give you one in case you didn’t like lollipops."
Jingye took another lollipop from his pocket, skillfully unwrapped it, and held it directly to Sang Luoluo’s lips.
Sang Luoluo looked at the lollipop, her expression indescribable.
Just how many lollipops did he have in that pocket?
She reached out to take it, but Jingye avoided her hand, placing it at her lips again.
"Just take it."
They locked eyes for two seconds.
Her beautifully shaped lips parted slightly, revealing a hint of moist interior.
Jingye moved his wrist slightly, placing the candy into her mouth.
She closed her lips around the candy, her soft, pink tongue instinctively licking its surface.
The darkness in Jingye’s eyes deepened abruptly, and he bit down on the same spot in his own mouth.
Sang Luoluo, her face flushed, turned to watch the screen. The sweetness from the candy slowly spread through her mouth.
On the screen, the male and female leads were passionately entangled in the pouring rain, kissing as if they couldn’t bear to part. The sound of water and heavy breathing came through the speakers, amplified in the dim theater.
Sang Luoluo uncomfortably averted her gaze.
When she watched it alone, she hadn’t felt anything, but sitting here next to him, every intimate scene felt unbearably awkward.
Jingye glanced at the screen for a moment before his gaze returned to the woman beside him.
He saw her head turned to the side, revealing a slightly red ear and a neat nape.
He silently curved the corner of his mouth, tossing the already finished lollipop stick into the trash. He picked up his Coke, bit the straw, and leisurely took a few sips.
Then, he lazily leaned toward her side.
Lowering his voice, he murmured against the background noise of the movie, like a lover’s whisper:
"Not interesting."

chapters.title: That Cup, I Drank From
chapters.content:
Sang Luoluo was startled by the sudden proximity and voice, turning her head abruptly.
Her lips barely grazed his jaw.
Her breath hitched, and all words stuck in her throat.
On the screen, the male and female leads were in the middle of a passionate kiss.
Below the screen, their breaths intertwined.
"S-Sorry, I didn't mean to."
Sang Luoluo panicked and leaned back, her lips still lingering with his tenderness. She unconsciously pressed them together.
Meng Lin, who was whispering to Chen Ge in the row ahead, heard the familiar voice behind her.
She turned her head in confusion, squinting toward the back row in the shifting light of the screen.
"Luoluo?" She widened her eyes in surprise. "What are you doing here?"
As soon as the words left her mouth, she saw Jing Ye beside Sang Luoluo.
Chen Ge also turned around, his face full of surprise. "Oh, you two are here too? What a coincidence."
"It is quite a coincidence." Jing Ye replied.
Chen Ge chuckled, running a hand through his hair. "You brought your sister to the movies, why didn't you tell me? It would have been more fun if we all came together."
Jing Ye: "If we all came together, you two probably wouldn't have been able to be alone today."
Chen Ge: "......"
"You two saw everything just now?"
If they were there, he and Meng Lin couldn’t have had their private conversation. They really couldn’t have been together.
"Your tuft of hair is as eye-catching as a traffic light," Jing Ye glanced at Chen Ge's striking flaxen hair tips, "We’re not blind, we saw it all clearly."
Chen Ge touched his "traffic light" tuft, awkwardly turning back. "Let’s watch the movie, let’s watch the movie. We’ll go eat together after it ends."
"Luoluo, I have a lot of snacks here, I’ll get you a few packs." Meng Lin enthusiastically turned around, holding several bags of chips and dried fruit in her arms.
Sang Luoluo had already finished her lollipop, and now she just felt thirsty.
"Linlin, it's okay, I just want to drink some cola to quench my thirst."
As soon as she finished speaking, a hand beside her handed over a cup of cola with a straw already inserted.
His entire palm was wrapped around the cup, leaving only space for the straw at the top.
If she wanted to take it, she would inevitably touch his hand.
Sang Luoluo hesitated, then reached out, her fingertips brushing the back of his hand that was holding the cup.
Then, the hand under her palm slowly pulled away, leaving the entire cup to her.
She took the cup, lowered her head, and began to sip through the straw.
Meng Lin took another look at the two of them.
She felt that the atmosphere between them was different from usual, and it was clearly not a good time to ask.
"Alright, just let me know if you want anything."
She turned back and casually pushed the popcorn bucket toward Chen Ge.
The two continued to eat and watch, occasionally whispering to each other. The atmosphere in the front row was relaxed and casual.
Sang Luoluo only noticed halfway through her drink.
To her left, the original cup of cola was still neatly placed in the cup holder of the armrest.
She released the straw, looked at the cup she was currently drinking from, then turned her head to her right—it was empty.
Her almond-shaped eyes secretly shifted toward Jing Ye beside her.
He also had nothing in his hands, just casually resting them on the armrest.
So... was this cup his?
She immediately handed the cup of cola on her left to him. "I haven't drunk from this one, you can have it."
"Mmm." Jing Ye took the cup but didn’t drink from it.
The corner of his eye twitched slightly, the mischief in his gaze shallow, hidden in the dim light. Sang Luoluo didn’t notice.
"You drank from my cup." After a slight pause, he asked, "Mind?"
"......"
Why did he have to say it out loud?
Wasn’t it better to just leave it unsaid?
A sudden heat rushed from her ears to her cheeks. "I don’t mind."
As soon as she spoke, the two of them tacitly turned their gaze back to the screen.
Because of this, she didn’t see the slight lift of the corner of Jing Ye’s lips beside her.
That smile was faint, yet scorching.
---
After the movie, the four of them stood at the entrance of the cinema.
"Where to eat next?" Chen Ge asked while looking around at the nearby signs.
Jing Ye turned his head to ask Sang Luoluo, "What do you want to eat?"
Sang Luoluo looked across the street at a clean-looking beef lamian noodle shop.
She raised her hand and pointed, "How about... that place?"
"Mmm." Jing Ye agreed readily. "Let’s go."
Chen Ge immediately protested, "Hey, Ye, why don’t you ask me and Meng Lin what we want to eat?"
Jing Ye didn’t stop walking, just threw over his shoulder, "If you don’t want to eat, then split up."
"Fine, fine! Who said we don’t want to eat?" Meng Lin laughed, linking arms with Sang Luoluo and pulling her toward the crosswalk.
Seeing this, Chen Ge quickly followed, still muttering, "Alright, alright, you two decide."
The green light came on, and Jing Ye walked on Sang Luoluo’s left, the vehicles on the left slowly coming to a stop.
The girls ordered small portions, the boys ordered large.
Chen Ge’s phone beeped. After reading the message, he looked up at Jing Ye. "Shen Juan and the others asked if we want to go to Jiang City for a few days."
Meng Lin’s eyes lit up. "I heard the night view from the mountaintop there is famous, and the stars are especially bright?"
Chen Ge nodded. "Yeah, do you want to go?"
Meng Lin immediately asked Sang Luoluo, "Luoluo, let’s go together, I want to see it."
Sang Luoluo had always loved stargazing, so she nodded. "Okay, I want to see it too."
"Alright, I’ll tell them." Chen Ge lowered his head to reply.
Four bowls of lamian noodles were served one after another.
Jing Ye carefully scalded a pair of chopsticks before handing them to Sang Luoluo, then did the same for his own.
Meng Lin watched from the side, secretly admiring: This Jing Ye, the more she got to know him, the more she felt he was considerate and thorough to an unreasonable degree.
Jing Ye then picked up several slices of beef from his bowl and placed them into Sang Luoluo’s.
Sang Luoluo’s heart warmed, and she softly said, "I have enough here, you don’t need to give me yours."
"Eat more. You’re too thin. Don’t collapse at a critical moment."
Jing Ye’s words carried a deeper meaning, but unfortunately, Sang Luoluo was too innocent to catch it.
She looked down at herself—delicate frame, 1.7 meters tall, exactly 50 kilograms.
In his eyes, she was probably as flimsy as a sheet of paper.
She pressed her lips together, her voice softening. "I know."
Chen Ge finished replying and glanced at the two across from him.
Jing Ye was being unusually good to Sang Luoluo, wasn’t he?
This level of care was nothing like his usual demeanor with anyone else.
Chen Ge suppressed his thoughts and steered the conversation back. "They said they’re going in the afternoon, to set up the tents before dark."
Meng Lin was surprised. "We’re staying overnight on the mountain? Are there bathrooms and places to wash up? I’d hate to have to go to the woods to feed mosquitoes just to use the bathroom. I’m not going if that’s the case."
Chen Ge laughed. "There are. The mountaintop campsite is developed, with public restrooms and washing areas. It’s not some wilderness."
Meng Lin: "That’s good! Otherwise, I’d have to flee down the mountain in the middle of the night."
Chen Ge couldn’t help but ruffle her hair. "You’ve got quite the demands."
They had only just confirmed their relationship not long ago and hadn’t even officially held hands yet. This hair-ruffling gesture was already the most intimate physical contact they’d had so far.
Meng Lin smiled at him.
Chen Ge: "After we finish eating, I’ll take you back to pack, then we’ll go in my car."
"Okay! Hurry, hurry, we’re running out of time." Meng Lin lowered her head and sped up her eating.
The table was filled with the light sounds of slurping noodles.
